primary_reviews.rationale: A word-by-word comparison of 1:1 with 1:2 bears out the zero-overlap claim: וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב puts no root, no participant and no formula into the sickbed opening וַיִּפֹּ֨ל אֲחַזְיָ֜ה, so a verse-edge cut here rests on genuine tier-1 lexical disjunction. Two accuracy problems sit beside that sound core. The WLC apparatus places its division after 1:2, not after 1:1, so the single witness brackets vv.1-2 together in the very shape the rejected alternative proposes, and no mark is disclosed anywhere in the row. Separately, my own consonantal sweep for root p-sh-' across the whole book returns 1:1, 3:5, 3:7, 8:20 and 8:22 only, which means the Moab notice is resumed at 3:5 (וַיְהִ֖י כְּמ֣וֹת אַחְאָ֑ב וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) rather than dropped, and the 'not picked up again' wording holds only because part 01 stops at 2:25.

challenges.claim: The row names 'grouping vv.1-2 as a joint scene-setting preface' as its strongest rival and rejects it, but never discloses that pmarks_2Kgs.json records "2Kgs.1.2": "SAMEKH" — the single Masoretic witness closes its section after v.2 and divides before v.3 (וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּר֙), which is exactly the vv.1-2 grouping being rejected. No mark is cited at all here, while three other rows in this cluster cite the marks that favour them. The mark is weak-tier and per book_strategy_draft.md can never lift or drive a boundary, so it does not overturn the lexical disjunction; the defect is non-disclosure of the one external datum running against a decision already held at medium_low confidence.
challenges.suggested_action: Add 'oshb:2Kgs.1.2 (samekh, single-witness)' to the rejected-alternative discussion and state plainly that the weak-tier mark favours the rival grouping but is outweighed by the total lexical disjunction between 1:1 and 1:2.

challenges.claim: 'its Moab theme is not picked up again anywhere in this part' is true only under a part boundary fixed by a different decision. My own book-wide consonantal grep for root p-sh-' in 2Kgs yields exactly five verses — 1:1, 3:5, 3:7, 8:20, 8:22 — and 3:5 reads וַיְהִ֖י כְּמ֣וֹת אַחְאָ֑ב וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, a resumptive repetition of 1:1's וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב with the same verb, the same two nations and the same death-of-Ahab peg, standing only nine verses later in the adjacent part.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword to 'not resumed until 3:5, outside this part', and cite the 1:1 / 3:5 resumptive repetition as positive evidence that 1:1 is a detached annalistic notice awaiting later pickup; it strengthens the standalone reading rather than weakening it.

primary_reviews.rationale: The verse-1 annal notice וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב is confirmed wayyiqtol narration sharing no verb, subject, or theme word with v.2's וַיִּפֹּ֨ל אֲחַזְיָ֜ה, and Moab does not recur anywhere across 1:1-2:25 (the writer's own part), so the topic-break claim holds. The rejected 'joint scene-setting preface' alternative is fairly stated, and the row's own hedge that the cross-book link to Ahab's 1 Kings close is background, not in-part evidence, correctly keeps that continuity out of the boundary argument itself.

All three Hebrew strings sit exactly where the prose puts them - וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב at 1:1, verse-initial וַיִּפֹּ֨ל אֲחַזְיָ֜ה at 1:2, וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at 3:5 - and not one character was disturbed in the rewrite. Both original defects are cured: the samekh keyed to 1:2 is now disclosed as dividing before v.3 and as favouring the rejected vv.1-2 grouping, marked single-witness and explicitly denied driving force; and the Moab claim is dated rather than absolute. A fresh intersection of the word set of 1:1 with that of 1:2 returns nothing at all, so 'share no formula or wording at all' survives my own test. Where the repair falls one verse short is the date itself: Moab resurfaces already at 3:4's וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב, which is also where this cluster's own row 008 opens its unit.

challenges.claim: The repaired sentence dates the pickup one verse late: 'The Moab theme ... is not resumed until 3:5'. My own consonantal sweep for m-w-'-b across 2 Kings returns 1:1, then 3:4, then 3:5 - 3:4 already reads וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד, so the nation re-enters the book at 3:4. Only the rebellion notice itself waits for 3:5 (my sweep for the root p-sh-` returns exactly 1:1, 3:5, 3:7, 8:20, 8:22).
challenges.suggested_action: Scope the sentence to the rebellion notice - 'the rebellion notice is not resumed until 3:5' - or date the theme to 3:4, so this row does not sit against row 008's own opening at the Mesha tribute notice.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both OL-M8-2Kgs-001-1 (samekh at 1:2 undisclosed) and OL-M8-2Kgs-001-2 (the 'not resumed anywhere' overstatement) are cured: the revised text names the samekh in both the main rationale and the rejected-alternative sentence, labels it weak-tier corroboration only, and states plainly the Moab theme is 'not resumed until 3:5, outside this part' with the 1:1/3:5 resumptive-repetition argument the challenge requested. Byte-collation of all three Hebrew quotes (1:1's disjunction verse, 1:2's fall-notice fragment, and 3:5's resumptive verse) against 2Kgs_oshb.txt returned exact substring matches, and the samekh citation checks out against pmarks_2Kgs.json (2Kgs.1.2: SAMEKH); both edges of the span are still argued from lexical disjunction rather than from the mark.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Independent collation confirms LF's zero-overlap reading: 1:1's וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל shares no root, actor, or theme word with 1:2's sickbed opening, so the verse-edge cut is real. OL is right that pmarks_2Kgs.json keys a SAMEKH to 1:2 (dividing before v.3, i.e. grouping vv.1-2 together) and that this mark sits undisclosed in the row, favoring the rejected 'joint preface' reading; it is weak-tier only, so it cannot overturn the lexical case, but OL's count of 'three other rows' citing favorable marks is itself low -- all seven remaining rows in this cluster (002 through 008) disclose at least one mark, only 001 discloses none. A book-wide grep for the root פ-ש-ע turns up exactly five hits (1:1, 3:5, 3:7, 8:20, 8:22), so OL is also right that the Moab theme resumes at 3:5 rather than vanishing from the book, though 3:5 sits roughly 47 verses after 1:1 (18 verses close ch.1, 25 close ch.2, plus 3:1-3:4 precede it), not the nine OL states -- the resumptive repetition itself (same verb, same two nations, same death-of-Ahab peg) is genuine and, if anything, strengthens the case that 1:1 is a forward-pointing detached notice rather than an orphaned one. Neither correction touches the frozen boundary; both fix a number rather than the substance of OL's finding.

post_resolution_check.notes: Sliced 1:1 and 1:2 byte-for-byte from oshb and confirmed the 1:2 samekh resolves to SAMEKH, single-witness, per pmarks. The row's forward-looking quotation of 3:4 matches the witness once Unicode combining-mark order is normalized (NFC/NFD both align); the raw byte order differs slightly from the source, logged as an aggregate note rather than a defect since the content is identical.

primary_reviews.rationale: The syntactic label at v.3 holds up: וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּר֙ is waw plus subject plus piel qatal, a textbook disjunctive frame set against the surrounding wayyiqtol chain, and it does answer the royal initiative of v.2. Internal cohesion for 1:2-16 is in fact stronger than the row argues — the death sentence הַמִּטָּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר עָלִ֥יתָ שָּׁ֛ם לֹֽא תֵרֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה recurs at 1:4, 1:6 and 1:16 byte-identical to its last word, an unused threefold refrain tying the span's two ends together more tightly than the captain triad does. What fails is the rejected alternative's assertion that the three sendings share 'identical dispatch wording'; collated character by character they diverge at three points, and one of the three has no ascent whatever. The samekh cited at 1:14 is correctly typed and placed, though the span also crosses an undisclosed samekh at 1:2 (raised under decision 001).

challenges.claim: 'each order and ascent uses the identical dispatch wording' is falsified on every element. Dispatch: v.9 וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו opens with no return-verb, whereas v.11 וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַחֵ֖ר וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו opens וַיָּ֜שָׁב and v.13 וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּשְׁלַ֛ח שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שְׁלִשִׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו opens וַיָּ֗שָׁב; v.13 further drops the indirect object אֵלָ֛יו that vv.9 and 11 both carry, and substitutes שְׁלִשִׁ֖ים for v.11's אַחֵ֖ר. Ascent: a programmatic consonantal test for the wayyiqtol of '-l-h inside 1:9 / 1:11 / 1:13 returns true, false, true — v.9 has וַיַּ֣עַל אֵלָ֗יו and v.13 has וַיַּ֡עַל וַיָּבֹא֩, but v.11 has no verb of ascent at all, only וַיַּ֨עַן֙ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו. Order: v.9 is הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דִּבֶּ֖ר רֵֽדָה, v.11 is כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מְהֵרָ֥ה רֵֽדָה, and v.13 is not an order but a supplication, תִּֽיקַר נָ֣א נַפְשִׁ֗י. The main rationale's hedged 'almost verbatim' is defensible; the rejected alternative's 'identical' is not, and that is the sentence carrying the whole argument against a three-way split.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'identical dispatch wording' with the verified shared core (שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים … וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו plus the escalating ordinal) and list the three attested variations; then rest the single-row triad on that shared core together with the threefold verdict refrain at 1:4 / 1:6 / 1:16, which is the span's strongest untapped cohesion signal.

primary_reviews.rationale: The disjunctive וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּר֙ אֶל אֵלִיָּ֣ה at v.3 is genuinely waw-plus-subject against v.2's wayyiqtol chain, and the three dispatch quotations at vv.9, 11, and 13 are byte-exact and do escalate a single formula rather than open three independent scenes; the samekh after 1:14 is correctly disclosed as weak-only corroboration. But the strongest_rejected_alternative misdescribes the tempting split as motivated by 'three separate kings' orders,' when only one king, Ahaziah, issues all three dispatches in vv.9, 11, and 13 -- there is no second or third king anywhere in the chapter.

challenges.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative attributes the tempting three-way split to 'three separate kings' orders,' but 2Kgs 1 has only one king, Ahaziah -- 1:2's וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים and the unbroken 3ms subject continuing through 1:9, 1:11, and 1:13's dispatch clauses all belong to him; no second or third king appears in the chapter.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise the phrase to 'three separate royal dispatches' or 'three of the king's own orders' so the rejected alternative does not misstate the cast.

primary_reviews.rationale: The central cure holds: the three captions are now quoted apart and each lands on its own verse (שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו at 1:9, שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַחֵ֖ר וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו at 1:11, שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שְׁלִשִׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו at 1:13), 'identical' is gone, the cast is no longer three kings, and the new load-bearing refrain checks out - my book-wide search for לֹֽא תֵרֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה returns 1:4, 1:6 and 1:16 and nothing else, while the samekh keyed to 1:14 does divide before the angel's word at v.15. Two things the repair itself introduced fail collation. The new cohesion word 'escalating headcount' is false against the text, since the constant וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו stands in all three verses; and the two forms quoted in the new drift sentence are accent-stripped strings found nowhere in the verses cited for them - the verse said to drop the first of the two in fact carries that pronoun twice, at וַיִּתְחַנֵּ֤ן אֵלָיו֙ and וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו, the former in precisely the shape the row prints.

challenges.claim: The repair now rests the single-row triad partly on 'an escalating count' / 'the escalating headcount' / 'an escalating ordinal', but nothing numeric escalates. Each sending is one captain of fifty with his fifty - וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו is unchanged at 1:9, 1:11 and 1:13 - and the sequence markers are not an ordinal series either: 1:9 carries none, 1:11 has אַחֵ֖ר ('another'), only 1:13 has שְׁלִשִׁ֖ים.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'escalating headcount/count' with what the Hebrew shows - a constant company of fifty sent three times, sequenced by 'another' at 1:11 and 'third' at 1:13 - and let the shared caption plus the threefold refrain at 1:4, 1:6, 1:16 carry the cohesion.

challenges.claim: Both forms in the new drift sentence are quoted accent-stripped and neither matches the verse cited. vv.9 and 11 read the object as אֵלָ֛יו (וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים), and the bare string the row prints does occur - inside 1:13, at וַיִּתְחַנֵּ֤ן אֵלָיו֙ - so 'v.13 drops the ... object' is true of the dispatch clause only and false of the verse. Likewise the ascent verb is וַיַּ֣עַל אֵלָ֗יו at 1:9 and וַיַּ֡עַל וַיָּבֹא֩ at 1:13; the form printed for it matches only 15:14 and 16:9 in the whole book.
challenges.suggested_action: Requote both forms from the witness (אֵלָ֛יו; וַיַּ֣עַל at 1:9 and וַיַּ֡עַל at 1:13) and scope the first claim to the dispatch clause, e.g. 'the dispatch clause of v.13 drops the object vv.9 and 11 carry, though the verse uses the pronoun twice later'.

primary_reviews.rationale: LF-M8-2Kgs-002-1's 'three kings' misstatement is gone -- the rejected alternative now reads 'three separate royal dispatches.' OL-M8-2Kgs-002-1's 'identical dispatch wording' claim has been replaced with an accurate variation list (v.13 drops the indirect-object pronoun that vv.9 and 11 both carry after the dispatch verb, v.11 swaps the ascent verb for a bare verb of answering, v.13's content is a plea rather than a command), which I re-verified clause by clause by direct line lookup of 1:9, 1:11, and 1:13 in 2Kgs_oshb.txt and found accurate down to the missing indirect object. The threefold death-sentence refrain that now anchors the triad argument is present near-verbatim in the oshb lines for 1:4, 1:6, and 1:16; no new mislabeling or invented participant appears in the rewritten passage.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The disjunctive frame at 1:3 (waw plus subject plus qatal against the surrounding wayyiqtol run) checks out as a genuine syntactic pivot answering Ahaziah's dispatch in 1:2. LF correctly catches that the strongest_rejected_alternative's phrase 'three separate kings' orders' cannot be right, since Ahaziah alone issues every dispatch across vv.9, 11, and 13 -- no second king appears anywhere in the chapter. OL's separate catch on the same sentence goes further: collating the three dispatch clauses letter by letter shows v.13 drops the אֵלָיו that both v.9 and v.11 carry, the ascent verb עלה is present in v.9 and v.13 but replaced by a bare 'answered' verb in v.11, and the content shifts from royal command (vv.9, 11) to a captain's plea for his life (v.13) -- so 'identical dispatch wording' is demonstrably false, though the row's own hedge of 'almost verbatim' survives untouched. Both defects sit inside one sentence but are independent findings rather than a shared miss, and neither disturbs the triad-as-escalation reading, which the death-sentence refrain repeated near-verbatim at 1:4, 1:6, and 1:16 supports on its own separate footing.

challenges.claim: pmarks_2Kgs.json records "2Kgs.1.17": "PE" as well as "2Kgs.1.18": "PE". Inside a two-verse span the row cites the petuchah that closes its own row (after 1:18) while passing over the petuchah falling between its two verses (after 1:17) — and that omitted mark is precisely the single-witness corroboration for the rejected alternative, described in the row as ending the legend at v.17 and leaving v.18 alone as the regnal notice. Marks belong to the weak-corroboration tier and cannot by themselves split the row, so the boundary is not shown to be wrong; but citing the favourable mark while suppressing the adjacent unfavourable one is selective evidence, and the stated 'medium' confidence was set without weighing it.
challenges.suggested_action: Disclose 'oshb:2Kgs.1.17 (petuchah, single-witness)' in the rejected-alternative and then rebut it on tier-1 grounds — that v.18's וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י formula and v.17's succession clause form one closing convention — instead of leaving the contrary mark unmentioned.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quoted clauses match the witness exactly, and the whole-verse constraint is correctly used to keep the fulfillment notice and succession formula together in v.17 rather than splitting mid-verse; the petuchah cited at the close of 1:18 is real (single-witness). But pmarks_2Kgs.json also records a PE keyed to 2Kgs.1.17 -- a mark sitting exactly at the seam the strongest_rejected_alternative proposes (ending the legend at v.17, opening the regnal notice at v.18) -- and the row discloses only the mark supporting its own close while never mentioning the one sitting at the seam it argues against.

challenges.claim: pmarks_2Kgs.json records a PE keyed to 2Kgs.1.17 (petuchah following v.17, single-witness) in addition to the PE keyed to 2Kgs.1.18 that the row cites; the first mark sits precisely at the v.17-to-v.18 seam that the strongest_rejected_alternative considers and rejects, but the row's evidence_refs and prose disclose only the mark favoring its own close.
challenges.suggested_action: Add the petuchah at 1:17 to the rationale or evidence_refs and note that it is weak-only and does not override the grammatical binding of the succession clause to v.17, so the evidentiary picture is complete rather than one-sided.

primary_reviews.rationale: The one-sidedness is genuinely gone: the row now records petuchot after both v.17 and v.18, tags them single-witness, and hands the seam back to the grammar instead of to either mark. That disclosure matches the witness exactly (marks keyed to 2Kgs.1.17 and 2Kgs.1.18, each following its verse), and the syntactic claim it leans on is checkable inside one verse: 1:17 carries וַיָּ֜מָת כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֣ה and וַיִּמְלֹ֤ךְ יְהוֹרָם֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו together, parted only by אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ. The closing quotation הֲלֽוֹא הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים is byte-clean and, on my search, unique to 1:18 in the book; I could find no grammatical or citation damage introduced by the rewrite.

Both LF-M8-2Kgs-003-1 and OL-M8-2Kgs-003-1 flagged the same one-sided disclosure -- the row cited only the 1:18 petuchah while suppressing the 1:17 petuchah sitting at the very seam its own rejected alternative proposes. The revision now discloses both marks in the same sentence, labels them single-witness and incapable of driving a split alone, and repeats the disclosure inside the rejected-alternative paragraph itself, matching what both challenges asked for. pmarks_2Kgs.json confirms PE at both 2Kgs.1.17 and 2Kgs.1.18, and both quoted Hebrew clauses (the fulfillment/succession verse, the source-citation formula) collate byte-for-byte against oshb.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both quoted clauses of 1:17 match the witness, and the whole-verse constraint correctly keeps the fulfillment notice bound to the succession formula rather than splitting mid-verse. LF and OL independently surfaced the identical gap: pmarks_2Kgs.json keys a PE to 1:17 in addition to the PE keyed to 1:18 that the row cites, and the first mark sits exactly at the v.17/v.18 seam that the row's own rejected alternative names and rejects -- a genuine convergent finding, since two blind reviewers reached the same evidentiary hole from unrelated starting points. The mark is weak-tier corroboration only and cannot split a whole verse bound by a shared succession clause, so the boundary stands, but the one-sided citation pattern (favorable mark disclosed, unfavorable mark suppressed) is a real disclosure defect the author round should fix by naming both marks and then arguing past the second on tier-1 grounds.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every load-bearing claim survives collation. The incipit וַיְהִ֗י בְּהַעֲל֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ אֶת אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּֽסְעָרָ֖ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם stands clause-initial in 2:1 and is purely temporal, sharing nothing with the regnal boilerplate just closed. The paired exchange is a true refrain rather than a paraphrase: כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי and חַי יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ are each byte-identical at 2:2, 2:4 and 2:6, varying only in the destination that follows (עַד בֵּֽית אֵ֔ל / יְרִיח֔וֹ / הַיַּרְדֵּ֔נָה), which is what a four-station itinerary requires. The tail is bound in as well, though unremarked: 2:15's בְנֵֽי הַנְּבִיאִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר בִּֽירִיחוֹ֙ repeats 2:5's בְנֵֽי הַנְּבִיאִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר בִּֽירִיחוֹ֮ consonant for consonant (accents alone differ), so the Jericho prophets who watch the ascent are the group already met on the outward leg. The 1:18 petuchah is correctly typed and expressly disclaimed as not the basis of the break.

All three sent-me/will-not-leave-you refrain pairs at vv.2, 4, and 6 are byte-exact matches to the oshb, and both span edges are genuine tier-1 signals: the 2:1 incipit וַיְהִ֗י בְּהַעֲל֤וֹת breaks cleanly from 1:17-18's regnal close, and v.18's rebuke gives way to 2:19's new petitioner with no formula overlap. No internal petuchah or samekh falls inside vv.1-18 to complicate the single-arc reading, and the per-station-split alternative is fairly rejected on the refrain's identical wording across all three stops.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Neither primary raised a challenge here, and independent checking shows why: the 2:1 incipit and the sent-me/will-not-leave-you refrain at 2:2, 2:4, and 2:6 are byte-identical across all three repetitions, cleanly binding the four-station itinerary into one continuous arc. OL's unchallenged aside that 2:15's בְנֵֽי הַנְּבִיאִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר בִּֽירִיחוֹ֙ repeats 2:5's phrase consonant for consonant also checks out on inspection, reinforcing rather than complicating the single-arc reading. No corrections are warranted; the row and its evidence stand as written.

primary_reviews.rationale: Nothing in this row misreports the Hebrew. וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֔ע stands first in 2:19 with a fresh plural subject, so a genuinely new petitioning party opens the vignette instead of continuing the search-party dialogue of 2:18. The close is equally clean: 2:22's עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה is an etiological formula absent from the surrounding chapters, and the contrast drawn with 2:25 is real, since that verse ends on the bare וּמִשָּׁ֖ם שָׁ֥ב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן with no fulfilment tag. Cast and location stay fixed through the salt sign-act of 2:20-21, leaving no seam inside the span. The petuchah reported at 2:22 matches pmarks_2Kgs.json in both type and verse and is offered only as corroboration.

The new-petitioner opener וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֔ע and the closing etiological tag כִּדְבַ֥ר אֱלִישָׁ֖ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר both match the witness exactly, and the petuchah at 2:22 (single-witness) is correctly disclosed as corroboration only. The rejected merge with the bears episode is fairly distinguished: v.22 closes on a to-this-day fulfillment tag while v.25 closes on a bare travel notice, an accurate contrast between the two vignettes' closing devices.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This row drew no challenges from either side, and independent verification finds nothing left to add: 2:19's new-petitioner opener and 2:22's etiological close both match the witness exactly, and the salt sign-act in between keeps one cast and one location throughout with no seam to hang a split on. The contrast the row draws against 2:23-25 (a to-this-day fulfillment tag here against a bare travel notice there) holds up as a genuine distinguishing device rather than a rationalization invented after the fact. Both arrays are empty; this decision needs no author-round attention.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quoted notices check out and both marks agree with pmarks_2Kgs.json in type and verse: 2:23 begins וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל, a verse-initial wayyiqtol of motion carrying an entirely fresh cast (וּנְעָרִ֤ים קְטַנִּים֙ in the same verse), and 2:25 does end on וּמִשָּׁ֖ם שָׁ֥ב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן. One thing glossed over is that 2:25 holds two itinerary notices — וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל precedes the Samaria return — so 'a second travel notice' is doing double duty. challenges.claim: book_strategy_draft.md states that in the Former Prophets pe and samekh 'never drive or lift a boundary'. This boundary_rationale nevertheless opens by locating its own start with the mark — 'Elisha's route resumes right where the previous vignette's petuchah left off' — before naming any Hebrew signal. The tier-1 evidence is present and sufficient on its own (וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל, verse-initial wayyiqtol of motion, plus a wholly new cast in the same verse), so this is a framing slip and not a wrong boundary; but as written the mark functions as the locator of the seam, the one role the strategy forbids it.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast the opening so the travel notice and the change of cast carry the boundary, and demote the 2:22 petuchah to a trailing corroboration clause, matching the explicit 'consistent with though not the basis for this break' formulation already used in decision 004.

primary_reviews.rationale: The bare travel notices that open (וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל) and close (וּמִשָּׁ֖ם שָׁ֥ב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן) this vignette both match the witness verbatim, and the petuchah at 2:25 (single-witness) closing the chapter is accurately cited. The claim that the ascension arc's refrain never recurs here holds up -- no sent-me/will-not-leave-you pair appears anywhere in vv.23-25.

The forbidden move - letting the mark locate the seam - has been reversed, and the Hebrew now placed first survives inspection: 2:23 does begin with וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל, a verse-initial wayyiqtol of motion, with the new cast וּנְעָרִ֤ים קְטַנִּים֙ arriving in that same verse. The 2:22 petuchah is demoted to the wording the strategy permits ('consistent with though not the basis for this break'), and both marks are keyed as the single witness has them, 2:25 being in fact the final verse of the chapter. The 'two itinerary notices rather than one' claim is literally true of 2:25, which reads וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל and then וּמִשָּׁ֖ם שָׁ֥ב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן; no character was altered anywhere in the rewrite.

OL-M8-2Kgs-006-1's complaint was a framing slip, not a wrong boundary: the mark was doing the locating work the book strategy forbids it. The rewrite now opens on the travel notice and new cast (the Bethel-ascent clause and 'young boys') before ever mentioning the 2:22 petuchah, which now arrives only as 'consistent with though not the basis for this break' -- the exact hedge the challenge asked to be matched. Both boundary marks check out against pmarks_2Kgs.json (PE at 2:22 and PE at 2:25), and the closing sentence now correctly counts two itinerary clauses inside v.25 rather than treating it as one.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The travel notices opening and closing this vignette (2:23's וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל and 2:25's close) match the witness, and OL is right that the row's opening sentence names the 2:22 petuchah before naming any Hebrew signal at all -- a framing lapse against book_strategy_draft.md's own rule that pe and samekh 'never drive or lift a boundary' in the Former Prophets. The lapse is cosmetic rather than substantive: the verse-initial motion verb plus the fresh cast of young boys inside that same clause is sufficient tier-1 evidence standing alone, and this very cluster already models the correct move -- decision 004 uses the formula 'consistent with though not the basis for this break' for an analogous mark -- so the fix is simply to reorder this row's opening sentence to match that existing pattern. The 2:23 boundary itself is untouched by the correction.

primary_reviews.rationale: The accession claim is accurate as far as it goes: 3:1 does begin וִיהוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ in clause-initial position, its synchronism reads בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט as described, 3:3 closes on the Jeroboam evaluation, and 3:4 does open disjunctively with a new subject, so both edges rest on Hebrew signals. The samekh at 3:3 is typed correctly and expressly held to weak tier. My objection lands on the rejected alternative, which asserts a property of 'every other regnal opening in the book' from a two-verse sample with no sweep behind it; the grep I ran myself neither supports the universal nor shows the two cited verses to be formal counterparts of 3:1.

challenges.claim: 'every other regnal opening in the book (8:16, 13:1) stands as an independent unit regardless of the narrative that follows it' is a book-wide universal resting on two instances with no book-wide check. I ran one. A consonantal sweep of 2Kgs returns 16 accession verses opening with the date formula b-sh-n-t / w-b-sh-n-t (8:16, 8:25, 9:29, 12:2, 13:1, 13:10, 14:1, 14:23, 15:1, 15:8, 15:17, 15:23, 15:27, 15:32, 16:1, 17:1) plus a further 15 carrying the ben-N-shanah … b-m-l-k-w accession element (8:17, 8:26, 12:1, 14:2, 15:2, 15:33, 16:2, 18:2, 21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18), so the universal is drawn from roughly two of twenty-plus openings. The same sweep undercuts the parallel itself: a regex for a fronted subject of the shape waw+PN ben PN malak 'al matches 2Kgs.3.1 and nothing else in the book, whereas both cited comparanda are date-fronted (וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ … at 8:16, בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙ … at 13:1). The 3:1 boundary is unaffected, carried as it is by the accession formula and by 3:4's disjunctive frame, but the argument offered against folding 3:1-3 into the campaign is not evidenced as stated.
challenges.suggested_action: Either drop the 'every other regnal opening' universal and argue from 3:1's own formula, or run the book-wide grep and cite its result; and note that 3:1's subject-fronted shape is unique in 2 Kings rather than presenting 8:16 and 13:1 as formal twins.

primary_reviews.rationale: The accession formula וִיהוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן and the disjunctive וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד both match the witness exactly, and the samekh at 3:3 (single-witness) is properly treated as corroboration only, never a driver. The two comparison regnal openings named in the rejected alternative, 8:16 and 13:1, do check out in the oshb as genuine synchronism-plus-reign-verb accession formulas, so the analogy holds rather than being a straw man.

This row's cure is arithmetical, so I recounted rather than took it on trust. A verse-initial consonantal sweep for b-sh-n-t / w-b-sh-n-t returns seventeen verses, of which 17:6 (בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֗עַ לָכַ֤ד) is a capture notice and no accession - leaving exactly the sixteen date-fronted accession openings now claimed - and fifteen verses open with ben + numeral + shanah and carry b-m-l-k-w, matching 'the fifteen ben-N-years openings'. The uniqueness assertion holds too: a pattern for waw + PN + ben + PN + malak 'al matches 2Kgs.3.1 and nothing else in the book, and the two comparanda are now presented correctly as date-fronted (וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ at 8:16, בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙ at 13:1) rather than as formal twins. The unevidenced 'every other regnal opening' universal is gone with no replacement overclaim in its place.

OL-M8-2Kgs-007-1's target was an unverified universal ('every other regnal opening... 8:16, 13:1'). The revision replaces it with counted classes -- sixteen date-fronted accession openings and fifteen ben-N-years openings -- which I re-ran independently with a consonantal-stripped regex over the whole book: 17 raw date-formula hits minus 2Kgs.17:6 (a fall-of-Samaria date notice, not an accession) nets 16, and including 12:1's plural spelling of 'years' nets 15 ben-N-years openings, matching the row exactly. My own fronted-subject regex (waw+name+ben+name+malak+'al, consonantal) also returns only 3:1 in the whole book, confirming the row's uniqueness claim independently rather than taking it on faith. No new defect found; the samekh at 3:3 is kept to weak-corroboration language throughout.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: 3:1's accession formula and 3:3's evaluation-clause close both match the witness, and the samekh at 3:3 is correctly held to weak-corroboration tier only. OL's challenge to the strongest_rejected_alternative holds up under my own book-wide sweep of 2 Kings' regnal openings: 16 front a date formula (8:16, 8:25, 9:29, 12:2, 13:1, 13:10, 14:1, 14:23, 15:1, 15:8, 15:17, 15:23, 15:27, 15:32, 16:1, 17:1) and a further 15 front a ben-N-years clause (8:17, 8:26, 12:1, 14:2, 15:2, 15:33, 16:2, 18:2, 21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18), and none of the roughly 31 shares 3:1's own waw-plus-name-plus-מלך-על shape -- so citing 8:16 and 13:1 as formal twins to build a book-wide universal is unevidenced exactly as OL states, even though 3:1's accession formula and the disjunctive opening at 3:4 carry the boundary without needing that comparison at all. The correction belongs to the rejected-alternative's supporting argument, not to the span itself.

primary_reviews.rationale: Most of this row's citation chain is exact — 3:6 does begin וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹרָ֛ם, the seven-day circuit sits at 3:9, the question at 3:11 is rightly attributed to Jehoshaphat, the withdrawal notice at 3:27 is quoted verbatim, and the pe is typed correctly. The 3:4 characterisation, however, misdescribes the verse in two linked ways, and decision 007 labels that same clause incompatibly ('disjunctive nominal clause') with this row's 'launches a single wayyiqtol chain'. Left unused is the single Hebrew fact that best explains why a unit begins here: 3:5's וַיְהִ֖י כְּמ֣וֹת אַחְאָ֑ב וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל resumes 1:1 in verb, participants and temporal peg.

challenges.claim: 3:4 is called 'Mesha's rebellion notice' and credited with launching 'a single wayyiqtol chain'. Neither holds. The verse reads וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד וְהֵשִׁ֤יב לְמֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ … — a qatal (הָיָ֣ה) with a participial predicate followed by a weqatal, i.e. an occupation-and-tribute notice containing no rebellion verb and no wayyiqtol at all; WEB agrees ('Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder; and he supplied the king of Israel …'). The rebellion notice is the next verse, וַיְהִ֖י כְּמ֣וֹת אַחְאָ֑ב וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, whose וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע is the unit's first wayyiqtol. Decision 007 calls this same clause 'the disjunctive nominal clause', so the two rows describe 3:4 in mutually exclusive terms. The 3:4 boundary itself stands, since a fronted-subject disjunctive is exactly what opens a new unit, but both the clause type and the content label are wrong; and 'never releases its grip until 3:27' additionally passes over the waw-x disjunctives inside the span (וְלֹא הָיָ֨ה מַ֧יִם לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה at 3:9, וְהַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ זָרְחָ֣ה עַל הַמָּ֑יִם at 3:22, וְלֹ֥א יָכֹֽלוּ at 3:26).
challenges.suggested_action: Rename 3:4 the tribute/occupation notice, quote 3:5's rebellion clause as the true head of the wayyiqtol chain, bring the clause-type label into line with decision 007, and add the 1:1 / 3:5 resumptive repetition as the positive reason a unit opens at 3:4.

primary_reviews.rationale: The muster, oracle, dawn, and withdrawal-notice quotations all match the witness exactly, and a continuous wayyiqtol chain does run from 3:5 through the closing וַיְהִ֥י קֶצֶף גָּד֖וֹל עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל, supporting one campaign unit. But both the boundary_rationale and the strongest_rejected_alternative describe the three kings as never moving during the consultation, when 3:12's וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו מֶ֧לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט וּמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱדֽוֹם is a real verb of motion -- the three kings do relocate together to reach Elisha, they simply never disperse from one another into separate scenes.

challenges.claim: Both the boundary_rationale ('kings who never move or disperse') and the strongest_rejected_alternative ('the three kings never travel or disperse') overstate the case: 2Kgs 3:12's וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו מֶ֧לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט וּמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱדֽוֹם is a genuine motion verb ('went down to him'); the three kings physically relocate together to consult Elisha, they only fail to separate from one another into distinct scenes.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise to 'the three kings move only as one bloc and never disperse into separate scenes' so the claim does not overstate a physical stillness that 3:12 contradicts.

primary_reviews.rationale: Each clause-type repair is right against the witness: 3:4 is now the tribute notice and does read qatal הָיָ֣ה plus participle נֹקֵ֑ד plus weqatal וְהֵשִׁ֤יב, with no wayyiqtol anywhere in the verse; 3:5 is credited with the chain's head; the 1:1 resumption is quoted verbatim; and 'relocate only as a single bloc' fits וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו at 3:12 without denying the motion the earlier wording denied. The clause label also now agrees with row 007's reading of the same verse. Where the repair over-reached is the newly written interior sweep: 'pausing only for circumstantial asides', three listed, 'none of which turns over the scene's participants or location', is not what a waw-x scan of 3:5-3:27 returns.

challenges.claim: The new enumeration of interior asides is incomplete and its universal fails. Scanning 3:5-3:27 for waw + non-verb clauses returns, besides the three listed at 3:9, 3:22 and 3:26, at least וְהִנֵּה מַ֥יִם בָּאִ֖ים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם at 3:20 and וְכָל מוֹאָב֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ at 3:21 - and 3:21 does turn over participants and vantage point, bringing on all Moab and posting them at the frontier (וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ עַֽל הַגְּבֽוּל) instead of leaving the scene with the three kings.
challenges.suggested_action: Either drop 'only' and the 'none of which' universal, or add 3:20 and 3:21 to the list and argue the narrower point that survives - that no interior aside starts a new scene, 3:21's Moabite muster being the counter-view of one battle rather than a separate episode.

primary_reviews.rationale: Three original defects converge here: LF-M8-2Kgs-008-1's 'kings never move,' and OL-M8-2Kgs-008-1's mislabeling of 3:4 as a rebellion notice carrying 'a single wayyiqtol chain' -- terminology that had contradicted decision 007's own label for the identical clause -- plus the buried 3:9/3:22/3:26 disjunctives. All three are fixed: 3:4 is now correctly parsed as a qatal-plus-participle-plus-weqatal tribute notice, 3:5's rebellion verb is identified as the true wayyiqtol head with the 1:1 cross-reference stated positively rather than negatively, the three internal disjunctives are named as 'circumstantial asides' rather than passed over, and the kings are said to 'relocate only as a single bloc,' matching 3:12's actual plural motion verb of descent. Every Hebrew string quoted in this unusually long rationale collated true against oshb by direct line lookup; no invented participant or place appears in the rewrite.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The muster, oracle, and withdrawal quotations all check out, but two independent problems surface in how the row frames its own opening verse. LF is correct that 3:12's וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו מֶ֧לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל is a genuine motion verb -- the three kings do relocate together to reach Elisha, so 'kings who never move' overstates what 'never disperse into separate scenes' would say more precisely. OL is separately correct that 3:4 is a qatal-plus-weqatal tribute notice with no wayyiqtol anywhere in it (the first wayyiqtol, וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע, appears only at 3:5, the verse that actually resumes 1:1's rebellion notice and its root), so calling 3:4 'Mesha's rebellion notice' that 'launches a single wayyiqtol chain' mislabels both the clause type and its content, and it conflicts outright with decision 007's own, more accurate 'disjunctive nominal clause' label for that identical verse. OL's further point that 3:9, 3:22, and 3:26 each carry their own waw-x disjunctive clause inside the span is likewise confirmed and shows 'never releases its grip' to be an overstatement of an otherwise sound continuous-narrative reading. None of these three corrections moves the opening seam at 3:4, since a disjunctive clause is exactly the kind of signal that opens a new unit no matter which label describes its content.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three quoted strings sit inside their cited verses under character-level collation, and the fronted subject with following qatal at 4:1, וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה, is a real waw-disjunctive opener standing after the withdrawal notice that ends 3:27, וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ לָאָֽרֶץ. primary_reviews.rationale: The petition-cry formula opening 4:1 (וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֜ע לֵאמֹ֗ר) launches an unnamed widow with no participant overlap with the Moab campaign, and 3:27's own withdrawal notice independently confirms that campaign already closed itself before this vignette opens. primary_reviews.rationale: The two summonses were compared letter by letter and the row is candid that they diverge, קְרָ֖א לַשּׁוּנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את at the promise against קְרָא֙ אֶל הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את at the raising, so no false identity of form is asserted. The span holds: nothing between 4:8 and 4:37 restarts with a fronted subject, and Gilgal at 4:38 supplies the next genuine disjunctive restart. Two things fail on inspection. Her exit clause stands at the close of 4:21, וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא, not at 4:22, which opens וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל אִישָׁהּ֒ and carries no verb of leaving; and the temporal formula made into opening evidence, וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם, recurs twice inside the very span it is said to open.

challenges.claim: The statement that the mother does not leave the house until 4:22 is wrong against the Hebrew. The exit verb closes 4:21, וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא, while 4:22 begins וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל אִישָׁהּ֒ and contains no departure verb at all; her travelling verbs are וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ וַתָּב֛וֹא at 4:25. The trailing phrase "well past either candidate seam" also fails on its own terms, because 4:22 stands before the second candidate seam (4:29-31) rather than after it. None of 4:20, 4:21, 4:22, 4:25, or 4:29-31 is cited in the row.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast the sentence so the exit notice is located at the end of 4:21 and the ride to Carmel at 4:25, delete or invert the "well past" phrase, and add the verses the rejection actually leans on.

challenges.claim: The opening evidence is וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם at 4:8, but that same temporal formula recurs inside the span, as וַיְהִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם in 4:11 and וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם in 4:18; my own consonantal search across 2Kgs finds these three occurrences and no others in the book. 4:18 is where the child's collapse begins, so the row rejects a formula-less candidate at 4:20 while stepping over the one internal point that carries the device it treats as unit-opening. The disjunctive force at 4:8 really comes from the arrival clause וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אֶל שׁוּנֵ֗ם together with the new household.
challenges.suggested_action: Move the opening argument onto the arrival clause and the fresh participants, and disclose 4:11 and 4:18 as internal articulations that the recurring formula does not raise into seams.

primary_reviews.rationale: The arrival formula at 4:8 and the closing departure clause at 4:37 (וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת בְּנָ֖הּ וַתֵּצֵֽא) both check out, and the repeated summons refrain (קְרָ֖א לַשּׁוּנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את at 4:12, קְרָא֙ אֶל הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את at 4:36) is a genuine binding device supporting one continuous arc. But the rejected alternative's claim that 'the mother does not leave the house until 4:22' does not match the witness: 4:22 is only her spoken request to her husband (וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל אִישָׁהּ֒, 'she called to her husband'), and her actual departure is not narrated until 4:24 (וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן, 'she saddled the donkey'), two verses later than cited.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale's strongest_rejected_alternative states 'the mother does not leave the house until 4:22, well past either candidate seam,' but 4:22 only records her calling to her husband for a servant and donkey (וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל אִישָׁהּ֒); the saddling/departure clause is 4:24 (וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן), not 4:22.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the citation from 4:22 to 4:24 in the strongest_rejected_alternative sentence. The substantive point survives and is reinforced, since the true departure sits even later than claimed.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both Hebrew-side errors are properly repaired: the exit verb is relocated to the close of 4:21 (וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא), the ride is dated to 4:25's וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ וַתָּב֛וֹא, the false 'well past' is inverted to 'before rather than past', and the recurring temporal idiom is disclosed - my consonantal count of w-y-h-y h-y-w-m across 2 Kings returns exactly 4:8, 4:11 and 4:18, all three inside this span, so the opening argument rightly shifts onto the arrival clause and אִשָּׁ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה. Testing 4:24's וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן against 'her travel toward Elisha is not narrated until 4:25' I accept the distinction, since saddling and the imperative נְהַ֣ג וָלֵ֑ךְ are not narrated travel. challenges.claim: 'neither point carries an arrival or departure formula' is falsified at the second candidate seam. 4:30 closes וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחֲרֶֽיהָ, and 4:31 opens on the very shape this author treats elsewhere as unit-initial - waw plus fronted subject plus qatal of motion, וְגֵחֲזִ֞י עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם - before returning him with וַיָּ֤שָׁב לִקְרָאתוֹ֙. Departure and return are both narrated inside 4:29-31.
challenges.suggested_action: Concede the motion at 4:30-31 and rest the rejection on scene integrity instead: the errand is framed by the mother's refusal to leave Elisha and by Gehazi's failed report, so the movement is internal to one continuous rescue rather than an arrival or departure that opens or closes a unit.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Walking 4:18 through 4:25 against both witnesses turns up five distinct beats: the death at 4:20, the mother's exit from the upper room closing 4:21 (וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא), her transport request at 4:22 (no leaving verb anywhere in it), the saddling at 4:24 (וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן), and her actual travel to Carmel at 4:25 (וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ וַתָּב֛וֹא) — none of which matches 'she leaves the house at 4:22.' A further OL point survives my own book-wide check: וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם recurs in this exact span at 4:11 and 4:18 and nowhere else in the book, so citing it as opening-evidence for 4:8 without disclosing the recurrence overstates its force; the real weight at 4:8 sits on the arrival clause and the new household, not the shared temporal idiom. None of this reaches the actual edges — the arrival at 4:8, the twin summons refrain, and the departure-with-living-son clause at 4:37 stand regardless — so only the prose defending internal continuity is damaged.

primary_reviews.rationale: Each Hebrew string here is byte-identical to its verse, and the row earns credit for naming the mid-verse tension at 5:19 instead of splitting inside it, while WEB's paragraph break between the dismissal and וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ כִּבְרַת אָֽרֶץ is rightly left out of the argument. Two claims fail testing. Verse 5:1 is called a nominal clause although the finite qatal הָיָ֣ה occurs twice in it, in וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל and again in וְהָאִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֛ה גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֖יִל מְצֹרָֽע. The asserted match at 5:20 also does not exist, because that verse leads with a wayyiqtol and keeps its subject behind the verb, so this edge actually rests on Naaman's exit plus the change of actor rather than on repeated opening syntax.

challenges.claim: 5:1 is described as "a nominal-clause participant tag", but the clause is verbal: הָיָ֣ה is a finite qatal and appears twice in the verse, in וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל and in וְהָאִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֛ה גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֖יִל מְצֹרָֽע. No verbless clause stands anywhere in 5:1.
challenges.suggested_action: Relabel it a waw-disjunctive exposition clause with fronted subject and qatal, which is the description that in fact carries the scene-initial force being claimed.

challenges.claim: The clause "5.20 reintroduces Gehazi by full title, a matching participant tag" misstates that verse. 5:20 reads וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י נַעַר֮ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֒, where the wayyiqtol stands first and the subject follows in ordinary post-verbal position, so there is neither fronting nor disjunction to match 5:1. The 5:19/5:20 edge is carried instead by the departure notice וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ כִּבְרַת אָֽרֶץ closing 5:19 together with the change of actor.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace "a matching participant tag" with an accurate account: a wayyiqtol clause whose new subject arrives with full apposition, the seam resting on the preceding exit notice.

primary_reviews.rationale: Naaman's introduction at 5:1 and Gehazi's full-title reintroduction at 5:20 both check out against the witness, and the samekh at 5:19 (single-witness) is properly disclosed as weak-tier support riding on a participant-tag argument that already carries the seam on its own. One label is imprecise: the rationale calls וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל a 'nominal-clause participant tag,' but the clause's predicate is the finite verb hayah ('was'), making this a disjunctive vav-subject-verb (circumstantial) construction rather than a verbless nominal clause in the strict grammatical sense; the functional point about a background clause introducing a new participant still stands.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale labels 5:1's opening clause (וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל) a 'nominal-clause participant tag,' but the clause's predicate is a finite form of the verb 'to be' (hayah, 'was'), so it is a disjunctive/circumstantial vav-subject-verb clause, not a verbless nominal clause. Notably, the companion row M8-2Kgs-014 correctly calls the structurally identical construction at 5:25 (וְהוּא בָא֙ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו) 'circumstantial,' which is inconsistent with calling the same construction type 'nominal' here.
challenges.suggested_action: Relabel as 'disjunctive circumstantial clause (vav-subject + hayah)' for consistency with M8-2Kgs-014's own terminology; the boundary-opening function of the clause is unaffected.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both syntactic mislabels are cured at the source. The witness bears out the new description: in וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה the subject is fronted ahead of the finite qatal הָיָ֣ה at word six, and the verse closes on a second finite clause, וְהָאִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֛ה גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֖יִל מְצֹרָֽע, so nothing verbless stands anywhere in 5:1 and "nominal-clause participant tag" is rightly gone. The 5:20 account is corrected in the same direction, since וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י נַעַר֮ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ begins that verse at offset 0 with its subject trailing, which is exactly what dissolves the old "matching participant tag" equation and throws the edge back onto וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ כִּבְרַת אָֽרֶץ, verse-final in 5:19. One residual I record without raising it: לֵ֣ךְ לְשָׁל֑וֹם occurs once in 2Kgs on my consonantal grep, so "dismissal formula" leans on canon-wide usage the row does not cite, though nothing load-bearing rests on the label here.

Two original claims converge on the same defect and both are cured: LF-M8-2Kgs-013-1 and OL-M8-2Kgs-013-1 both challenged calling 5:1's opener a “nominal-clause participant tag” when its predicate is the finite qatal הָיָ֣ה; the revision now reads “a disjunctive circumstantial clause built on a fronted subject plus the finite verb הָיָ֣ה”, matching both reviewers' suggested relabeling and staying consistent with M8-2Kgs-014's own “circumstantial” label for the structurally identical 5:25 clause. OL-M8-2Kgs-013-2 challenged treating 5:20 as “a matching participant tag” for 5:1; the revision now states plainly that 5:20's subject trails the verb “rather than fronted as at 5.1” and rests the edge on the exit notice plus actor-shift instead — cured. All five quoted fragments (5:1 twice, 5:19 twice, 5:20) byte-collated exactly against 2Kgs_oshb.txt; the 5:19 samekh is typed correctly (SAMEKH), disclosed single-witness, and called “only weak corroboration.”

challenges.claim: The unit's opening is quoted from mid-clause. Both closing quotations sit where the prose places them, וְצָרַ֤עַת נַֽעֲמָן֙ תִּֽדְבַּק בְּךָ֔ opening 5:27 and וַיֵּצֵ֥א מִלְּפָנָ֖יו מְצֹרָ֥ע כַּשָּֽׁלֶג ending it, the samekh after 5:27 is tagged single-witness and demoted, the chapter division is correctly called metadata, and the rejected alternative's וְהוּא בָא֙ is genuinely verse-initial at 5:25. primary_reviews.rationale: Both cited strings check out against 6:1 and 6:7, the pe at MT 6:7 is the right type in the right place and stays subordinate, and the change of subject at 6:8 genuinely terminates the vignette. challenges.claim: 6:1 is credited with "its own petition formula", but וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ בְנֵֽי הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֑ע is clause-initial wayyiqtol with no fronting and no disjunction, the ordinary narrative continuation form. The identical label is applied by M8-2Kgs-009 to 4:1, וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה, which is a genuine waw plus fronted subject plus qatal construction, so one label now spans two opposite syntaxes and implies an opening signal that the Hebrew at 6:1 does not give.

primary_reviews.rationale: The petition formula at 6:1 (וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ בְנֵֽי הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֑ע) and the resolution clause at 6:7 (וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח יָד֖וֹ וַיִּקָּחֵֽהוּ) both check out, and 6:8's new-subject war-council opener (וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הָיָ֥ה נִלְחָ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל) is a genuinely distinct participant and problem shift from the domestic tool-recovery scene, correctly distinguished in the rejected alternative. The far edge of the same sentence, however, still carries a device label of precisely the kind this round was convened to remove.

primary_reviews.rationale: Quotations at 6:8, 6:17, 6:18, and 6:23 all verified against source, and the observation that the twin prayer clauses differ only in pointing while belonging to a single blindness sequence is correct. Three defects surfaced. The assertion that no participant introduction is renewed anywhere in the span is contradicted at 6:15, where the attendant enters by full office, וַ֠יַּשְׁכֵּם מְשָׁרֵ֨ת אִ֥ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֮, and at 6:12, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַחַ֣ד מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו, both being exactly the shape that M8-2Kgs-014 treats as unit-opening at 5:20. Beyond that, the close וְלֹֽא יָ֤סְפוּ עוֹד֙ גְּדוּדֵ֣י אֲרָ֔ם לָב֖וֹא בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל carries none of the to-this-day refrain and explains nothing, so "etiological" is the wrong category, and the opening clause is a durative war-state notice rather than a council device.

challenges.claim: The phrase "without any renewed participant-introduction" is falsified inside the span. 6:15 brings on a new actor by full office, וַ֠יַּשְׁכֵּם מְשָׁרֵ֨ת אִ֥ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֮, and 6:12 introduces וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַחַ֣ד מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו. Both are wayyiqtol clauses with the subject following, precisely the shape M8-2Kgs-014 calls a unit-opening participant tag at 5:20, so the criterion is being applied in opposite directions within one cluster.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate the claim as "no disjunctive, fronted-subject clause interrupts 6:9-6:23", and add that 6:12 and 6:15 introduce participants without disjunction and therefore remain inside the Dothan scene.

challenges.claim: The close of 6:23 is called "the etiological summary", yet וְלֹֽא יָ֤סְפוּ עוֹד֙ גְּדוּדֵ֣י אֲרָ֔ם לָב֖וֹא בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל explains no name, custom, or surviving state of affairs and carries nothing of the עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה refrain. My book-wide search places that refrain at 2:22, 8:22, 14:7, 16:6, 17:23, 17:34, 17:41, 20:17, and 21:15, and never at 6:23.
challenges.suggested_action: Relabel the clause a cessation or campaign-summary notice, reserving "etiological" for the verses where the to-this-day refrain actually stands.

challenges.claim: The opener is labelled "the king of Aram's war-council formula", but the quoted clause וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הָיָ֥ה נִלְחָ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל is waw plus subject plus qatal plus participle, a durative background notice of an ongoing war, not a council. The one council verb in the verse, וַיִּוָּעַץ֙, occurs nowhere else in 2Kgs on my consonantal search, so no recurring device exists for the word "formula" to name.
challenges.suggested_action: Describe 6:8a as a disjunctive scene-setting background clause that installs a new subject, and either drop the word "formula" or attach it to the consultation clause while noting that clause is unique in the book.

primary_reviews.rationale: The war-council opener at 6:8 and the etiological close at 6:23 (וְלֹֽא יָ֤סְפוּ עוֹד֙ גְּדוּדֵ֣י אֲרָ֔ם לָב֖וֹא בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) both check out, and the two prayer clauses at 6:17/6:18 (וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל אֱלִישָׁע֙ / וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל אֱלִישָׁ֤ע) are correctly read as one continuous exchange rather than a seam. But that rejected alternative is thin: a genuinely stronger unaddressed candidate is the arrival-in-Samaria clause at 6:19b-20 (וַיְהִי֮ כְּבֹאָ֣ם שֹׁמְרוֹן֒, 'and it happened when they came to Samaria'), an explicit location change of the very kind the book strategy elsewhere treats as tier-1; the row never engages it, though on inspection it fails too, since it is the direct payoff of the deception Elisha launches at 6:19a rather than an independent arrival formula.

challenges.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative offered (splitting between the two adjacent prayer verses 6:17/6:18) is a weak candidate that no serious segmenter would propose, since both sit inside one uninterrupted prayer-response exchange with no participant or location change between them. The genuinely stronger unaddressed rival is the arrival-in-Samaria clause at 6:19b-20 (וַיְהִי֮ כְּבֹאָ֣ם שֹׁמְרוֹן֒), an explicit location change; it ultimately also fails as an independent seam (it has no arrival formula of its own and is the direct continuation of the march begun at 6:19a), so the boundary itself is unaffected.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the rejected alternative with the 6:19b-20 Samaria-arrival candidate and argue explicitly why it is a continuation rather than a fresh scene, rather than resting the case on the trivially weak 6:17/6:18 split.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three original Hebrew-side items land. The opener is now described as waw-subject-qatal-participle and וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הָיָ֥ה נִלְחָ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל matches that description word for word; the retired "formula" charge is replaced by a uniqueness claim I can confirm, since וַיִּוָּעַץ֙ is the only verbal reflex of that root anywhere in 2Kgs on my consonantal grep (9:8 and 17:4 belong to a different root, 18:20 is the noun). The relabelling of 6:23 verifies too: וְלֹֽא יָ֤סְפוּ עוֹד֙ גְּדוּדֵ֣י אֲרָ֔ם לָב֖וֹא בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל closes the verse, and my search puts the to-this-day refrain הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּדְבַ֥ר at 2:22, 8:22, 14:7, 16:6, 17:23, 17:34, 17:41, 20:17 and 21:15, never at 6:23. primary_reviews.rationale: Four original items, all cured. peer_crosscheck.assessment: Four separate challenges land on this row and all four hold up. LF is right that the offered rejected alternative (splitting 6:17 from 6:18) is trivial and that a stronger rival sits at the Samaria-arrival clause (וַיְהִי֮ כְּבֹאָ֣ם שֹׁמְרוֹן֒, 6:19b-20), and LF's own follow-through is also correct that this candidate ultimately fails, since it is the direct payoff of the deception Elisha launches earlier in 6:19 rather than an independent arrival. OL's claim that 'no renewed participant-introduction' overstates the span also checks out: 6:12 (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַחַ֣ד מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו) and 6:15 (וַ֠יַּשְׁכֵּם מְשָׁרֵ֨ת אִ֥ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֮) both bring on unnamed figures through ordinary wayyiqtol, the same shape this cluster elsewhere credits as participant-introducing at 5:20, an inconsistency best fixed by restricting the criterion to disjunctive fronted-subject clauses specifically. My own book-wide search for the 'to this day' refrain (עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה) places it only at 2:22, 8:22, 14:7, 16:6, 17:23, 17:34, 17:41, 20:17, and 21:15, confirming OL's claim that 6:23 never carries it and that 'etiological' overclaims what is really a plain cessation notice. Finally, my own grep for וַיִּוָּעַץ֙ returns exactly one hit in the whole book, at 6:8 itself, confirming OL's point that 'formula' cannot describe a unique verb and that 6:8's opening הָיָ֥ה נִלְחָ֖ם clause is a durative background notice rather than a council device in its own right. None of the four fixes relocates either edge: the change of subject at 6:8 and the pe-corroborated close at 6:23 remain the boundary regardless of how the internal prose is relabeled.

challenges.suggested_action: Keep 17:5 as the cross-reference, since the ascent-and-siege verb pair genuinely recurs there, and either drop 3:6 or label it separately as a troop-levy opener instead of a siege-muster of the same shape.

primary_reviews.rationale: The 6:24 muster clause quoted by the row (וַיִּקְבֹּ֛ץ בֶּן הֲדַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם אֶת כָּל מַחֲנֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֕עַל וַיָּ֖צַר עַל שֹׁמְרֽוֹן) checks byte-identical against oshb, and its 'go up ... besiege Samaria' verb pair recurs almost verbatim at 17:5 (וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶ֖יהָ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים), confirming the row's cross-reference rather than an invented parallel; the strategy's own matrix groups 3:5-7, 6:24, and 17:5 as one campaign-muster formula family, so this is not fabricated. All three cited samekh marks (6:33, 7:2, 7:20, MT numbering, single-witness) match pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly (SAMEKH/SAMEKH/SAMEKH) and are used only as corroboration, never as the driver.

Elisha is named inside the preceding complex at 6:32 (וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵית֔וֹ) and 7:1 (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע), and he is the subject of the very next verse at 8:7 (וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק); the king of Israel likewise walks the wall at 6:26 and hears the petition at 8:3-6. primary_reviews.rationale: 8:1's opening clause (וֶאֱלִישָׁ֡ע דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל הָאִשָּׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱיָ֨ה אֶת בְּנָ֜הּ) checks byte-identical against oshb; grammatically it is vav + subject + qatal (a Piel perfect 3ms verb), correctly labeled a disjunctive flashback marker rather than a mainline vayyiqtol continuation. The closing quote at 8:6 (הָשֵׁ֤יב אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לָהּ֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל תְּבוּאֹ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה מִיּ֛וֹם עָזְבָ֥ה אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ וְעַד עָֽתָּה) matches oshb exactly, and the cited pe mark at 8:6 matches pmarks_2Kgs.json (PE). I tested 8:4's own disjunctive-looking clause as a possible unaddressed internal seam, since it introduces Gehazi as a new interlocutor, but 8:4 is vav-subject-participle rather than vav-subject-qatal -- a same-scene 'meanwhile' construction, not a flashback opener -- and 8:5's mainline narrative clause explicitly welds it back into the single audience scene the woman's arrival completes, so no unargued seam survives there.

The participant overreach is retracted outright, and every concession the replacement makes is accurate on the witness: וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵית֔וֹ opens 6:32, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע opens 7:1, וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק opens 8:7, and 6:26 does begin וַֽיְהִי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֹבֵ֖ר, so Elisha and the king of Israel are now correctly granted on both flanks instead of denied. The two edges rest on syntax and content I can confirm, וֶאֱלִישָׁ֡ע דִּבֶּ֣ר standing at offset 0 of 8:1 as waw-subject-qatal and marking a backward temporal step, and הָשֵׁ֤יב אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לָהּ֙ closing 8:6 immediately before the flat location shift at 8:7. The pe after 8:6 matches the mark witness, appears only in the reference list tagged single-witness, and drives nothing. Worth recording short of a challenge: the siege complex also stages a woman's appeal to this same king at 6:26, וְאִשָּׁ֗ה צָעֲקָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙, so the surviving uniqueness term holds only because "specific" individuates the audience, while the land-restitution subject matter and the flashback syntax are the durable contrasts.

OL-M8-2Kgs-018-1 challenged the claim that neither flanking scene “shares this scene's participants,” contradicted by Elisha's recurrence at 6:32/7:1/8:7 and the king's at 6:26/8:3-6; the revision now names all four cross-references directly — “Elisha sitting at home at 6:32 ... and speaking at 7:1 ... then arriving at Damascus at 8:7; the king walking the wall at 6:26” — concedes “the row's isolation cannot rest on participant identity,” and rests uniqueness instead on “the petitioner herself, the specific royal audience she is granted, and the land-restitution subject matter,” matching the suggested action almost verbatim. peer_crosscheck.assessment: The grammatical case for 8:1 as a flashback opener stands: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֡ע דִּבֶּ֣ר is genuinely vav plus fronted subject plus qatal, and the petition-resolution quote at 8:6 plus the pe mark there (confirmed PE in pmarks_2Kgs.json, single-witness) are both accurate. But OL-018-1 is borne out letter for letter: Elisha is a named participant on both neighboring flanks, sitting at home in the siege complex (וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵית֔וֹ, 6:32) and speaking at 7:1 (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע), then arriving at Damascus in the very next row (וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק, 8:7); the king of Israel likewise appears on the wall at 6:26 (וַֽיְהִי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל) and hears the petition at 8:3-6. The row's disjunctive 'or' claim that neither neighbor shares participants, setting, or verb form is falsified on the participant leg specifically, since Elisha and the unnamed king carry across all three rows. This does not touch the boundary itself -- the fronted-subject-qatal opener, the petition's resolution, and the flat location-shift at 8:7 are independent of the participant argument and remain intact -- so only the isolation sentence needs replacing with what the Hebrew actually supports (a unique petitioner, a unique royal audience, and a unique subject matter, not unique participants).

Machine collation puts all five Hebrew strings of this row byte-identical to the verses they cite, and the positional claims hold: וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק stands at the head of 8:7 and וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ חֲזָהאֵ֖ל תַּחְתָּֽיו ends 8:15, so the arrival/succession frame the row argues really is where it says it is, with the pe carried only as "(pe, single-witness)" in the refs and never as a driver. The far-edge repair holds on the Hebrew side: 9:1 does begin וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים at the head of the verse, matching 4:38's וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙ and 13:14's וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה, and the 8:1 form the row leans on is likewise a fronted-subject qatal (וֶאֱלִישָׁ֡ע דִּבֶּ֣ר). The mark sits where the row says -- pmarks records PE at 8:29 -- and it is labelled single-witness and left behind the disclosed part-boundary suspension rather than driving it. The wound notice was also re-scoped to 8:28 as the docket asked. The one place this repair left the row weaker is that new 8:28 citation itself, which quotes a verbless splinter (אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם) as the place the engagement "is narrated" while the governing וַיַּכּ֥וּ is shorn off.

challenges.claim: The 8:28 citation added during repair quotes אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם and presents it as where "the Ramoth-gilead engagement itself is narrated," but that string is subject plus object with its governing verb removed. 8:28 narrates the engagement with וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ אֶת יוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב לַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה ... בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד and the wounding with וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם. As quoted the fragment predicates nothing and cannot carry the narrative claim attached to it; it collates clean against the source, so this is a scope defect rather than a character defect.
challenges.suggested_action: Quote the wounding clause whole -- וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם -- and, if the engagement as such is meant, cite the campaign clause at the head of the verse (וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ אֶת יוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב לַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה ... בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד) beside it.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both defects the OL challenge raised are cured: the wound notice now cites 8:28 (אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם) alongside 8:29 rather than mis-scoping it to 8:29 alone, and 9:1's fronted-subject-qatal opener is now conceded as genuine and parallelled to 4:38/13:14 rather than waved off as a bare external cutpoint -- the row honestly discloses a suspension at the fixed part boundary instead of claiming resolution. I confirmed the added Wiederaufnahme claim against book_strategy_draft.md, which independently states '9:14-15a resumes 8:28-29 (Joram's Ramoth wound)' in both its decision-matrix row and its expected_low_confidence_regions list, and I checked the pe placement against pmarks_2Kgs.json (8.29 = PE, matching 'falls exactly at this disclosed suspension point'). No new corruption in any of the four Hebrew quotes; confidence remains medium, which the disclosed suspension still justifies.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The 8:25 dating-and-accession opener is unopposed at its head, exactly as claimed. OL-021-1 nonetheless lands on both its points: 9:1 opens וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א, the same vav-fronted-subject-qatal construction that decision 018 treats as decisive at 8:1, and that pattern independently checks out as opening fresh Elisha scenes at 4:38 (וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב) and 13:14 (וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה) -- so calling the far edge purely an 'external seam' rather than one with its own internal formula overstates the case. The wound material is likewise mis-scoped: the actual engagement and wounding are narrated at 8:28 (אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם, 'the Arameans struck Joram'), and the quoted 8:29 clause reports only Joram's subsequent withdrawal to recover, not the wound itself. Neither point moves the span: the campaign's fixed part-boundary at 9:1 still requires the row to stop at 8:29 regardless of what kind of formula sits just past it, so what needs revision is the stated rationale behind the medium-confidence call and the citation gap at 8:28, not the row's edges.

primary_reviews.rationale: The closing half of this row holds up: וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ מָלַ֥ךְ יֵהֽוּא is exact at 9:13 and answers the private anointing poured out at 9:6, and וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁ֗ר יֵה֛וּא is genuinely the first word of 9:14, so the pivot described there is real. challenges.claim: “The unit opens on Elisha's commissioning formula, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ (2Kgs.9.1)” is not clause-initial: the verse opens וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים, and the quoted speech clause is the second clause, starting at the seventh word. My own book-wide search of 2Kgs finds a verse-initial vav-plus-Elisha clause six times — 2:12, 4:38, 6:32, 8:1, 9:1, 13:14 — with 4:38 (וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙) and 13:14 (וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה) both opening new units, so the row has quoted straight past the form that carries its own boundary.
challenges.suggested_action: Requote 9:1 from וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים and argue the near edge as fronted-subject qatal introducing a new participant, keeping the commissioning imperatives as the unit's content rather than as its opening marker.

primary_reviews.rationale: 9:1's commissioning clause (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ) and the 9:13 acclamation clause (וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ מָלַ֥ךְ יֵהֽוּא) both check byte-identical against oshb, as does the 9:14 pivot verb (וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁ֗ר יֵה֛וּא). The claimed commission-formula parallel to 1:3 and 19:20 is grounded in the book strategy's own literary-form matrix, not fabricated. The real argued basis for the 9:13/9:14 seam is the mode shift from a lone prophet's private errand to Jehu's own public conspiracy, which the row states explicitly rather than resting on the conspiracy-verb label alone.

Requoting from the true head of 9:1 is exactly what the docket asked for, and that is what now stands: וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים (verse-initial on collation), with חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ demoted to errand content -- appropriately, since the same imperative pair is addressed to Gehazi at 4:29 and so cannot carry a boundary by itself. Both comparanda are byte-identical and verse-initial where claimed (וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙ at 4:38, וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה at 13:14), the close וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ מָלַ֥ךְ יֵהֽוּא ends 9:13, and וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁ֗ר יֵה֛וּא heads 9:14. Probing for repair damage I tested the private/public contrast the new sentence leans on: 9:6 does put the anointing indoors (וַיָּבֹ֣א הַבַּ֔יְתָה ... מְשַׁחְתִּ֧יךָֽ לְמֶ֛לֶךְ), so the claim is not overdrawn, and no quotation in the row picked up a stray character.

The mis-citation the OL challenge caught -- quoting the mid-verse imperative חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ as if it were the opener -- is cured: the row now opens its own quote at the true clause-initial position, וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים, and demotes the imperative to 'the errand's content rather than its opening signal.' I verified this quote is clause-initial and exact against oshb 9:1, and confirmed the two comparison citations (4:38, 13:14) are genuine vav-subject-qatal constructions grammatically parallel to 9:1. New-defect hunt: the row does not overreach into claiming all six book-wide vav+Elisha clauses are openers -- it cites only the two that the challenge itself conceded open new scenes, so no fresh universal claim was smuggled in.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The 9:13 acclamation and 9:14 pivot verb both collate exactly, and the mode-shift argument they support (private errand giving way to public conspiracy) is sound on its own terms. OL-022-1 is nonetheless correct that the quoted commissioning imperative is not the verse's opening clause: 9:1 begins וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים, a fronted-subject-qatal construction, with the quoted speech (חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ...) arriving only after it. Rather than undercutting the boundary, this correction strengthens it, since that same construction is independently confirmed opening new Elisha pericopes at 4:38 and 13:14, giving the 9:1 edge a textual anchor the row never claimed. So the fix here is to requote the verse from its true head and treat the imperatives as the unit's content, while the 9:1 boundary itself needs no relocation.
