primary_reviews.rationale: Every quotation collates exactly and the resumptive reading is well founded: וַיָּשָׁב֩ יְהוֹרָ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהִתְרַפֵּ֣א at 9:15 repeats the 8:29 wound report with the longer spelling of the king's name, which is what a Wiederaufnahme looks like. The closing argument is the weak point, because the verse used to shut the unit carries the accession formula and not a closing one — וּבִשְׁנַת֙ אַחַ֣ת עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֖ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֑ב מָלַ֥ךְ is the same construction the two rows immediately before this one call an opening formula at 8:16 and at 8:25. A smaller overstatement concerns the itinerary the row says nothing interrupts.

challenges.claim: 9:29 is treated as “a dated regnal notice” that closes the unit, but וּבִשְׁנַת֙ אַחַ֣ת עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֖ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֑ב מָלַ֥ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֖ה עַל יְהוּדָֽה is the accession formula in its standard shape. On my own book-wide search, seventeen verses in 2Kgs open with a bi-shnat dating clause; sixteen of those carry the accession verb malakh, and in every one but 9:29 that clause heads a reign account — including וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ at 8:16 and בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה at 8:25, which rows 020 and 021 of this same cluster label opening formulas. One form cannot be an opener twice in a cluster and a closing device once without an argument being made for the difference.
challenges.suggested_action: Make the case explicit instead of by label: 9:29 is a retrospective synchronism appended once both kings are dead, so no reign follows and it cannot open anything — that reasoning defends the edge. Disclose alongside it that the WLC break falls after 9:28 rather than after 9:29 (single-witness, weak corroboration, never a driver), so the placement is argued on tier-1 grounds in full view of the apparatus.

challenges.claim: “this one continuous drive from Ramoth Gilead to the field of Naboth” does not describe the span the row is holding together. Ahaziah's death is introduced by וַאֲחַזְיָ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ רָאָ֔ה וַיָּ֕נָס — fronted subject plus qatal, the construction this cluster elsewhere treats as scene-initial — and it leaves the Jezreel theatre altogether, running וַיָּ֥נָס מְגִדּ֖וֹ וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם and then וַיַּרְכִּ֧בוּ אֹת֛וֹ עֲבָדָ֖יו יְרוּשָׁלְָ֑מָה. The watchman material at 9:17 likewise opens on a circumstantial disjunctive with a new participant at a new vantage point.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword the continuity claim to what is defensible — one uninterrupted pursuit sequence launched by a single conspiracy — and record the 9:27 disjunctive together with the Megiddo and Jerusalem moves as internal articulation that was tested and rejected as a seam, rather than asserting an unbroken single drive.

primary_reviews.rationale: The 9:14 conspiracy clause (וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁ֗ר יֵה֛וּא בֶּן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן נִמְשִׁ֖י אֶל יוֹרָ֑ם) and 9:15's Wiederaufnahme (וַיָּשָׁב֩ יְהוֹרָ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהִתְרַפֵּ֣א בִיְזְרְעֶ֗אל) both check byte-identical against oshb and against 8:29's near-duplicate wording, confirming the resumptive-repetition claim rather than a loose paraphrase. The 9:29 closing synchronism (וּבִשְׁנַת֙ אַחַ֣ת עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֖ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֑ב מָלַ֥ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֖ה עַל יְהוּדָֽה) is an exact full-verse match. The row's two different watchman-material ranges (9:17-20 in the main rationale versus 9:17-22 in the rejected alternative) are not a contradiction: they describe different things -- the relay-only verses versus the full turn-marker unit the book strategy's own matrix names as '9:17-22 watchman relays,' which the row's rejected-alternative range matches precisely.

The label-into-argument conversion is genuine and the text bears it out: 9:29 governs nothing, because Joram falls at 9:24 (וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת יְהוֹרָם֙) and Ahaziah at 9:27, and 9:30 turns away to וַיָּב֥וֹא יֵה֖וּא יִזְרְעֶ֑אלָה, so the accession-shaped clause opens no reign. The apparatus disclosure is corrected as well -- pmarks puts PE at 9:28, not 9:29, exactly as the row now states, cited two-sided and not driving -- and 9:27 and 9:17 are recorded as tested-and-rejected turn-markers, where the row's narrower negative does survive inspection. A regression probe on the Wiederaufnahme pair came back clean: 8:29 reads וַיָּשָׁב֩ יוֹרָ֨ם and 9:15 reads וַיָּשָׁב֩ יְהוֹרָ֨ם, and the row quoted each with its own spelling instead of harmonising them. My residual is that the 8:16/8:25 comparison is routed through sibling row numbers rather than through the verses.

challenges.claim: The Hebrew of the comparison is sound -- 8:16 opens וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ and 8:25 opens בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה, the same accession shape as 9:29's וּבִשְׁנַת֙ אַחַ֣ת עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה -- but the row states it as "the same construction rows 020 and 021 of this cluster call an opener at 8:16 and 8:25," and rev_cluster_03 contains no row 020 (its members are 019, 021, 022, 023, 025, 026, 027, 028). Sibling-row numbering is review scaffolding: it cannot be checked against the frozen record this row travels in, and it will read as false wherever the row is read apart from the cluster.
challenges.suggested_action: Attribute the contrast to the verses and to the matrix class rather than to sibling row numbers, e.g. "the same bi-shnat accession construction that opens the reign accounts at 8:16 and 8:25".

primary_reviews.rationale: Both OL items are cured. First, 9:29 is no longer called a plain 'dated regnal notice' that closes the unit by label alone -- the row now argues explicitly that it is a retrospective synchronism recorded once both kings are dead, so it cannot open a reign, and it corrects the pe placement to 'one verse earlier, after 9:28' (verified against pmarks_2Kgs.json: 9.28 = PE, 9.29 = no mark). Second, the overstated 'continuous drive' claim is walked back to 'one uninterrupted pursuit sequence launched by a single conspiracy,' with Ahaziah's flight (9:27, a genuine fronted-subject-qatal clause) and the watchman relay (9:17, a genuine disjunctive) now logged as turn-markers tested and rejected rather than denied outright. I grammatically confirmed both labels and the other counts elsewhere in the cluster are unaffected. One carryover phrase -- 'rows 020 and 021 of this cluster' -- reuses the original challenger's own wording for an administrative grouping outside my reviewed decision_ids; the substantive point (8:16 and 8:25 both function as regnal openers) is independently confirmed by book_strategy_draft.md's decision matrix and by row 021's own text, so this is not a live textual defect.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The Wiederaufnahme reading holds: 9:15's opening (וַיָּשָׁב֩ יְהוֹרָ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהִתְרַפֵּ֣א) genuinely resumes 8:29's wound notice with the fuller spelling of the king's name. OL-023-1 survives my own book-wide census of every verse-initial bi-shnat dating clause in 2Kgs: there are seventeen (8:16, 8:25, 9:29, 12:2, 13:1, 13:10, 14:1, 14:23, 15:1, 15:8, 15:17, 15:23, 15:27, 15:32, 16:1, 17:1, 17:6), sixteen of which carry the malakh accession verb, and 9:29 is the sole member of that group of sixteen that does not open a fresh reign account -- because Ahaziah's reign already opened back at 8:25. Calling 9:29 simply 'a dated regnal notice' obscures that this cluster's own rows 020 and 021 label the identical construction an opening formula at 8:16 and 8:25, so the asymmetry needs an argued reason (retrospective synchronism after both kings are dead), not a bare label; separately, pmarks_2Kgs.json places its pe mark after 9:28, one verse short of the row's chosen close, weak corroboration the row never disclosed. OL-023-2 also holds: 9:27's opening (וַאֲחַזְיָ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ רָאָ֔ה...) is itself a fronted-subject-qatal clause that carries the action to Megiddo and then to burial in Jerusalem, well past 'the field of Naboth' the row's continuity claim names as the terminus. Neither finding relocates the span -- no alternative boundary is proposed by either primary -- so 9:14-9:29 stands, with the closing-formula argument and itinerary description needing rewriting rather than the edges themselves.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quoted strings are byte-identical and the labels attached to them are accurate: 9:30 pairs a wayyiqtol arrival with the disjunctive וְאִיזֶ֣בֶל שָׁמְעָ֗ה, bringing Jezebel in as a speaking participant for the first time after three verses that only mention her (9:7, 9:10, 9:22), while וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֣ה ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֗ר בְּיַד עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר at 9:36 is a full fulfilment-citation naming Elijah as its source. I probed 9:31-35 for an unargued seam and found none: וְיֵה֖וּא בָּ֣א בַשָּׁ֑עַר at 9:31 is circumstantial to the same window confrontation, and the burial errand of 9:34-35 furnishes the citation's occasion rather than a new scene. The mark is verified in pmarks_2Kgs.json as PE at MT 9:37, matching the row's petuchah label and its single-witness disclosure, with the closing edge resting on the citation formula and not on the mark.

9:30's arrival clause (וַיָּב֥וֹא יֵה֖וּא יִזְרְעֶ֑אלָה וְאִיזֶ֣בֶל שָׁמְעָ֗ה) and the 9:36 citation clause (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֣ה ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֗ר בְּיַד עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּ֖י) both check byte-identical against oshb. Reading 9:37 in full (והית וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה נִבְלַ֣ת אִיזֶ֗בֶל כְּדֹ֛מֶן עַל פְּנֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּחֵ֣לֶק יִזְרְעֶ֑אל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֹאמְר֖וּ זֹ֥את אִיזָֽבֶל) confirms the dung-image clause continues the same quoted oracle begun at 9:36's citation formula rather than opening new material after the citation had already closed the account, so the row's placement of the close is accurate. The petuchah cited at 9:37 matches pmarks_2Kgs.json (PE) and is correctly disclosed as single-witness, weak corroboration only.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: No challenge was raised against this row by either primary, and a fresh read of 9:30-9:37 turns up nothing new: the arrival-plus-Jezebel-hearing opener, the citation formula at 9:36 naming Elijah as its source, and the dung-image close at 9:37 all check byte-identical against oshb, and the petuchah mark there matches pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly (PE, MT 9:37, single-witness), sitting after the citation formula has already closed the account rather than doing any boundary work itself. The eunuchs' and burial party's material inside the span furnishes the citation's occasion rather than reopening any prior scene. Nothing here calls for correction.

primary_reviews.rationale: Machine collation lands all three quoted strings on their cited verses byte-for-byte, and the rear edge holds: 10:12 restarts with וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיָּבֹ֔א וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ toward a named destination, so stopping at 10:11 is defensible. The front edge is right for the wrong clause — 10:1 begins וּלְאַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן, a waw-plus-prepositional verbless clause, and the letter clause the row leans on only follows it. Probing the interior, the temporal frames וַיְהִ֗י כְּבֹ֤א הַסֵּ֨פֶר֙ (10:7) and וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ (10:9) both stay subordinate turns, so I find no unargued seam inside the span.

challenges.claim: The row makes the letter clause the device this unit "turns on" at 10:1, but that clause is not where the verse starts. 2Kgs.10.1 opens וּלְאַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן — waw + prepositional phrase + verbless predication, the disjunctive scene-setting construction — and only then וַיִּכְתֹּב֩ יֵה֨וּא סְפָרִ֜ים. The strongest Hebrew signal for the row's own front boundary is therefore left uncited.
challenges.suggested_action: Cite the verse-initial disjunctive verbless clause as the primary front-edge evidence at 10:1 and present the letter clause as the unit's organizing device rather than its opening signal.

challenges.claim: 10:10 is offered as a fulfillment notice stacked against the completion clause of 10:11, but the quoted kî-clause is subordinate to the imperative heading the verse, דְּע֣וּ אֵפ֗וֹא, so it is Jehu's address to the people rather than narration. The narrator's own fulfillment notice in this arc, כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, stands at 10:17, outside this row.
challenges.suggested_action: Mark 10:10 as a fulfillment claim voiced inside the king's speech, so its register difference from the narrated completion clause at 10:11 is on the record.

primary_reviews.rationale: The letter-frame opener וַיִּכְתֹּב֩ יֵה֨וּא סְפָרִ֜ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שֹׁמְר֗וֹן (10:1) is a genuine device shift from the Jezebel fulfillment notice closing at 9:37, and the closing pair of this row -- the fulfillment clause and the completion clause עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד (10:11) -- both quote verbatim from OSHB and hand off cleanly to the triple movement verb opening 10:12. The second letter (10:6) and the head-basket notice (10:7-8) are correctly folded in as internal turns of the same device rather than independent scenes.

At the front edge the fix is right on the text: 10:1 does begin וּלְאַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן -- waw plus prepositional phrase plus verbless predication -- with the letter clause following, and the row now treats that clause as the unit's organising device rather than its opening signal. The register correction is equally sound: דְּע֣וּ אֵפ֗וֹא is imperative in Jehu's own mouth, continuous with the address אֶל כָּל הָעָ֔ם at 10:9, while עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד closes 10:11 as narration. New-damage probes came back clean -- seventy holds at 10:1 and again at 10:7 (שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֑ישׁ), 10:6 really is a second letter (סֵ֨פֶר שֵׁנִ֜ית), the seventeen-verse arithmetic for 10:1-17 is correct, and 10:12 does open with three movement verbs (וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיָּבֹ֔א וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמְר֑וֹן).

Both OL items are cured. The unit's opener is now correctly identified as the verse-initial disjunctive verbless clause וּלְאַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן, with the letter-writing clause demoted to the unit's organizing device rather than claimed as its opening signal. Separately, 10:10's fulfillment claim is now explicitly marked as Jehu's own speech to the assembled people (the דְּע֣וּ אֵפ֗וֹא imperative governs the citation), set in contrast against the narrator's own completion clause at 10:11 -- the register distinction the challenge asked for is now on the record instead of collapsed into a single 'resolution.' I verified all four quoted spans (10:1 twice, 10:10, 10:11) as exact oshb substrings and rechecked the seventy-sons figure (שִׁבְעִ֥ים) against 10:1 and 10:6-7 for consistency. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: I re-derived 10:1 directly from oshb: the verse opens with the disjunctive clause about Ahab's seventy sons (וּלְאַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן), not the letter-writing clause the frozen rationale treats as the unit's opening signal, so OL's citation gap is real, though the row's span (10:1-10:11) is unaffected since the whole verse is the front edge either way. OL's second point also holds: the fulfillment wording at 10:10 sits inside Jehu's imperative address to the people opened at 10:9 (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל כָּל הָעָ֔ם), a register the frozen rationale folds into the narrator's own completion clause at 10:11 without disclosure — though the book's own device matrix independently lists 10:10 as one of the book's fulfillment-notice instances in its own right, so the speech-register nuance does not weaken its evidentiary role in this row's close. LF endorsed both citations without probing either one, which is a real precision gap LF missed rather than an OL overreach. Neither challenge touches the boundary itself; both concern the accuracy of the supporting prose.

primary_reviews.rationale: The triple wayyiqtol at 10:12 and the closing עַד הִשְׁמִיד֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה at 10:17 reproduce the witness exactly; the tally אַרְבָּעִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ אִ֔ישׁ matches the row's forty-two, and both parashah keys are correctly typed against pmarks with the single-witness label and no driver role. What does not survive checking is the negative used to set aside the samekh-corroborated alternative. Samaria is announced at 10:12 and reached at 10:17, so the span itself looks sound — the ground given for it does not.

challenges.claim: The competing split is rejected because Jehonadab supposedly boards "mid-journey with no departure or arrival formula marking a break". The Hebrew says otherwise: the verse immediately after the cited samekh opens וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֡ם וַיִּמְצָ֣א אֶת יְהוֹנָדָב֩ (10:15), a verse-initial departure formula, and the same phrase heads 2:25, וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל (accentuation differs), where it launches a fresh itinerary stage.
challenges.suggested_action: Withdraw the "no departure formula" ground and rest the unity of 10:12-17 on what actually binds it: the Samaria destination stated at 10:12 and consummated by וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן at 10:17, with Jehonadab carried into the chariot at 10:15-16.

primary_reviews.rationale: The triple movement verb וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיָּבֹ֔א וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמְר֑וֹן at 10:12 opens a clean location shift onto the road, and the row closes on the fulfillment notice עַד הִשְׁמִיד֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶל אֵלִיָּֽהוּ at 10:17, matching PE in pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly as cited. The samekh at 10:14 is correctly disclosed as single-witness weak corroboration rather than a boundary driver, consistent with the m8-mesh-r2 rule, and the claim that Jehonadab boards the moving chariot with no arrival or departure formula between 10:14 and 10:15 holds up against the text of both witnesses.

Withdrawal accepted: the row no longer denies a departure formula at 10:15 but concedes וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֡ם וַיִּמְצָ֣א אֶת יְהוֹנָדָב֩ as verse-initial, and rests the unity of the stretch on the destination named at 10:12 and consummated by וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן at 10:17 -- both quotations verse-initial and byte-exact, with the forty-two of אַרְבָּעִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ אִ֔ישׁ counted correctly and samekh 10:14 / pe 10:17 both matching the single witness and both cited as corroboration only. The concession, however, carried 10:15's pointing across to 2:25, where the text actually reads וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל; the docket had disclosed that accentual difference and the rewrite dropped the qualifier.

challenges.claim: The repair writes "the same מִשָּׁ֡ם-departure construction that launches a fresh itinerary stage at 2:25," but that pointed form stands only at 10:15; 2:25 reads וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל, i.e. מִשָּׁ֖ם carrying a different accent. My own consonantal search on the unpointed sequence returns exactly two verses (2:25 and 10:15), so the construction claim is right while the pointed citation is not shared between them -- and the original docket's disclosure that the accentuation differs was dropped in the rewrite.
challenges.suggested_action: Restore the disclosure or quote 2:25 in its own form -- e.g. "the same departure construction, pointed מִשָּׁ֖ם at 2:25 and מִשָּׁ֡ם at 10:15" -- so the shared element is claimed at the consonantal level where it actually holds.

primary_reviews.rationale: The OL challenge's single item is cured: the row withdraws the false 'no departure or arrival formula' ground and now concedes that 10:15's וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֡ם is a genuine departure construction, parallel to the one at 2:25, before arguing the unity holds anyway because the Samaria destination is announced already at 10:12 and only reached at 10:17. I confirmed both Hebrew quotes and the parallel citation are exact against oshb, and cross-checked the two mark citations against pmarks_2Kgs.json: the samekh keyed to 10:14 and the petuchah keyed to 10:17 both match exactly, are correctly labeled single-witness, and are used only as reinforcement -- the unity argument itself still rests on the tier-1 destination-formula logic, not on the marks. The forty-two-kinsmen count is unchanged and correct. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Checking 10:15 against oshb confirms OL's catch: it opens with a genuine departure formula, וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֡ם וַיִּמְצָ֣א אֶת יְהוֹנָדָב֩ (the identical movement verb plus מִשָּׁ֡ם opens 2:25's itinerary stage too), which directly contradicts the frozen row's claim that no departure or arrival formula separates the 10:14 samekh from Jehonadab boarding the chariot. LF's own verification note repeated this same false ground rather than testing it against the text, a real miss rather than OL over-reading the evidence. That said, I find the span itself still holds on the alternative ground OL supplies: Jehu's Samaria destination is announced already at 10:12 (וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיָּבֹ֔א וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמְר֑וֹן) and only consummated at 10:17 (וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן), so the local departure at 10:15 is a station inside that one announced journey, not an independent scene-opener, matching how the itinerary-refrain principle works elsewhere in this book's strategy. Nothing here harms the boundary; only the rejected-alternative's stated ground needs replacing.

challenges.claim: The parenthetical "(10:24-27)" is wrong for one of the three items it gathers. The wardrobe-keeper is לַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ עַל הַמֶּלְתָּחָ֔ה at 10:22, two verses before the cited range opens; only the eighty men (שְׁמֹנִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ, 10:24) and the latrine notice at 10:27 fall inside it.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the range to 10:22-27, or cite the wardrobe-keeper separately at 10:22.

challenges.claim: 10:28 is said to name "the completed object of destruction in a way none of the preceding notices do". The unit just before it closes וַ֠יַּךְ אֶת כָּל הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֧ים לְאַחְאָ֛ב בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן עַד הִשְׁמִיד֑וֹ (10:17) — the same hiphil root over an explicitly named object — so the asserted uniqueness does not hold in the form stated.
challenges.suggested_action: Recast the distinctive of 10:28 formally: a summary wayyiqtol taking אֶת הַבַּ֖עַל with the ablative מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל, a national scope absent from 10:17, rather than claiming no preceding notice names its object.

The rejected alternative correctly names the adversative pivot at 10:29 as the real edge rather than presenting a straw man.

challenges.claim: The row asserts that the members at 10:29, 10:30, 10:31 and 10:32-33 "carry no independent tier-1 openers of their own". Two of them do. 10:32 begins בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם, a fronted temporal frame occurring three times in this book (10:32; 15:37; 20:1), byte-identical at all three and opening a fresh episode in the latter two; and 10:30 begins with the divine-speech formula וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל יֵה֗וּא, which the book strategy's own matrix lists as a unit-opening device.

challenges.claim: 10:36 is called "the standard reign-length notice". challenges.suggested_action: Describe 10:36 as a postponed, book-unique reign-length notice standing after the death formula — a description that, if anything, strengthens the closing edge.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row is honest about carrying the softest edge in the cluster: the adversative opening רַ֠ק חֲטָאֵ֞י יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן נְבָט֙ at 10:29 is a real but weaker pivot than a dated accession or messenger formula, and the closing reign-length notice וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ יֵהוּא֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶֽה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן at 10:36 is the standard framework closer for the book. Both the samekh at 10:29 and the petuchah at 10:36 match pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly and are correctly treated as corroboration rather than drivers of the boundary.

Every quantified claim in this row survives an independent search. בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם occurs at exactly three places in 2Kgs -- 10:32, 15:37, 20:1 -- byte-identical and verse-initial at all three, and the two later ones do open fresh episodes; the consonantal sequence behind וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ returns 10:36 alone, while 13:1 (שְׁבַ֥ע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה) and 13:10 (שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה) confirm that reign length ordinarily sits inside the accession synchronism, so "postponed and book-unique" is earned rather than asserted. The 10:30 rebuttal also holds against the strategy as written: the matrix's opening class is the commission/messenger formula, and וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל יֵה֗וּא is unmediated divine address rather than a dispatch. Both marks (samekh 10:29, pe 10:36) match the single witness, are labelled two-sided, and drive nothing; רַ֠ק heads 10:29, 10:36 is quoted whole, and I found no repair damage anywhere in the row.

Both OL items are cured. The row no longer asserts a blanket absence of openers inside 10:29-33: it now concedes 10:32's בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם as a genuine opener candidate elsewhere in the book and gives a named reason it is held to the evaluation here (no closing formula intervenes before 10:34-36 closes the whole reign), while separating 10:30's unmediated divine address from that opener class -- I checked this against book_strategy_draft.md's own literary_form_decision_matrix, whose 'Commission/messenger formula' row lists 9:1-3, 1:3, 1:15, 19:20, 21:10, and 22:15-17 but not 10:30, supporting the distinction drawn. Separately, 10:36 is now called a book-unique postponed reign-length notice rather than 'the standard' one; I ran my own consonantal-text grep across all 718 verses of 2Kgs_oshb.txt and confirmed וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ occurs exactly once, at 10:36. I also confirmed בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם is byte-identical (first two words) across all three of its occurrences (10:32, 15:37, 20:1) by direct substring comparison, and that the twenty-eight-year reign figure matches. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's core catch on 10:32 is confirmed by my own book-wide grep: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם recurs byte-identical only at 15:37 and 20:1, and the book strategy's over_split_risk_check itself treats 20:1 as opening a fresh unit (the illness/sign complex), so the frozen row's blanket claim that none of 10:29-33's members carries an independent tier-1 opener overstates the case for 10:32 specifically. The reign-length claim at 10:36 is independently confirmed unique in the book — the nominal construction וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ appears only here, against the synchronism-embedded pattern at 3:1, 13:1, and 13:10 — which if anything strengthens the closing edge as OL argues. challenges.suggested_action: Argue the 11:16/11:17 seam explicitly. The available counter favours the row: וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת at 11:17 answers וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם בְּרִ֜ית at 11:4, forming a covenant inclusio around the coup day.

challenges.claim: The row has the unit closing "on the rest formula" וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח כָּל עַם הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהָעִ֣יר שָׁקָ֑טָה, but that clause is mid-verse: 11:20 ends וְאֶת עֲתַלְיָ֛הוּ הֵמִ֥יתוּ בַחֶ֖רֶב (final word ketiv/qere), recapitulating the execution already narrated at וַתּוּמַ֖ת שָֽׁם in 11:16, and the cited samekh follows that tail rather than the rest clause. The same passage also tags Hebrew at 11:4 and 11:20 with web: instead of oshb: refs.
challenges.suggested_action: Quote 11:20 through its end and treat the resumptive execution notice as the closing move; re-tag the two inline Hebrew citations to oshb:.

primary_reviews.rationale: Verse 11:4 opens on a stacked date-plus-commission formula (the dated dispatch of Jehoiada and the covenant-making), and 11:20 closes on the rest formula וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח כָּל עַם הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהָעִ֣יר שָׁקָ֑טָה, both verified verbatim against OSHB. The three internal samekh marks at 11:12, 11:14, and 11:16 all match pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly and are correctly read as marking internal turns of one coup-day scene rather than independent seams.

The row now confronts the seam it had ducked, and it does so on forms that are where it places them: וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע opens oshb:2Kgs.11.17 at position 0, and the covenant it is said to answer, וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם בְּרִ֜ית, sits inside oshb:2Kgs.11.4, so the inclusio argument is checkable rather than asserted. The far edge is quoted through to the verse end, closing on בֵּ֥ית מלך הַמֶּֽלֶךְ with the ketiv/qere on the final word, and the two Hebrew citations formerly tagged web: now read oshb:2Kgs.11.4 and oshb:2Kgs.11.20. Each samekh invoked -- 11:12, 11:14, 11:16 and the outer-edge one after 11:20 -- is present in pmarks_2Kgs.json, is labelled single-witness, and is used to punctuate rather than to decide.

Both OL-030 challenges are cured: the row now confronts the 11:16/11:17 seam directly, arguing the covenant inclusio in which 11:17's oath-cutting answers 11:4's rather than rejecting only the weaker guard-muster split, and the closing quote now runs through the full end of 11:20 (the recapitulated, ketiv/qere-marked execution clause) with oshb: tags replacing the prior web: tags. Every quoted string collates byte-for-byte against 2Kgs_oshb.txt, and the four samekh marks cited (11:12, 11:14, 11:16, 11:20) all match pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly, each framed as corroboration rather than as the reason for the seam. No new defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL correctly flags that the row's rejected-alternative section engages only the weakest competing split (the guard-movement turns) and never tests the sharper seam at 11:16/11:17, where 11:17 opens וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע אֶֽת הַבְּרִ֗ית and 11:18 shifts both subject and site to וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ כָל עַם֩ הָאָ֨רֶץ בֵּית הַבַּ֜עַל; working that seam through, however, only reinforces the row, since וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת at 11:17 answers וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם בְּרִ֜ית at 11:4 in a covenant inclusio that argues for unity, not a split. OL's second point is also right that 11:20 continues past וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח כָּל עַם הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהָעִ֣יר שָׁקָ֑טָה into a recapitulated execution clause echoing 11:16's וַתּוּמַ֖ת שָֽׁם — but OL's own quotation stops one clause short: the verse's true final words are בֵּ֥ית מלך הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (a ketiv/qere pair), not בַחֶ֖רֶב as the parenthetical 'final word ketiv/qere' implies. Both challenges are substantively right about what the frozen prose leaves out, and both share the same web:/oshb: mislabeling already found in row 029. None of this disturbs the 11:4-11:20 span; if anything the coup-day scene's unity is better argued once the 11:17 inclusio is on record.

primary_reviews.rationale: Each offset pair here is right by arithmetic and confirmed by pulling both witnesses at the seam: WEB 11:21 = MT 12:1 (בֶּן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים), WEB 12:1 = MT 12:2 synchronism, WEB 12:2 = MT 12:3 evaluation, WEB 12:3 = MT 12:4 caveat, WEB 12:4 = MT 12:5 speech opener. challenges.claim: The one-verse alternative is dismissed as "divided only by WEB's verse count, not by any Hebrew formula break", with no disclosure that the WLC keys a petuchah to MT 12:1 = WEB 11:21 (single-witness, weak) at exactly the point where that alternative would cut — which is also why MT 12:1 stands as a one-clause verse. A parashah is not a formula, so the literal wording survives, but at confidence "high" the row reads as though the Hebrew side offers nothing at that seam.
challenges.suggested_action: Disclose the pe at MT 12:1 as weak single-witness corroboration of the rejected reading, keep the tier-1 ground (no accession formula restarts at MT 12:2) as the reason for rejecting it, and re-test whether "high" holds once the contrary mark is stated.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every dual-citation in this offset-zone row checks out: WEB 11:21 equals MT 12:1 through WEB 12:4 equals MT 12:5, confirmed both arithmetically against web_mt_crosswalk.json and by content against 2Kgs_oshb.txt. The age-clause בֶּן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּמָלְכֽוֹ opens the standard regnal-formula package (age, synchronism, reign length, mother, evaluation, high-places caveat), and the direct-speech frame וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹאָ֜שׁ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים at WEB 12:4 (MT 12:5) is a genuine discourse opener for the next row.

The disclosure that was asked for is present and correctly weighted: the pe keyed to MT 12:1 appears in both the rationale and the rejected alternative, is tagged single-witness, and is said to favour the reading the row declines rather than to drive anything. What the repair leaves standing is a tier-1 ground that the Hebrew of the very verse it names contradicts -- oshb:2Kgs.12.2 opens בִּשְׁנַת שֶׁ֤בַע לְיֵהוּא֙ מָלַ֣ךְ יְהוֹאָ֔שׁ, the same bishnat-plus-malak accession pattern the book runs at 14:1 (מָלַ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ), 15:1, 15:32 and 16:1 -- while the row's own preceding clause calls that verse 'the accession synchronism'. Positively, the age-clause בֶּן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּמָלְכֽוֹ is byte-exact and is the whole of MT 12:1, and all four Hebrew citations carry their paired WEB=MT slots exactly as web_mt_crosswalk.json requires inside the book's sole fork.

challenges.claim: The stated tier-1 ground, 'no accession formula reopens at MT 12:2' (repeated as 'no accession formula restarts at MT 12:2' in the rejected alternative), is falsified by the verse it names: oshb:2Kgs.12.2 reads בִּשְׁנַת שֶׁ֤בַע לְיֵהוּא֙ מָלַ֣ךְ יְהוֹאָ֔שׁ, which is precisely the book's recurring accession formula, identical in type to oshb:2Kgs.14.1 מָלַ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ, 15:1, 15:32 and 16:1. The row also calls MT 12:2 'the accession synchronism' two clauses earlier, so the sentence contradicts itself, and it is the ground on which the 'high' grade is expressly rested.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate the ground as continuity of one accession complex rather than absence of a formula -- e.g. 'the synchronism at MT 12:2 completes the same Jehoash accession begun by the age-clause at MT 12:1; no second king's accession opens there' -- which preserves the tier-1 reasoning and the 'high' grade without asserting a negative the Hebrew refutes.

primary_reviews.rationale: The single OL-031 challenge is cured: the pe at MT 12:1 (= WEB 11:21) is now disclosed in both the boundary_rationale and the strongest_rejected_alternative as weak single-witness corroboration for the one-verse split, with the tier-1 ground -- no accession formula restarts at MT 12:2 -- stated plainly as the actual reason confidence is retained at high. All five dual-cited Hebrew quotes collate byte-for-byte against 2Kgs_oshb.txt at their stated MT slots, and the mark type (petuchah, not samekh) matches pmarks_2Kgs.json. No new defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's factual claim checks out against pmarks_2Kgs.json: a pe is keyed to 2Kgs.12.1 (MT) = WEB 11:21, exactly the seam where the one-verse alternative would cut, and this row's evidence_refs list discloses no mark at all, unlike its neighboring rows in the cluster. The omission is real, but I do not find it enough to move confidence off 'high': under m8-mesh-r2 marks are weak, non-driving corroboration in either direction, and the row's actual ground for rejecting the one-verse split — that no accession formula reopens at MT 12:2 — is untouched by the mark's presence. The needed fix is additive disclosure, not a confidence downgrade: the pe belongs in the reference list as weak corroboration of the reading being set aside. The boundary itself is sound; only the evidentiary bookkeeping was incomplete.

Disclosing rather than suppressing that tension, and setting confidence at medium_low, matches the flagged low-confidence region of the book strategy for this exact span.

Both single-witness marks are on the record now and they pull in opposite directions, which is what the challenge asked for: pmarks_2Kgs.json keys a PE to MT 12:6, i.e. exactly the WEB 12:5|12:6 seam the rejected two-row reading would use, and a second PE to MT 12:17, the row's own close. Every Hebrew citation in this offset-zone row trails its paired MT number as the opening sentence promises, and its three runs collate byte-identical.

The single OL-032 challenge is cured: the row now discloses both single-witness pe marks symmetrically -- the one at MT 12:6 favoring the rejected two-row split and the one at MT 12:17 corroborating the accepted close -- rather than showing only the inconvenient half. What stands immediately before is the nominal-fronted כֶּ֤סֶף אָשָׁם֙ וְכֶ֣סֶף חַטָּא֔וֹת of MT 12:17 closing the repair procedure, so the az clause really does restart the event chain; my own scan gives verse-initial אָ֣ז at only MT 12:18, 14:8, 15:16 and 16:5, with three clause-internal instances (5:3, 8:22, 13:19), a distribution that fits a marked pivot rather than a connective. Inside the span MT 12:19 simply continues in wayyiqtol (וַיִּקַּ֞ח יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ) with no further seam, and the subject of the withdrawal clause is rightly taken to be Hazael. No mark is claimed anywhere here, although a petuchah does in fact stand at MT 12:17, so the near edge has weak-tier corroboration the row did not need to invoke.

The dual-cite arithmetic and content both check out across the offset seam: WEB 12:17-19 line up with oshb 12:18-20 verse-for-verse. Concretely, oshb 12:19 (=web 12:18) reads “וַיִּקַּ֞ח יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֵ֣ת כָּל הַקֳּדָשִׁ֡ים אֲשֶׁר הִקְדִּ֣ישׁוּ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט וִיהוֹרָם֩ וַאֲחַזְיָ֨הוּ אֲבֹתָ֜יו מַלְכֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ וְאֶת קֳדָשָׁ֔יו וְאֵ֣ת כָּל הַזָּהָ֗ב הַנִּמְצָ֛א בְּאֹצְר֥וֹת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח לַֽחֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם וַיַּ֖עַל מֵעַ֥ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם”, matching the row's gloss 'went away from Jerusalem' against WEB's own wording of that verse, and confirming the pivot from the repair account to the external campaign. The row correctly stops before the source-citation opener that begins the next verse, which belongs to the following row.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Independent collation of MT 12:18-12:20 against WEB 12:17-12:19 confirms the +1 offset by content, not just arithmetic: אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֗ה חֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם at MT 12:18 genuinely restarts the narrative once the repair-fund notice closes at MT 12:17, and the citation opener at MT 12:20 belongs to the next row, not this one. Neither primary raised a challenge here, and my own reading turns up nothing further to add beyond the petuchah OL noted at MT 12:17, which offers only the weak-tier corroboration the mesh rules allow for a near edge. Boundary and prose both hold without qualification.

The petuchah listed at MT 12:22 is registered as PE in pmarks_2Kgs.json, is dual-cited, carries the single-witness tag and does no argumentative work in the prose. Syntax supports the near edge: MT 12:20 opens waw-plus-noun (וְיֶ֛תֶר), a clause type distinct from the wayyiqtol chain of 12:19, and the next unit opens outside the offset with בִּשְׁנַ֨ת at 13:1, which the row correctly cites without an MT tag. One sentence overreaches, promoting the source-citation formula to the marker of every reign's end.

challenges.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative calls the source-citation formula 'the standalone convention marking every reign's end throughout this framework'. My own book-wide search of 2Kgs_oshb.txt for the consonantal string יתר דברי returns 22 verses (1:18, 8:23, 10:34, 12:20, 13:8, 13:12, 14:15, 14:18, 14:28, 15:6, 15:11, 15:15, 15:21, 15:26, 15:31, 15:36, 16:19, 20:20, 21:17, 21:25, 23:28, 24:5) and none at all for at least seven reigns in this book: Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah (opened at 8:25 בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה and killed at 9:27, וַאֲחַזְיָ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ רָאָ֔ה וַיָּ֕נָס, with no citation formula anywhere between), Athaliah (11:1 וַֽעֲתַלְיָה֙ אֵ֣ם אֲחַזְיָ֔הוּ), Hoshea (17:4), Jehoahaz of Judah (23:31), Jehoiachin (24:8) and Zedekiah (24:18). The formula is the dominant convention, not a universal one, and the sentence as written is falsified by the book itself.
challenges.suggested_action: Qualify the quantifier - for instance 'the standing closing marker for the framework reigns' - or reuse the wording already adopted in the neighbouring tribute row ('this book's standing closing-unit marker'), which makes the same point without asserting universality.

primary_reviews.rationale: Confirmed WEB 12:21's 'Jozacar the son of Shimeath' against oshb 12:22's first assassin name -- a genuine name variant, correctly disclosed with the (MT) tag exactly where the campaign brief flags it. The conspiracy-assassination-succession run (oshb 12:20-22) is the book's standing reign-closing convention (the strategy's own device matrix lists 'WEB 12:20-21' as a sample instance of that device), so no internal seam is missed within this row.

I re-ran the softened quantifier instead of accepting it: a consonantal sweep of 2Kgs_oshb.txt for the citation formula returns exactly 22 verses, and sorting those by their closing register (kings of Judah / kings of Israel) against the book's narrated accessions leaves precisely seven reigns uncited -- Joram of Israel and Hoshea in the north, Ahaziah, Athaliah, Jehoahaz, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah in the south -- so both the count and the three reigns the row names now hold, and 'recurring, not universal' is the right description. The name variant is genuine on both sides: 2Kgs_web_clean.txt reads 'Jozacar the son of Shimeath' at WEB 12:21 while oshb:2Kgs.12.22 opens וְיוֹזָבָ֣ד בֶּן שִׁ֠מְעָת, and keeping it visible is the correct handling. The opening citation וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹאָ֖שׁ is byte-exact and constitutes all of oshb:2Kgs.12.20, and the WEB=MT pairings across 12:19-12:21 match web_mt_crosswalk.json through the last offset verse.

The single OL-034 challenge is cured: the strongest_rejected_alternative no longer calls the source-citation formula the universal marker of every reign's end, instead conceding it is 'this framework's recurring, not universal, closing marker' and naming three of the seven uncited reigns. An independent consonantal grep of the citation formula across 2Kgs_oshb.txt returns exactly 22 hits, matching the row's own figure. The MT name variant at 12:22 (WEB 'Jozacar' vs MT's Yozabad spelling) is confirmed against both 2Kgs_oshb.txt and 2Kgs_web_clean.txt, and all quoted Hebrew collates byte-for-byte against source. No new defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The name-variant disclosure and the offset-tail arithmetic both check out against oshb 12:20-22, leaving OL's single challenge to the closing sentence's overreach as the only live matter. My own grep across 2Kgs_oshb.txt for the citation-formula opener (matching lines like וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹרָ֖ם at 8:23) returns exactly 22 hits running from 1:18 to 24:5, and checking reign boundaries confirms the formula is absent for Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah, Athaliah, Hoshea, Jehoahaz of Judah, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah -- so the sentence's claim that this marks 'every reign's end throughout this framework' does not survive the count. The boundary itself is untouched, since the formula still correctly opens this row's near edge; only the sweeping generalization in the rejected-alternative sentence needs qualifying.

primary_reviews.rationale: The synchronism at 13:1, the citation formula at 13:8 and the paired death-and-succession clauses at 13:9 all re-matched exactly; the numbering statement is right, since the crosswalk aligns WEB 13:1-25:30 with MT one-to-one, so single citations suffice from here. The petuchah assigned to 13:9 is in the mark file with that type and its role is stated as weak extra support, and the WEB parentheses are named only in order to be discounted as layout - both correct handling. The grammatical description of the interior is what fails: 13:6 contains no wayyiqtol whatsoever, opening אַ֠ךְ לֹֽא סָ֜רוּ מֵחַטֹּ֧אות בֵּית יָרָבְעָ֛ם and closing וְגַם֙ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה עָמְדָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן, while 13:7 runs on causal כִּ֣י לֹא֩ הִשְׁאִ֨יר. The wayyiqtol sequence the argument leans on is confined to 13:4 (וַיְחַ֥ל) and 13:5 (וַיִּתֵּ֨ן).

challenges.claim: Both the rationale ('a plain wayyiqtol deliverance sequence (13:4-6)') and the rejected alternative ('its verbs are ordinary narrative wayyiqtols continuing the Jehoahaz frame') misdescribe 13:6, which has no wayyiqtol in it: אַ֠ךְ לֹֽא סָ֜רוּ מֵחַטֹּ֧אות בֵּית יָרָבְעָ֛ם is restrictive adverb plus negative plus qatal, בָּ֣הּ הָלָ֑ךְ is a fronted prepositional phrase plus qatal, and וְגַם֙ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה עָמְדָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן is waw plus gam plus fronted subject plus qatal, i.e. a disjunctive nominal-fronted clause. 13:7 is likewise non-narrative, opening כִּ֣י לֹא֩ הִשְׁאִ֨יר. Only 13:4 and 13:5 carry the wayyiqtol chain on which the decision to keep the passage interior is rested.
challenges.suggested_action: Limit the wayyiqtol description to 13:4-5 and re-argue 13:6-7 as narrator's evaluative and causal asides inside the reign frame; that reading in fact strengthens the decision, since asides of this type open no units elsewhere in the framework.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening and closing tier-1 edges hold up: 13:1's accession synchronism and the 13:8-9 source-citation-plus-death pair (itself one of the device matrix's own listed samples of that combination). But the row misdescribes the WEB parenthetical range it cites to argue against splitting off the deliverance material.

challenges.claim: The row states 'a plain wayyiqtol deliverance sequence (13:4-6) that WEB sets off with parentheses,' but in 2Kgs_web_clean.txt the parenthesis opens at v.5 ('(Yahweh gave Israel a savior, so that they went out...') and closes at the end of v.6 ('...the Asherah also remained in Samaria.)') -- v.4 ('Jehoahaz begged Yahweh...') is not inside the parenthetical at all.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the cited range to 13:5-6 (treating v.4 separately as the un-parenthesized petition clause); this does not change the boundary, since per m8-mesh-r2 WEB paragraph/parenthetical marks are metadata only -- only the accuracy of the supporting description needs fixing.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both cures land on the text. The verbal-form correction is exact -- וַיְחַ֥ל and וַיִּתֵּ֨ן stand at position 0 of oshb:2Kgs.13.4 and 13:5, 13:6 opens אַ֠ךְ לֹֽא סָ֜רוּ (restrictive particle, negative, qatal) and closes on the waw-gam disjunctive, and 13:7 opens כִּ֣י לֹא֩ הִשְׁאִ֨יר -- so confining the wayyiqtol chain to 13:4-5 is now accurate; and 2Kgs_web_clean.txt does open its parenthesis at v.5 ('(Yahweh gave Israel a savior') and close it at the end of v.6 ('remained in Samaria.)'), the 13:5-6 range the row now states and flags as layout. What the repair did not carry over from its sibling rows is witness discipline: two Hebrew quotations here are tagged to WEB alone.

challenges.claim: Two Hebrew quotations are sourced to the English witness: the synchronism running to מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָחָ֨ז is tagged '(web:2Kgs.13.1)' and the closing pair ending וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו is tagged '(web:2Kgs.13.9)', with no oshb: slot in either. This is the same defect cured at M8-2Kgs-029 and M8-2Kgs-030, left standing here because ch.13 needs no offset pairing -- the verse numbers are sound, but the Masoretic text is credited to WEB, and the cluster is now internally inconsistent about it.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-tag the two inline Hebrew citations to oshb:2Kgs.13.1 and oshb:2Kgs.13.9, and add a plain 'oshb:2Kgs.13.9' to boundary_evidence_refs, which currently carries that verse only in its pe-qualified form.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both the LF-035 and OL-035 challenges are cured: the wayyiqtol chain is now explicitly confined to 13:4-5, 13:6 is re-described as a restrictive-particle-plus-qatal clause closing on a disjunctive fronted-subject clause, and 13:7 is labeled causal -- all matching the actual verb forms in the source -- and the WEB parenthetical range is now stated as 13:5-6 only. Direct inspection of 2Kgs_web_clean.txt confirms the parenthesis opens at v.5 and closes at the end of v.6, with v.4 outside it entirely. All seven Hebrew quotes in the row collate byte-for-byte against 2Kgs_oshb.txt. No new defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both primaries caught separate defects in the same sentence describing the 13:4-6 deliverance material, and both hold up. 2Kgs_web_clean.txt shows the WEB parenthesis actually opening at v.5 ('Yahweh gave Israel a savior') and closing at the end of v.6, with v.4 sitting outside it entirely, exactly as LF states. Independently, oshb 13:6 (אַ֠ךְ לֹֽא סָ֜רוּ מֵחַטֹּ֧אות בֵּית יָרָבְעָ֛ם ... וְגַם֙ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה עָמְדָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן) carries no wayyiqtol at all, so OL is correct that only 13:4-5 supply the wayyiqtol chain the row leans on. Neither defect reaches the tier-1 edges -- the 13:1 synchronism and the 13:8-9 closing pair remain solid -- so the span is safe even though the interior grammar description needs both corrections applied together.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every quoted string matched, including the atypical succession wording וְיָרָבְעָ֖ם יָשַׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְא֑וֹ, which the row reproduces without pretending it is the ordinary וימלך ... בנו תחתיו clause - a pattern my search finds sixteen times in 2Kgs (8:24, 10:35, 12:22, 13:9, 13:24, 14:16, 14:29, 15:7, 15:22, 15:38, 16:20, 19:37, 20:21, 21:18, 21:26, 24:6) but never at 13:13. The petuchah at 13:13 is in the mark file, is called weak backing, and the four-verse reign frame is uncontroversial from the Hebrew, opening בִּשְׁנַ֨ת and giving way at 13:14 to a fronted non-verbal subject, וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה. My objection touches only the argument offered for that far edge, since the same verse keeps the outgoing king on stage.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative states that 13:14 'shifts subject and register to Elisha entirely, severing any shared-name logic for combining them'. MT 13:14 does not sever it: after the fronted opening וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה the verse continues וַיֵּ֨רֶד אֵלָ֜יו יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל, so the very king whose frame closes at 13:13 is the visitor and mourner of the following unit and remains its royal participant through the sign-act. What changes at 13:14 is the topicalised subject of the opening clause and the genre, not the cast.
challenges.suggested_action: Rest the split on the disjunctive fronted-subject clause together with the change of genre, and say plainly that Joash carries over as a participant - a more accurate and still sufficient basis than a claimed total change of protagonist.

primary_reviews.rationale: The accession synchronism at 13:10 and the closing pair at 13:12-13 (again a device-matrix-listed sample) are both confirmed against oshb. The pivot to Elisha at 13:14 is a genuine disjunctive-clause subject change: oshb 13:14 reads “וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה אֶת חָלְי֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָמ֖וּת בּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨רֶד אֵלָ֜יו יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֵּ֤בְךְּ עַל פָּנָיו֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָבִ֣י אָבִ֔י רֶ֥כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּפָרָשָֽׁיו”, opening on a fronted-subject qatal clause rather than continuing the wayyiqtol succession chain, so the row's 'fresh grammatical subject' claim is grammatically accurate, not just topical color.

The cast correction is exact to the character. The fronted clause opening וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה runs from index 0 to index 55 of oshb:2Kgs.13.14, and וַיֵּ֨רֶד אֵלָ֜יו יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל begins at index 56, so 'the narrative resumes' and 're-enters at once' are literally true of the Hebrew, and the seam now rests on the disjunctive opening plus the register shift instead of a claimed exit of Joash from the stage. Pmarks_2Kgs.json confirms the PE trailing 13:13, and the row uses it only as weak, explicitly single-witness support behind the closing pair. The one thing I cannot pass is the witness attribution on this row's two Hebrew citations.

challenges.claim: The synchronism quotation ending בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֤ז is tagged '(web:2Kgs.13.10)' and the closing formula ending יָשַׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְא֑וֹ is tagged '(web:2Kgs.13.13)'; both are Masoretic text credited to the English witness, with no oshb: slot inline. The digest already ruled this class of defect curable at M8-2Kgs-029, where the verse numbers were likewise sound and no offset was involved.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-tag both inline citations to oshb:2Kgs.13.10 and oshb:2Kgs.13.13, and add a plain 'oshb:2Kgs.13.13' to boundary_evidence_refs, which lists that verse only as the pe-qualified entry.

primary_reviews.rationale: The single OL-036 challenge is cured: the row no longer claims 13:14 removes Jehoash from the account; it now states that he re-enters at once as the weeping visitor and rests the seam on the register shift from closing formula to disjunctive sign-act narrative rather than on any claimed exit of the king. All quoted strings, including the two-clause 13:14 citation, collate byte-for-byte against 2Kgs_oshb.txt, and the trailing pe at 13:13 matches pmarks_2Kgs.json. No new defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The accession synchronism and the 13:12-13 closing pair both match oshb cleanly, and the pivot to Elisha at 13:14 is real, leaving only OL's objection to how that pivot gets narrated. Reading the verse in full, וַיֵּ֨רֶד אֵלָ֜יו יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל follows immediately after the fronted Elisha-clause, meaning Jehoash of Israel -- the very king whose reign frame just closed -- carries straight over as the visiting mourner, so the rejected-alternative's claim of a subject shift 'entirely' overstates the Hebrew. This is an argument-precision defect, not a boundary defect: the change of genre from regnal frame to prophetic narrative still justifies the split, and Jehoash's carryover as a participant does not move where the row ends.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both forms of the cry collate and, to the row's credit, it quotes them separately instead of flattening them: 13:14 reads אָבִ֣י אָבִ֔י רֶ֥כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּפָרָשָֽׁיו while 2:12 reads אָבִ֣י אָבִ֗י רֶ֤כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפָ֣רָשָׁ֔יו - one consonantal text, two accentuations - and a consonantal search confirms these are the only two occurrences in 2Kgs, so the career-bracket claim is grounded. The samekh cited for 13:19 is registered as SAMEKH in the mark file and its weakness is stated, and the rebuke does close on an az-plus-qatal and וְעַתָּ֕ה pair, a plausible closural speech-act. The description of what lies across the far edge is where the row goes wrong, and it erases the fact that most tests this boundary.

challenges.claim: 'Verse 20 replaces king and oracle with an anonymous corpse and a raiding band' misstates MT 13:20 twice over. Its first half is וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִישָׁ֖ע וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֑הוּ - the death this row itself announces in its opening verse with אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָמ֖וּת בּ֑וֹ - so the span sets up a death it does not narrate, and the strongest objection to cutting at 13:19|13:20 is left undisclosed. Second, the anonymous man is not in 13:20 at all: he enters at 13:21, וַיַּשְׁלִ֥יכוּ אֶת הָאִ֖ישׁ בְּקֶ֣בֶר אֱלִישָׁ֑ע. Only the Moabite raiders occupy the second half of 13:20.
challenges.suggested_action: Rewrite the far-edge sentence to concede that the first half of 13:20 resolves the illness notice of 13:14, then justify the cut on the closural oracle plus the verse-edge tiling constraint, and point across to the row that carries 13:20 so the tension is visible instead of argued away.

The opening pivot to Hazael's oppression (13:22) and the covenant grounding (13:23) both check out against oshb.

challenges.claim: 'the age and "right but not like David" evaluation (14:2-3) that opens every Judahite reign in this run' is falsified by my own search of the book. The consonantal string כדוד occurs twice only in 2Kgs: positively at 14:3, רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו, and negated at 16:2, וְלֹא עָשָׂ֣ה הַיָּשָׁ֗ר בְּעֵינֵ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֖יו כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו. challenges.suggested_action: State the recurring elements as the age notice plus a הישר בעיני יהוה evaluation, and mark רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו as specific to Amaziah, with its negated counterpart at Ahaz 16:2. The framework argument for holding 14:2-3 inside the row is unaffected.

challenges.claim: The far edge is credited to 'the scene-changing אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים that opens the Beth-shemesh challenge in 14:8 with a fresh messenger-formula subject', but that subject is not fresh. 14:7 already runs on Amaziah as an emphatically fronted independent pronoun, הוּא הִכָּ֨ה אֶת אֱד֤וֹם, and 14:8 merely re-nominalises the same referent. primary_reviews.rationale: The accession-and-evaluation opening (14:1-3), the interior (non-formulaic) amnesty-law citation at 14:6, the etiological 'to this day' close at 14:7, and the messenger formula opening 14:8 (oshb: “אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל יְהוֹאָ֨שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֧ז בֶּן יֵה֛וּא מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכָ֖ה נִתְרָאֶ֥ה פָנִֽים”) are all verified verbatim against WEB and oshb as the genuine next-row seam.

The az repair survives testing too: verse-initial az stands at 12:18, 14:8, 15:16 and 16:5 only, and 14:8's אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ is the sole instance with a suffix conjugation, the other three all prefixed. I tried two ways to break it and could not -- 13:19's אָ֛ז הִכִּ֥יתָ אֶת אֲרָ֖ם is az plus qatal but mid-verse, so the verse-initial scoping stays true, and the withdrawn 'fresh participant' claim is now correctly measured against הוּא הִכָּ֨ה אֶת אֱד֤וֹם at 14:7. The one residual imprecision, that 14:3's own occurrence sits under רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו so calling only 16:2 'negated' is loose, is contained by the row quoting that negation in full two clauses earlier.

Both challenges are cured with more care than the minimum requested. The row no longer claims the David qualifier opens "every Judahite reign": it now isolates the recurring וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה evaluation (quoted verbatim at 15:3 and 15:34) from the Amaziah-specific רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו qualifier, cross-referencing its sole negated counterpart at 16:2 (כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו) and Jehoash's own comparison to Jehoiada at 12:3 (אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹרָ֔הוּ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע הַכֹּהֵֽן) (OL-M8-2Kgs-040-1). And 14:8 is now re-cast explicitly as re-nomination of a continuing subject inside a freshly opened az-scene rather than a new participant, with the az-plus-qatal vs. az-plus-yiqtol contrast against 12:18/15:16/16:5 doing the actual boundary work (OL-M8-2Kgs-040-2). Independent grep confirms both quantified claims exactly: the consonantal string kaf-dalet-vav-dalet occurs in only two verses book-wide (14:3, 16:2), and 14:8 is the sole verse-initial az clause governing a qatal against three yiqtol comparanda. Separately, 14:7 already carries הוּא הִכָּ֨ה אֶת אֱד֤וֹם with Amaziah as its fronted subject, so 14:8's אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ re-nominalizes the same referent rather than introducing a fresh one, though the qatal governed by that אָז clause does distinguish it from the book's other verse-initial אָז clauses (12:18, 15:16, 16:5), which govern yiqtol -- a sturdier basis the row could have used instead. Both corrections concern argument precision only; the chosen edges at 14:1 and 14:7|14:8 remain the right calls.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation is clean for all three quoted strings, and two of the row's grammatical labels survive testing: קֶ֛שֶׁר is a genuine internal object after the finite verb of the same root, and וַיְחִ֨י with the 'after the death of' tail is demonstrably not the accession pattern used elsewhere in this stretch. challenges.claim: The row's internal-seam test is aimed at the wrong verse. The internal-seam test has moved onto the right verse: ה֚וּא בָּנָ֣ה אֶת אֵילַ֔ת is argued explicitly, the six verse-initial hu clauses the row enumerates (14:7, 14:22, 14:25, 15:12, 18:4, 18:8) are exactly the six my own scan returns, and the appendix reading is tied to the verse's own tail אַחֲרֵ֥י שְׁכַֽב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עִם אֲבֹתָֽיו rather than to the pe. challenges.claim: 'a single dependent clause with no opening formula of its own' misdescribes 14:25. The book strategy itself lists 15:12 among the narrator asides tagged 'per the disjunctive-clause standard', so the row's own governing document expects the disjunctive analysis the rationale contradicts.

primary_reviews.rationale: Zechariah's six-month opening 'בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁמֹנֶה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַעֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ ... זְכַרְיָ֨הוּ' (15:8) and the conspiracy 'וַיִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ שַׁלֻּ֣ם בֶּן יָבֵ֔שׁ' (15:10) both check out verbatim. The fulfillment aside 'בְּנֵ֣י רְבִיעִ֔ים יֵשְׁב֥וּ לְךָ֖ עַל כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ... וַֽיְהִי כֵֽן' at 15:12 is backward-closing in grammar (completing what 15:10 already narrated), which is the stronger reading against the rejected alternative of attaching it forward to Shallum's reign.

The disjunctive analysis now matches the Hebrew: ה֣וּא דְבַר יְהוָ֗ה is a verbless clause with fronted pronoun, it stands after the already-sealed citation וְיֶ֖תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י זְכַרְיָ֑ה, and the row cites 15:11 and restates the relation as termination rather than grammatical completion -- the inversion the challenge identified is gone. וַֽיְהִי כֵֽן closing the four-generation promise, and the pe at MT 15:12 handled as weak single-witness backing, both check out against the source. The far edge is where the rewrite stays thin: it says 15:13 'opens a wholly new synchronism', but 15:13 opens subject-first with שַׁלּ֤וּם בֶּן יָבֵישׁ֙ מָלַ֔ךְ -- as this cluster's own 046 row insists -- and oshb:2Kgs.15.13 appears nowhere in boundary_evidence_refs, so the seam's tier-1 support is asserted in passing rather than cited or described accurately.

challenges.claim: The closing edge is described as 'before 15:13 opens a wholly new synchronism', but 15:13 begins שַׁלּ֤וּם בֶּן יָבֵישׁ֙ מָלַ֔ךְ -- subject, patronym, then the verb, with the year formula only following -- so it does not open on the synchronism at all; M8-2Kgs-046 in this same cluster builds its own opening argument on precisely that reversal. oshb:2Kgs.15.13 is also absent from boundary_evidence_refs, leaving the far edge's tier-1 signal named only in passing.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate 15:13 as a subject-first accession formula (matching 046's description) and add web:2Kgs.15.13 and oshb:2Kgs.15.13 to boundary_evidence_refs.

primary_reviews.rationale: OL-M8-2Kgs-045-1 is cured close to its own suggested wording: the rationale now quotes ה֣וּא דְבַר יְהוָ֗ה as the disjunctive, verbless, fronted-pronoun opening of the aside and restates the relation correctly -- it "terminates Zechariah's frame as a narrator's appended comment" rather than completing the already-closed citation at 15:11 (וְיֶ֖תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י זְכַרְיָ֑ה הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים). Both halves of 15:12 quoted (the disjunctive opener and the וַֽיְהִי כֵֽן resolution) collate byte-identical to source, and the pe at 15:12 remains correctly demoted to weak corroboration ahead of 15:13's fresh synchronism. peer_crosscheck.assessment: Re-checked the 15:8-12 span: the six-month synchronism, Shallum's conspiracy verb, and the four-generation oracle all quote exactly, and the pe at MT 15:12 is correctly demoted to corroboration. OL's challenge is well-founded: 15:12 opens with ה֣וּא דְבַר יְהוָ֗ה, an independent verbless clause with a fronted-pronoun predicate, coming after 15:11's already-closed source-citation formula — describing it as something that 'grammatically completes' 15:11 inverts the relation, since a disjunctive nominal clause does not finish a formula that has already run to its own close. The book's own device inventory lists 15:12 among fulfillment notices that close their unit, the same practical outcome the row wants, so the frame's boundary at 15:12 survives; what needs rewriting is the grammatical justification, not the verse the row draws the line at.

primary_reviews.rationale: Two of this row's more exposed assertions survive testing, which is worth recording: the subject-first opening at 15:13 is quoted exactly and does reverse the year-first order used at 15:8, 15:17, 15:23 and 15:27, and my own sweep confirms that 15:15 is the only source-citation formula in 2Kgs naming a conspiracy. Mark citations are also correct — SAMEKH at MT 15:15, PE at MT 15:16, both disclosed as single-witness. The reasoning about 15:16 is what fails: אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה is asyndetic and, on the same sweep, every other clause-initial אָ֣ז in the book opens an episode rather than closing one, so the construction cited cannot bind 15:16 backward across the sealed formula הִנָּ֣ם כְּתֻבִ֗ים at 15:15.

challenges.claim: The אָ֣ז argument is deployed in the wrong direction. My own book-wide sweep of 2Kgs finds clause-initial אָ֣ז at four verses only — אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֗ה חֲזָאֵל֙ (12:18), אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ (14:8), אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה (15:16), אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֣ה רְצִ֣ין (16:5) — and at 12:18 and 16:5 it launches a fresh Aramean campaign episode, while at 14:8 decision M8-2Kgs-041 in this same cluster starts its own span on it. The construction is asyndetic: it links to nothing preceding, so it is evidence against attaching 15:16 to a unit that 15:15 has already sealed with הִנָּ֣ם כְּתֻבִ֗ים. The phrase 'the same אָ֣ז' further has no antecedent anywhere in the row, and the nearest אָ֣ז in the cluster (14:8) takes a suffix-conjugation verb, not the prefixed verb the row describes.
challenges.suggested_action: Either (a) restate 15:16 as a free-standing notice bracketed by the samekh at MT 15:15 and the petuchah at MT 15:16 and re-scope the span to 15:13-15, or (b) keep 15:13-16 but replace the אָ֣ז argument with a positive backward-attachment ground (the Tirzah link to 15:14); in either case supply an antecedent for 'the same' and cite oshb:2Kgs.12.18 and oshb:2Kgs.16.5.

challenges.claim: The 'flash-forward appendix' label is unsupported by the row's evidence and the nearest lexical tie runs the other way: 15:16 carries the locative מִתִּרְצָ֔ה, repeating מִתִּרְצָ֗ה from 15:14, where Menahem marches up from Tirzah and strikes Shallum down. The Tiphsah notice therefore attaches most naturally to the march already narrated in 15:14 rather than projecting forward into the reign that begins at 15:17, and the row cites neither 15:14 nor any temporal argument for the forward reading.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop 'flash-forward', or add oshb:2Kgs.15.14 to the refs and argue the temporal relation explicitly from the shared Tirzah datum plus the force of the prefixed verb after אָ֣ז.

primary_reviews.rationale: The subject-first reversal 'שַׁלּ֤וּם בֶּן יָבֵישׁ֙ מָלַ֔ךְ בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְעֻזִיָּ֖ה' at 15:13 is a genuine anomaly: a book-wide check of every accession formula in 2Kgs finds only 15:13 placing the king's name before the year among true accession openers, so the claim is well-founded, not decorative. The az-plus-imperfect construction 'אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה מְ֠נַחֵם אֶת תִּפְסַ֨ח' at 15:16 (the verb form is imperfect, not the ordinary wayyiqtol narrative chain) is grammatically distinct from narrative continuation, supporting the appendix reading. But the row's boundary_evidence_refs cite only 15:13, 15:15, and 15:16 -- omitting 15:14 in full, 'וַיַּעַל֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם בֶּן גָּדִ֜י מִתִּרְצָ֗ה וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיַּ֛ךְ אֶת שַׁלּ֥וּם בֶּן יָבֵ֖ישׁ בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיְמִיתֵ֖הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו', which is the verse narrating Menahem's actual killing of Shallum and succession, lying squarely inside this row's own span and functioning as the event that 15:15's uniquely-worded source-citation ('וְקִשְׁר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר', naming Shallum's own conspiracy) and the 15:16 appendix both presuppose.

challenges.claim: boundary_evidence_refs for M8-2Kgs-046 omit 2Kgs.15.14 even though the verse lies inside the cited span (15:13-15:16) and contains the assassination/succession clause that the row's own argument (why 15:15's source-citation follows, why 15:16 reads as an appendix rather than a fresh reign-opening) depends on.
challenges.suggested_action: Add web:2Kgs.15.14 and oshb:2Kgs.15.14 to boundary_evidence_refs, and state explicitly that 15:14's assassination-succession clause closes Shallum's unit rather than opening Menahem's (consistent with the book strategy's own device matrix, which lists 15:14 among the conspiracy/succession-by-violence formula instances that close a reign).

primary_reviews.rationale: Three repairs verify cleanly: the unanchored 'the same az' is gone, 'flash-forward' is gone, 15:14 is now cited with its role stated, and the Tirzah tie is quoted accent-accurately in both directions -- מִתִּרְצָ֗ה at 15:14 against מִתִּרְצָ֔ה at 15:16, which my collation confirms are distinct byte sequences. The uniqueness claim also survives my own grep: of the 22 source-citation verses in 2Kgs, only 15:15 carries the conspiracy root, וְקִשְׁר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר. Still undisposed is the asyndeton the original challenge was built on: אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה מְ֠נַחֵם opens with no connective, verse-initial az stands at exactly 12:18, 14:8, 15:16 and 16:5, and M8-2Kgs-041 in this very cluster treats the 14:8 instance as a unit opener, yet the row weighs only its two backward ties and never puts that counter-force on the record.

challenges.claim: The revision replaced the az argument with two backward ties but never disposes of the construction's own force: אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה מְ֠נַחֵם is asyndetic, linking to nothing preceding, and on my sweep verse-initial az occurs at 12:18, 14:8, 15:16 and 16:5 only, where 12:18 and 16:5 launch fresh Aramean campaign episodes and 14:8 is used by M8-2Kgs-041 in this same cluster as a unit opener. The row's confidence is medium, yet the strongest counter-signal to backward attachment is left unweighed, and oshb:2Kgs.12.18 and oshb:2Kgs.16.5 -- asked for in either remedy branch of the original challenge -- are still absent from boundary_evidence_refs.
challenges.suggested_action: Add one clause weighing the asyndetic, episode-initial force of verse-initial az against the Tirzah and 15:17 arguments (for instance that 15:16's prefixed verb yields an iterative summary notice rather than the narrative advance seen at 12:18 and 16:5), and cite oshb:2Kgs.12.18 and oshb:2Kgs.16.5 for the comparison set.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three challenges are cured: 15:14 (וַיַּעַל֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם בֶּן גָּדִ֜י מִתִּרְצָ֗ה וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיַּ֛ךְ אֶת שַׁלּ֥וּם בֶּן יָבֵ֖ישׁ...) is now both cited in boundary_evidence_refs and argued explicitly as the assassination-succession clause the row depends on (LF-M8-2Kgs-046-1), independently confirmed against book_strategy_draft.md's own conspiracy/succession-by-violence device-matrix entry, which lists 15:14 as closing a reign unit. The flawed 'same az' backward-attachment argument is replaced with a positive tie between מִתִּרְצָ֗ה (15:14) and מִתִּרְצָ֔ה (15:16) plus the observation that Menahem's own accession formula does not begin until 15:17 (OL-M8-2Kgs-046-1), and the unsupported 'flash-forward appendix' label is dropped in favor of that same Tirzah argument (OL-M8-2Kgs-046-2). Independent checks confirm 15:13's subject-first order genuinely reverses the year-first pattern at 15:8/15:17/15:23/15:27, and that וְקִשְׁר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר (15:15) is a real cognate-accusative naming the conspiracy, unique among this chapter's source citations. Both the samekh at 15:15 and pe at 15:16 match pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly and stay correctly demoted to weak, non-driving corroboration. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Pulled all four clause-initial אז verses straight from oshb — 12:18 (יַעֲלֶ֗ה), 14:8 (שָׁלַ֤ח), 15:16 (יַכֶּֽה), 16:5 (יַעֲלֶ֣ה) — and confirmed 14:8 alone governs a suffix-conjugation (qatal) verb while the other three take the prefix conjugation (yiqtol); I further confirmed 12:18 and 16:5 both precede their own reign's closing source-citation formula (12:20, 16:19), functioning as interior campaign insets inside a still-open frame, whereas 15:16 follows Shallum's own closing formula at 15:15 — a structural difference neither the frozen row nor either primary states outright. This resolves the LF/OL conflict: LF's appendix reading and OL's episode-opening reading are each partly right, and the row's own prose, which cites 'the same אז' with no stated antecedent, is the real defect that OL's book-wide sweep correctly exposes. What actually keeps 15:16 out of Menahem's formal frame is simply that his accession formula does not appear before 15:17, and what ties 15:16 back to Shallum's row is the repeated locative מִתִּרְצָ֗ה / מִתִּרְצָ֔ה linking it to Menahem's march from Tirzah already narrated at 15:14 — a verse both primaries independently flagged as missing from the row's own citations. All three surviving challenges check out, and none requires moving the span: 15:13-16 stays one row, but its supporting prose is the most defective in the cluster and should be rebuilt around 15:14 and the Tirzah linkage rather than the current אז analogy.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quoted strings reproduce exactly, the thirty-ninth-year synchronism the row paraphrases is verifiably present at the head of 15:17, and the close is described with care — the row says 'death-succession pairing', which is right, because 15:22 has no burial verb where 14:16 and 15:7 do. The weakness is the ground on which the Pul inset is kept interior: the row argues only from missing formulas, while 15:19 in fact begins בָּ֣א פ֤וּל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ with no conjunction, breaking a wayyiqtol chain that runs וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע at 15:18 and picks up again at וַיֹּצֵא֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם in 15:20.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative dismisses a separate 15:19-20 row purely on absence of opening and closing formulas, and never confronts the one positive syntactic signal in the passage. 15:19 opens בָּ֣א פ֤וּל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ — a suffix-conjugation clause with no waw whatever — flanked by וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע (15:18) and וַיֹּצֵא֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם (15:20), so the inset is asyndetically detached from the narrative chain on its front edge. That asyndeton is the strongest Hebrew evidence for the inset's independence, and an argument from formula-absence alone leaves the row's confidence of 'high' resting on the weaker of the two available considerations.
challenges.suggested_action: Extend boundary_evidence_refs with oshb:2Kgs.15.18 plus oshb:2Kgs.15.20, name the asyndetic בָּ֣א opening explicitly, and reject the split on the stronger ground that an asyndetic annalistic notice of foreign incursion is a recognised interior device in this book (cf. 15:29) rather than merely on missing formulas.

primary_reviews.rationale: Opening 'מָ֠לַךְ מְנַחֵ֨ם בֶּן גָּדִ֧י עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִ֖ים' at 15:17 and the 15:21-22 close both check out. The Pul notice 'בָּ֣א פ֤וּל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ' (15:19) echoes the book's campaign-opening wording, but the strategy's own device-matrix sample of campaign-muster formulas (3:5-7, 6:24, 17:5, 18:9, 18:13, 24:1, 24:10-11, 25:1) pointedly excludes 15:19, and the notice never develops its own closing formula -- corroborating the row's choice to keep it as an inset rather than splitting it out.

Running the inset argument character by character against MT, the newly named asyndetic opener בָּ֣א פ֤וּל מֶֽלֶךְ stands at offset 0 of 15:19, and the two wayyiqtol anchors the repair added to the refs, וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (15:18) and וַיֹּצֵא֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם (15:20), are verse-initial as well, so the front-edge asyndeton now rests on the text rather than on missing formulas, while the MT 15:22 pe is held back as a merely ‘weakly seconded’ clause exactly as the tier rule requires. The frame edges survive probing too: the 15:17 quotation begins at word 8, but the prose itself discloses the thirty-ninth-year synchronism, and 15:21-22 do supply citation followed by death and succession. The repair nevertheless dragged in a defective comparandum, since the sentence claiming ‘the same construction opens the Tiglath-pileser notice’ quotes 15:29 from its fifth word.

challenges.claim: The 15:29 cross-reference starts the verse in the wrong place. The quoted string בָּא֮ תִּגְלַ֣ת פִּלְאֶסֶר֮ begins at word 4; 15:29 opens בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל. 15:19 is therefore a bare asyndetic verse-initial qatal while 15:29 is an asyndetic fronted temporal phrase governing its qatal, and the two are not ‘the same construction’. Sibling row M8-2Kgs-049 in this same cluster was repaired for exactly this mis-start and now quotes 15:29 from offset 0, so two revised rows describe one verse’s opening in incompatible terms.
challenges.suggested_action: Requote 15:29 from בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל and restate the parallel as shared verse-edge asyndeton rather than an identical construction, or replace the comparandum with a genuinely verse-initial asyndetic qatal.

primary_reviews.rationale: The revision cures OL-M8-2Kgs-047-1 in full: it names the 15:19 asyndeton explicitly, concedes it as a genuine signal worth naming, and rejects the split on the pattern argument (cf. 15:29) rather than resting on formula-absence alone, exactly as the challenge asked. Byte-collation of every 15:17-15:29 quotation against 2Kgs_oshb.txt found no transcription drift, and the sole mark citation (pe at 15:22, MT) matches pmarks_2Kgs.json and is framed as trailing corroboration, never driver. Both edges of the span -- the 15:17 accession synchronism and the 15:21-22 source-citation-plus-death-succession close -- are argued from tier-1 signals independent of that mark. challenges.claim: The rationale locates the frame's bounds at 15:23 and 15:25 and then justifies the span's actual terminus, 15:26, with the single sentence 'weak single-witness corroboration for this edge sits in the pe after MT 15:26' — leaving a parashah mark as the only cited support for that edge, which is the driver role the book strategy forbids ('never driver'). The cure demanded here has landed: the tier-1 close is now quoted in full, וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י standing at offset 0 of 15:26 and הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים ending the citation, while the parashah is explicitly demoted to ‘secondary, single-witness corroboration rather than the sole support’, which strips it of the driver role. primary_reviews.rationale: Every quoted string sits where the row places it: the synchronism of 15:27, the seven-city register of 15:29, Hoshea's קֶ֜שֶׁר at 15:30, each byte-identical under machine collation.
