My objection is to how the interior is described: the register does not begin at the quoted וַיִּקַּ֣ח but at בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בָּא֮, which the row's flat denial of any articulation formula cannot accommodate.

challenges.claim: The rationale says the conquest register lacks 'any accession-type formula that would mark it as separately opened' and the rejected alternative says it 'carries no independent articulation formula'. Both statements start the verse in the wrong place. 15:29 does not open with the quoted wayyiqtol; it opens בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בָּא֮ תִּגְלַ֣ת פִּלְאֶסֶר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֒ — asyndetic, with a fronted temporal PP governing the qatal בָּא֮, and וַיִּקַּ֣ח only resuming after that frame is set. My own book-wide grep of verse-initial temporal and אָ֣ז frames in 2Kgs returns twelve instances (10:32, 12:18, 14:8, 15:16, 15:29, 15:37, 16:5, 16:6, 18:16, 20:1, 20:12, 24:10), several of which demonstrably launch discrete episodes — אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה מְ֠נַחֵם at 15:16, בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת at 20:1. The row's own siblings treat that class as consequential (050 has to argue 15:37 away; 051 concedes אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֣ה at 16:5 as a genuine rival), so the denial here is both inaccurate and internally inconsistent.
challenges.suggested_action: Engage the actual opener: concede that 15:29 carries the book's standard asyndetic temporal-frame articulation (בִּימֵ֞י plus qatal) and rest containment on other grounds — no evaluation, no source citation, subject continuity with Pekah's frame — or reduce confidence from high to medium.

primary_reviews.rationale: Verified the accession synchronism at 15:27 ("בִּשְׁנַ֨ת חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַעֲזַרְיָ֖ה") and the conspiracy-succession close at 15:30 ("וַיִּקְשָׁר קֶ֜שֶׁר הוֹשֵׁ֣עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֗ה עַל פֶּ֨קַח֙") against oshb; both are exact and both edges hold as real tier-1 openers/closers, with 15:32 correctly opening the next row. But the strongest_rejected_alternative tests 15:29 only against a register/catalogue analogy ("the later Jerusalem/Bethel purge catalogue"), not against the writer's own "campaign-muster / siege formula" category, which the matrix applies to structurally identical "in the days of/his days X, Y king of Assyria came up" openers (17:5, 18:9, 18:13, 24:1, 25:1); 15:29's own opener, "בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בָּא֮ תִּגְלַ֣ת פִּלְאֶסֶר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֒", matches that pattern more closely than the register comparison actually tested.

challenges.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative frames 15:29's rival case as a register/catalogue analogy rather than testing it against the book strategy's own literary_form_decision_matrix "Campaign-muster / siege formula" device ("opens a war/siege unit"), which is exemplified by the same "in the days of/his days X, Y came up" construction at 17:5, 18:9, 18:13, 24:1, 25:1. 15:29 opens with בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בָּא֮ תִּגְלַ֣ת פִּלְאֶסֶר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֒, matching that pattern, not the purge-catalogue pattern the row actually argues against.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row’s central repair verifies from the source: 15:29 is now quoted from its head, בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל, at offset 0, so the earlier denial that the register carries any articulation is gone, and every member of the class the row appeals to — 10:32, 15:16, 15:37, 16:5, 20:1 — is on my own check a verse-initial asyndetic temporal frame. I also confirmed the appeal to the strategy against book_strategy_draft.md, whose literary_form_decision_matrix does list 17:5, 18:9, 18:13, 24:1 and 25:1 under ‘Campaign-muster / siege formula’, so that attribution is honest rather than invented. Two smaller descriptions of the same verse do not survive the text: its object chain is mislabelled by kind, and the subject the containment argument names is not the subject the Hebrew supplies.

challenges.claim: ‘The seven-city register’ miscounts by kind. The chain governed by 15:29’s taking-verb has seven direct-object members, but two are territories rather than towns — הַגִּלְעָד֙ and הַגָּלִ֔ילָה — and an eighth captured entity, כֹּ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ נַפְתָּלִ֑י, follows as a summary apposition. Only five members (Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor) are cities.
challenges.suggested_action: Write ‘seven-item conquest register (five towns plus Gilead and Galilee, summarised by כֹּ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ נַפְתָּלִ֑י)’ so the label matches the object chain.

challenges.claim: ‘runs a single verse under Pekah’s continuing subject’ inverts the syntax. The subject of 15:29’s clauses is תִּגְלַ֣ת פִּלְאֶסֶר֮, not Pekah, who stands only inside the temporal frame בִּימֵ֞י פֶּ֣קַח מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל; 15:30’s subject is then Hoshea. If anything the clause-level subject changes at 15:29, which is a datum for the rejected alternative rather than against it. The adjacent phrase about a ‘fresh regnal subject’ not arriving until 15:32 suggests a regnal rather than grammatical sense was intended, but as written the two senses of ‘subject’ collide.
challenges.suggested_action: Say ‘runs a single verse inside Pekah’s regnal frame’, and note separately that the clause subject is the Assyrian king, so clause-subject continuity is not among the grounds for containment.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both prior challenges are cured: the rejected alternative now tests 15:29 against the book strategy's own campaign-muster device, contrasting it with the multi-verse compass of 18:13 and 24:1, rather than the register/catalogue analogy LF-M8-2Kgs-049-1 objected to; and the rationale concedes the asyndetic בִּימֵ֞י...בָּא֮ opener as a genuine fronted-temporal-frame device (attested at 10:32, 15:16, 15:37, 16:5, and 20:1, all verified byte-identical against oshb) instead of denying it carries any articulation, curing OL-M8-2Kgs-049-1. primary_reviews.rationale: Jotham's frame collates cleanly: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְפֶ֥קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֖הוּ stands verse-initial at 15:32, כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֛ה עֻזִיָּ֥הוּ אָבִ֖יו עָשָֽׂה is exact at 15:34, and pmarks does key a PE to MT 15:38. I also tested the comparative remark, and it survives: the consonants כדוד appear in only two verses of this book, 14:3 (רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו) and 16:2, neither belonging to Jotham — though readers should note the qualification is not wholly absent, since רַ֤ק הַבָּמוֹת֙ לֹ֣א סָ֔רוּ follows at 15:35. challenges.claim: The rejected alternative keeps 15:37 interior because it 'is grammatically bound to Jotham's closing sequence'. No such binding exists in the text. בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הֵחֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה לְהַשְׁלִ֨יחַ֙ is asyndetic — there is no waw joining it to 15:36 — and is built as a fronted deictic adverbial plus qatal, a syntactically self-standing clause. Checking the construction across the book shows it opening units rather than continuing them: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הֵחֵ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה לְקַצּ֖וֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל starts the Hazael notice at 10:32 and בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת starts the illness narrative at 20:1. The row also leaves unmentioned that this clause is wedged between the source citation of 15:36 and the burial notice of 15:38, an intrusion into the middle of the closing frame rather than an addition to its end.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'grammatically bound' with an accurate description — asyndetic fronted-PP plus qatal, dependent on context deictically rather than syntactically — and carry the containment argument on the absent accession formula plus the clause's position inside, not after, the closing frame.

primary_reviews.rationale: Confirmed 15:32's synchronism ("בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְפֶ֥קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֖הוּ") and 15:34's evaluation ("כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֛ה עֻזִיָּ֥הוּ אָבִ֖יו עָשָֽׂה") open the row correctly. I independently checked the claim that Jotham's evaluation lacks the "yet not like David" qualifier "found elsewhere in this run": 2Kgs 14:3 does carry it ("רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו", for Amaziah), so the comparison is accurate rather than merely asserted. The 15:37 aside ("בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הֵחֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה") is correctly kept interior since it has no accession or campaign-opening formula of its own, and the death-burial-succession triad at 15:38 genuinely closes the unit.

The syntactic repair is exactly right against the witness: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הֵחֵ֣ל opens 15:37 at offset 0 with no waw, so ‘asyndetic rather than grammatically joined’ properly replaces the old and false binding claim, and the construction really is identical to 10:32’s, the two verses agreeing word for word through the qatal and diverging only in the accent borne by the divine name. The Amaziah contrast checks out as well — לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו כְּכֹ֧ל stands at 14:3 and is absent from 15:34, whose evaluation closes on the comparison with Uzziah instead. What the revised containment argument now leans on, however, is a verse the row never cites, and the same silence covers the qualifier standing one verse before the aside.

challenges.claim: The revised containment argument rests on placement — the aside is ‘wedged between the 15:36 source citation and the 15:38 burial notice’ — yet oshb:2Kgs.15.36 appears nowhere in boundary_evidence_refs, so the load-bearing left bracket (וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹתָ֖ם …) is uncited. The same gap covers 15:35: the row calls 15:34 a positive evaluation lacking Amaziah’s qualifier, while the very next verse opens רַ֤ק הַבָּמוֹת֙ לֹ֣א סָ֔רוּ, a qualification of that evaluation that is neither mentioned nor cited.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:2Kgs.15.36 and oshb:2Kgs.15.35 to boundary_evidence_refs, and concede in the prose that Jotham’s evaluation does carry the high-places qualifier at 15:35, just not the Davidic one attested at 14:3.

primary_reviews.rationale: OL-M8-2Kgs-050-1 is cured cleanly: the false 'grammatically bound' claim is replaced with an accurate asyndetic, fronted-deictic-adverbial-plus-qatal description of 15:37, backed by the same construction opening fresh units at 10:32 and 20:1 (both verified byte-identical), and containment now rests on 15:37's absent accession formula and its position wedged between the 15:36 citation and 15:38 burial notice rather than on a nonexistent syntactic tie. The 14:3/16:2 evaluation-formula contrast this row also leans on is independently confirmed unique to those two verses by a targeted consonantal search of the whole book. No new defect located in this row.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Jotham's frame checks out cleanly: the synchronism at 15:32, the evaluation at 15:34, and the death-burial-succession triad at 15:38 all match the source exactly, and I independently confirmed the 'found elsewhere in this run' David-qualifier claim against 14:3's רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו, so the uncontested part of the rationale is sound. OL's single challenge lands, though: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הֵחֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה carries no waw at all, so calling it 'grammatically bound' to the closing sequence misdescribes an asyndetic fronted-adverbial-plus-qatal clause that opens fresh episodes elsewhere at the identical phrase בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם in 10:32 and 20:1. Containment nonetheless survives on grounds OL itself supplies: no accession formula attaches to 15:37, and the clause sits wedged between the 15:36 citation and the 15:38 burial notice rather than trailing after the closed frame. The span is unaffected; only the grammatical characterization needs repair.

primary_reviews.rationale: Ahaz's accession line, his negative evaluation, the אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֣ה campaign notice and the Damascus resolution reproduce the pointing of 16:1, 16:2, 16:5 and 16:9 without deviation, and אָ֣ז does stand verse-initial at 16:5 as implied. I put the superlative to a book-wide test as well: וְלֹא עָשָׂ֣ה הַיָּשָׁ֗ר occurs exactly once in 2Kgs, at 16:2, so 'the starkest form' is safe even beyond the scope claimed. The defect lies elsewhere — a seam inside the span that the row never brings up at all, while carrying the span at high confidence.

challenges.claim: 16:6 is a Hebrew-visible seam inside the span and is nowhere argued. It reads בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֤ם אֶת אֵילַת֙ לַֽאֲרָ֔ם: asyndetic, a fronted temporal adverbial governing the qatal הֵ֠שִׁיב, a change of theatre from Jerusalem to Elath, and a terminal etiological tag עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה that closes notices elsewhere in this book rather than continuing them. That is the same articulation class the row itself grants standing to at 16:5, and its rejected alternative weighs only the 16:5 cut while passing over 16:6 in silence. As weak single-witness corroboration only, pmarks_2Kgs.json also keys a PE to MT 16:6 — the sole parashah break in chapter 16 before 16:20 — so the strongest internal division in the span is both syntactically marked and unaddressed.
challenges.suggested_action: Argue 16:6 explicitly, for instance as an Elath parenthesis syntactically detached but narratively subordinate to the same Aramean crisis, or re-cut with the syntax of 16:6 as driver and the MT 16:6 pe cited only as corroboration; if the single span stands, lower confidence from high to medium.

primary_reviews.rationale: The accession synchronism at 16:1 ("בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַֽע עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְפֶ֖קַח") and negative evaluation at 16:2 ("וְלֹא עָשָׂ֣ה הַיָּשָׁ֗ר בְּעֵינֵ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֖יו כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו") both check out verbatim, and 16:9's resolution ("וַֽיִּתְפְּשֶׂ֔הָ וַיַּגְלֶ֖הָ קִ֑ירָה וְאֶת רְצִ֖ין הֵמִֽית") genuinely closes the unit before 16:10's fresh journey clause. But the row never mentions 2Kgs 16:6, which carries a pe mark (pmarks_2Kgs.json: "2Kgs.16.6":"PE", MT, single-witness) landing on the "to this day" refrain the book strategy itself names at this exact verse; the aside there, "בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין...עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה", is structurally the same kind of temporal-clause narrator's note as 15:37, which decision 050 explicitly argues down one row earlier -- but 051 is silent on its own parallel case.

challenges.claim: 16:6 (בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֤ם אֶת אֵילַת֙ לַֽאֲרָ֔ם...וַיֵּ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה) carries a pe mark (pmarks_2Kgs.json, MT numbering, single-witness) and is one of the book strategy's own named "to this day" etiological-refrain occurrences (frontier_or_atlas_candidate_expectations: "2:22, 8:22, 10:27, 14:7, 16:6, 17:23, 17:34, 17:41"), yet neither boundary_rationale nor boundary_evidence_refs mention it, unlike the parallel aside at 15:37 which decision 050 explicitly engages and dismisses.
challenges.suggested_action: Add a sentence disposing of 16:6 the way 050 disposes of 15:37 -- note that "בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא" introduces a background aside with no accession or campaign opener of its own, so its pe mark is weak corroboration of an internal narrator's note rather than a seam -- so the reasoning is on record instead of silent.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both outstanding demands on this row are met from the Hebrew. 16:6 is now argued rather than passed over: its opener בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב is quoted from offset 0, its tag עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה verifies as verse-final, its MT 16:6 pe is disclosed as single-witness and weak while the rejected alternative weighs it openly, and confidence is duly stepped down to medium. I re-ran the row’s universal instead of trusting it — a consonantal sweep of 2Kgs for the negated ‘did what was right’ formula returns 16:2 and nothing else — so ‘a form found nowhere else in the book’ stands on my grep as well as the author’s. Residual damage: the Elath aside is described only as far as its first half, and one verb-form label lands on the wrong verse.

challenges.claim: ‘its actor Rezin is already on scene from 16:5’ holds for 16:6a only. From word 13 the verse installs a wholly new plural subject and closes the notice with it, וַֽאֲדוֹמִים֙ בָּ֣אוּ אֵילַ֔ת וַיֵּ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֔ם, and that subject carries a ketiv/qere the row does not disclose — ketiv וארמים (Arameans) against qere וַֽאֲדוֹמִים֙ (Edomites) — which changes who occupies Elath ‘to this day’. Since participant continuity is the ground on which the row keeps 16:6 subordinate, a mid-verse change of subject plus an undisclosed witness variant is material. Relatedly, 16:7-8, where the Assyrian rescue named in this row’s own literature_type_guess is requested and paid for (וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אָחָ֜ז …), appear in neither the prose nor boundary_evidence_refs.
challenges.suggested_action: Extend the 16:6 sentence to cover 16:6b’s new plural subject, disclose the ketiv/qere with both readings, and add oshb:2Kgs.16.7 and oshb:2Kgs.16.8 so the rescue narrative the row is named for is actually cited.

challenges.claim: ‘on the same asyndetic fronted-temporal-plus-qatal pattern’ takes its nearest antecedent from 16:5, but 16:5’s verb is not a qatal: the verse opens אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֣ה, adverb plus prefix conjugation. Only 16:6’s הֵ֠שִׁיב is a suffix-conjugation form, so the label is transferred from the verse that has it to the verse that does not.
challenges.suggested_action: Disambiguate the antecedent, for instance ‘on the fronted-temporal-adverbial pattern of 15:37, here with a qatal where 16:5 has אָ֣ז plus a yiqtol’, so the two verb forms stay distinct.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the cluster's strongest repair: the HIGH-severity OL-M8-2Kgs-051-1 finding that 16:6 was a Hebrew-visible, pe-marked seam left wholly unargued is now met head-on -- 16:6 is quoted, its asyndeton and theatre-shift to Elath are conceded as a genuine candidate, its pe is cited and correctly matches pmarks_2Kgs.json, and confidence is stepped down from high to medium exactly as the challenge invited, subsuming LF-M8-2Kgs-051-1's simpler ask in the same fix. One imprecision survives the repair, though: the clause describing 16:6 as shifting theatre 'on the same asyndetic fronted-temporal-plus-qatal pattern' sits directly against the quoted 16:5 clause, whose verb יַעֲלֶ֣ה is an imperfect (yiqtol), not a qatal like 16:6's הֵ֠שִׁיב, so the 'same pattern' wording either misdescribes 16:5's verb form or needs to state plainly that it compares 16:6 to the qatal-class parallels (15:37, 10:32, 20:1) rather than to 16:5 itself.

challenges.claim: The sentence 'shifts theatre to Elath on the same asyndetic fronted-temporal-plus-qatal pattern' follows immediately after quoting 16:5's אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲ֠רָם, but יַעֲלֶ֣ה is a Qal imperfect (yiqtol), not a qatal; 16:6's own verb הֵ֠שִׁיב is the qatal. As written, the clause reads as claiming 16:5 and 16:6 share a fronted-temporal-plus-qatal shape, which is true only of 16:6 and of the book's other cited comparanda (15:37, 10:32, 20:1), not of 16:5.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword to make clear the comparison is between 16:6 and the qatal-class parallels elsewhere in the book (15:37, 10:32, 20:1), not between 16:6 and 16:5's own אָז-plus-imperfect construction -- e.g. 'shifts theatre to Elath on the same asyndetic fronted-temporal-plus-qatal pattern seen at 15:37, 10:32, and 20:1' -- so the verb-form label is not implicitly applied to 16:5 as well.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Pulled 16:1-9 whole against oshb as instructed: the accession synchronism, negative evaluation, אָ֣ז campaign notice at 16:5, and Damascus resolution at 16:9 all match verbatim, and the row is right that וְלֹא עָשָׂ֣ה הַיָּשָׁ֗ר... כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו occurs nowhere else in the book. Both primaries flag the same silence - LF at medium severity, OL at high: 16:6 (בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין... עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה) is an asyndetic temporal-frame clause of the same class the row already concedes at 16:5, it shifts theatre from the Jerusalem siege to Elath, it closes with the book's 'to this day' tag (confirmed on the strategy document's own list at 2:22/8:22/10:27/14:7/16:6/17:23/17:34/17:41), and pmarks_2Kgs.json keys the chapter's only mid-span PE to 16:6 alone between 15:38 and 16:20 - yet none of this appears in boundary_rationale or boundary_evidence_refs. My own re-derivation agrees the omission is real: the row cannot rest at high confidence while ignoring its own strongest internal candidate. Ruling: the span itself survives intact - 16:6 remains a one-verse, actor-continuous aside about Rezin's Elath campaign with no evaluation, source-citation, or accession formula of its own, so it does not clear the bar for its own row - but CONFIDENCE must drop from high to medium until boundary_rationale explicitly disposes of 16:6 the way it disposes of 16:5, disclosing the pe as weak corroboration rather than omitting it.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three anchors reproduce the source exactly — the journey and commission clauses of 16:10, Uriah's compliance at 16:16, and 16:18, which does terminate on מִפְּנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר as stated. Syntactically the opener is an unmarked wayyiqtol, so the seam rides on participant change rather than clause type, and the medium confidence assigned here reflects that honestly. Two descriptive claims inside the row nevertheless collapse when the neighbouring verses are collated.

challenges.claim: The commission half of the 'scene-opening pair with no parallel earlier in the frame' has a close parallel four verses earlier, inside Ahaz's own frame. 16:7 reads וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אָחָ֜ז מַלְאָכִ֗ים אֶל תִּ֠גְלַת פְּלֶ֤סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ — the identical sending frame, with the same verb, the same royal subject and the same אֶל plus addressee, as 16:10's וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶל אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן, and it is directed at the very Assyrian king whom 16:10 then goes out to meet. The 'no parallel' assertion is therefore unavailable as support for separate row-hood.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the 'no parallel' assertion or narrow it to the journey half (לִ֠קְרַאת plus royal audience), which does lack an earlier counterpart, and let participant novelty (Uriah, the altar pattern) carry the argument.

challenges.claim: The row reads 16:16 as the compliance that 'answers the commission' of 16:10, but the verbal correspondences cross that pairing. The sending commission of 16:10 is discharged already at 16:11 — וַיִּ֛בֶן אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז מִדַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק כֵּ֤ן עָשָׂה֙ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֔ן — while 16:16's כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָחָֽז answers the distinct order issued at 16:15, וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ אָ֠חָז אֶת אוּרִיָּ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן לֵאמֹ֗ר. There are two pairs in the span, each matched by its own verb of sending or of commanding, not one; relatedly, the compliance formula is not confined to this annal, since 11:9 has וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֞וּ שָׂרֵ֣י … כְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה֮ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵן֒.
challenges.suggested_action: State the doubled commission-compliance structure (16:10 to 16:11, then 16:15 to 16:16), which if anything strengthens the row, and either delete 'absent elsewhere in the annal' or scope it explicitly to Ahaz's frame given 11:9.

primary_reviews.rationale: Confirmed the journey-and-commission opener at 16:10 ("וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֡ז לִ֠קְרַאת תִּגְלַ֨ת פִּלְאֶ֤סֶר" ... "וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶל אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֶת דְּמ֧וּת הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ") introduces both a new participant (Uriah) and a fresh location exactly as claimed, and the compliance formula at 16:16 ("וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֑ן כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָחָֽז") answers it. The medium-confidence disclosure is honest given the strategy names "one continuous 16:1-20 row" as a live alternative, and no internal mark or competing opener sits between 16:10 and 16:18 that the row overlooks.

Every substantive repair here verifies. challenges.claim: In ‘where 16:10 supplies the explicit royal title … that 16:7’s bare … omits’, the two cited words are given accentless and are therefore not substrings of the verses they are attributed to: 16:10 reads הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ at word 15, and 16:7 reads אָחָ֜ז at word 1. challenges.suggested_action: Replace the two accentless forms with the pointed and accented forms as they stand in 16:10 and 16:7, or mark them explicitly as unpointed lexical citations the way the row already marks its root citation.

challenges.claim: 'the pe at MT 16:20 closes both this row and the book's next reign' misdescribes what that mark delimits. pmarks_2Kgs.json keys one PE to 2Kgs.16.20 and a separate PE to 2Kgs.17.6; the next reign in the book is Hoshea's, which begins at 17:1 with מָ֠לַךְ הוֹשֵׁ֨עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֧ה and is closed by the latter mark, not the former. primary_reviews.rationale: The accession slot at 17:1, עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה at 17:3, וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן at 17:5 and the deportation clause of 17:6 all reproduce the source without a character's difference, and the PE is correctly keyed to MT 17:6 and correctly flagged. The absence of a closing formula also checks out, since 17:7 proceeds directly to וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי rather than to a citation. Two evidentiary supports fail, however: the row's tally of the escalation verb and its claim about how reigns are launched in this book.

challenges.claim: 'The root עלה … drives the escalation twice' undercounts by half. Across 17:3-5 the root carries four finite verbs: עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה at 17:3; the negated hiphil at 17:4, וְלֹא הֶעֱלָ֥ה מִנְחָ֛ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר, which is the pivot of the whole notice; and two wayyiqtols inside 17:5 alone, וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ followed by וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן. The undercount matters because the rejected alternative leans on 'the repeated עלה chain linking 17:3 and 17:5' precisely while omitting the 17:4 occurrence that lies in the conspiracy verse the alternative wants to separate.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the tally to four occurrences across 17:3-5 and route the rejection through 17:4's הֶעֱלָ֥ה, which supplies the very link the proposed split would have to sever.

challenges.claim: 'the same launching formula every reign in Kings uses' is a universal claim, and my own survey of accession openers in this book falsifies it. Seven Judahite reigns launch with an age-at-accession clause carrying no synchronism and no accession-verb slot at all: בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (21:1), בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (22:1), בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (24:18), and likewise 21:19, 23:31, 23:36 and 24:8. Hezekiah's is launched differently again, by a waw-consecutive: וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁלֹ֔שׁ לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֖ה (18:1). The synchronism-plus-qatal pattern generalized here belongs to the dual-monarchy stretch only, and ends when the northern kingdom does.
challenges.suggested_action: Restrict the claim to the synchronized reigns of the dual-monarchy sequence (roughly 13:1 through 17:1) or delete the universal and cite the immediate parallels 15:27 and 15:32 instead.

primary_reviews.rationale: The regnal opening at 17:1 ("מָ֠לַךְ הוֹשֵׁ֨עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֧ה") and deportation close at 17:6 ("וַיֶּ֥גֶל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַשּׁ֑וּרָה") both check out, and the observation that no death-burial-succession formula follows -- because the kingdom itself ends -- is a correct, well-argued reading of the gap before 17:7's homily. But the Leitwort claim undercounts: "עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה" in 17:3 pairs a preposition (עָלָיו, "against him") with the actual root-עלה verb (עָלָה), not two occurrences of the root, and 17:5 itself contains the root twice ("וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן"), so the true count across 17:3+17:5 is three verb occurrences, and the row's own quote silently skips the first "וַיַּ֥עַל" of v.5.

challenges.claim: "The root עלה (\"went up\") drives the escalation twice -- עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה in 17:3 and וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן in 17:5" misstates the count: עָלָיו in 17:3 is the preposition על plus 3ms suffix ("against him"), not a second token of the root עלה -- only עָלָה in that pair is the verb -- and 17:5 already contains the root twice (וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן), giving three total verb occurrences across 17:3 and 17:5, not two, with the row's own quote omitting the first, וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise to either count all three occurrences of the verb עלה (17:3, and both in 17:5) or reframe the claim as a paronomasia between עָלָיו and עָלָה rather than a shared root, so the philological label matches the text.

primary_reviews.rationale: The philological corrections asked of this row are confirmed by my own morphological pass over 17:3-5, which returns exactly four finite verbs of the ascent root — עָלָ֔ה in 17:3, מִנְחָ֛ה in 17:4, and the two wayyiqtols opening 17:5 (וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ …) — against two prepositional forms, עָלָ֣יו in 17:3 and שָׁלֹ֥שׁ in 17:5, so both the tally of four and the parenthetical disclaimer about the preposition hold. The retreat from the earlier book-wide universal also survives independent testing: my sweep confirms that 21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8 and 24:18 each open on a bare age-at-accession clause carrying no synchronism, and that 18:1 alone launches with a waw-consecutive. Two items remain — one verse the strategy assigns unit-opening force and never gets disposed of, and a mis-identification of which accession is the immediate one. The accentless citation forms in the 17:3 parenthesis are recorded in the collation tally.

challenges.claim: 17:5 is named by book_strategy_draft.md’s literary_form_decision_matrix under ‘Campaign-muster / siege formula’ (3:5-7, 6:24, 17:5, 18:9, 18:13, 24:1, 24:10-11, 25:1) with the stated effect ‘Opens a war/siege unit’, yet this row swallows 17:5 mid-span and its strongest_rejected_alternative tests only a split at 17:4. The omission is sharpened by sibling row M8-2Kgs-049, which leans on that same matrix entry, 17:5 included, to keep 15:29 embedded. On the Hebrew the containment is defensible — 17:5’s וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ continues the wayyiqtol chain under the subject already installed at 17:4, with neither asyndeton nor fronting — but that argument is nowhere made.
challenges.suggested_action: Add a sentence disposing of 17:5 as a named campaign-muster: unlike 18:13 or 25:1 it opens with a plain wayyiqtol under an unchanged subject, so the matrix device is present here without its unit-opening force.

challenges.claim: ‘the immediately preceding notices at 15:27 and 15:32’ skips the actually immediate one. My sweep of verse-initial בִּשְׁנַת֙ accession openers in 2Kgs runs … 15:27, 15:32, 16:1, 17:1, and 16:1 carries the identical shape, בִּשְׁנַת֙ … מָלַ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז. 16:1 is this cluster’s own row M8-2Kgs-051, which quotes that very synchronism, so the nearest parallel to 17:1 is passed over in favour of two more distant ones.
challenges.suggested_action: Add 16:1 to the parallel list and to boundary_evidence_refs, or drop ‘immediately preceding’ and describe 15:27, 15:32 and 16:1 together as the surrounding synchronized run.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three original challenges are cured with precision: the עלה tally now stands at four occurrences across 17:3-5 (עָלָה at 17:3, הֶעֱלָ֥ה at 17:4, and the two wayyiqtols of 17:5), each verb form correctly labeled and byte-verified against oshb, satisfying both LF-M8-2Kgs-054-1 and OL-M8-2Kgs-054-1; the rejected alternative now routes containment through 17:4's הֶעֱלָ֥ה as the latter challenge required; and the 'every reign in Kings' universal is replaced with a claim scoped to the dual-monarchy stretch, with all seven bare age-at-accession Judahite openers (21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18) and Hezekiah's waw-consecutive 18:1 opener confirmed verbatim against source, curing OL-M8-2Kgs-054-2. This is the cluster's most heavily revised row and it now reads as the cleanest: no miscount, mislabel, or refs gap survives.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The accession slot, the deportation close, and the pe at 17:6 all check out, and the 'no closing formula because the kingdom itself ends' reading holds against 17:7's immediate pivot to וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי. Both primaries challenge the עלה tally, and reconciling them matters: LF is right that עָלָיו in 17:3 is the preposition על plus suffix, not a second root-token, but LF's own corrected total of three still misses 17:4's וְלֹא הֶעֱלָ֥ה מִנְחָ֛ה (Hiphil, 'did not pay tribute'), which OL catches - the accurate count across 17:3-5 is four finite occurrences of the root, not two and not three. OL's second challenge also lands: I independently confirmed seven Judahite reigns (21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18) open on a bare age-at-accession clause with no synchronism at all, and Hezekiah's own reign at 18:1 opens with a waw-consecutive rather than the bare synchronism-plus-מלך pattern generalized here, so 'the same launching formula every reign in Kings uses' is a false universal that should be scoped to the dual-monarchy stretch. Neither correction touches the 17:1-6 boundary itself.

challenges.claim: 'the governing כי launched at 17:7 is not answered until the עד אשר of 17:23' is contradicted three verses earlier. 17:20 already ends on עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁלִיכָ֖ם מִפָּנָֽיו, the same subordinator carrying the same expulsion sense, so 17:23 supplies the second such clause and not the first. challenges.claim: The rejected alternative defeats the 17:18-20 cut by asserting that 'the removal verb the whole indictment has been building toward only arrives four verses later, at 17:23'. The verb arrives before the alleged digression rather than after it: 17:18 already has וַיְסִרֵ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו, the identical hiphil with the identical מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו complement that recurs in 17:23's עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁר הֵסִ֨יר יְהוָ֤ה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֔יו. The argument therefore depends on a distribution the Hebrew does not have, and as it happens the true distribution would have served better.
challenges.suggested_action: Substitute the accurate observation that 17:23 resumes the removal formula first stated at 17:18 across the intervening Judah material, which keeps the block whole on evidence that can be checked.

challenges.claim: 17:19 is labelled 'disjunctive in form'. challenges.suggested_action: Relabel as asyndetic and subject-fronted under גַּם focus; the containment conclusion is unaffected.

challenges.suggested_action: Correct the rebuttal to cite the 17:18/17:23 verbal echo as a Wiederaufnahme (the matrix's own continuity-signal category) bracketing the Judah notice -- that is a stronger basis for keeping the span unified than the "delayed verb" claim currently made.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both members of the resumption sit exactly where the repair places them: 17:18 supplies וַיְסִרֵ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו, 17:23 opens עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁר הֵסִ֨יר יְהוָ֤ה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֔יו, one Hiphil wayyiqtol and one Hiphil qatal of the same root sharing the same complement, so the discarded "verb only arrives at 17:23" distribution is genuinely gone and the accentual difference on the noun (atnach against zaqef qatan) is the sole residue. The interior joints collate clean as well -- 17:20 does end on עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁלִיכָ֖ם מִפָּנָֽיו, 17:21 does open verse-initially on כִּֽי קָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל, and 17:19's גַּם יְהוּדָ֕ה לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר carries no waw at all, curing the waw-disjunctive mislabel -- while the pe at MT 17:23 stays in the weak tier the strategy assigns it. I confirmed both strings byte-for-byte against oshb; the corrected reading is a Wiederaufnahme - 17:23 resumes the verb first fired at 17:18 across the intervening Judah material of 17:19-22 - rather than a first arrival, and this is a stronger, checkable basis for keeping the block unified than the delayed-verb claim it replaces. OL's two further challenges also survive: 17:20 already closes on its own עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁלִיכָ֖ם מִפָּנָֽיו and 17:21 opens a fresh כי clause (כִּֽי קָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל), so 'one unbroken dependency from 17:7 to 17:23' oversimplifies a passage with several nested causal clauses; and 17:19's גַּם יְהוּדָ֕ה לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר carries no waw at all, making 'disjunctive' the wrong label for what is an asyndetic, גַּם-fronted clause. None of these corrections moves the span's edges - they strengthen the case for unity rather than weaken it, so the boundary is not harmed, only the rebuttal prose surrounding it.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both quoted clauses of 17:41 are verbatim (וַיִּהְי֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה יְרֵאִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה; גַּם בְּנֵיהֶ֣ם וּבְנֵ֣י בְנֵיהֶ֗ם), and the generational-scope claim holds -- no earlier verse in the chapter states a three-generation continuity. challenges.claim: Two grammatical assertions fail. (a) “A single grammatical subject chain ... carries the evaluation and revolt notice through 18:8”, and the alternative's “unbroken subject chain begun in 18:3”, ignore 18:7, which opens by handing the subject to Yahweh — וְהָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ — before וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד בְּמֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר returns it to Hezekiah. challenges.suggested_action: Call 18:13 a regnal-year date formula (fourteenth year of Hezekiah) and reserve “accession” for the synchronism at 18:1.

challenges.claim: 18:17 is called “a muster formula”, but the clause is a dispatch: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֡וּר with three named officers, the arrival being supplied only by the following וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם. No mustering verb (qbts, 'sp, pqd) occurs in the verse, and the mislabel is visible inside this same cluster: M8-2Kgs-063 calls the identical verse “An embassy-arrival formula”.
challenges.suggested_action: Harmonise the label with 063 — a sending-and-arrival formula introducing new envoys — and reserve “muster” for the campaign-muster verses the book strategy lists.

primary_reviews.rationale: 18:13's fourteenth-year Sennacherib synchronism and the 18:16 temple-door-stripping close both quote verbatim, and the 18:16 petuchah is confirmed in pmarks_2Kgs.json. The rejected alternative's quoted phrase (תַּרְתָּ֥ן וְאֶת רַב סָרִ֣יס וְאֶת רַב שָׁקֵ֨ה) matches 18:17 exactly, and the underlying claim -- that wholly new envoy-participants open the next scene -- is correct and sufficient to hold this notice apart from the embassy that follows.

Both cures land and neither brings new damage. 18:13's date is named for what it is, the regnal-year formula וּבְאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗ה, with accession reserved for 18:1, and the actor contrast is accurate against 18:9's עָלָ֞ה שַׁלְמַנְאֶ֧סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֛וּר. The muster label is retired on evidence I re-ran rather than assumed: a consonantal scan of 18:17 finds no qbts, 'sp or pqd anywhere in the verse, only וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֡וּר with arrival supplied by וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם, exactly as the revised prose states. The right edge בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא קִצַּ֨ץ חִזְקִיָּ֜ה is verse-initial at 18:16, where pmarks_2Kgs.json does record a PE, disclosed as single-witness.

Both OL-062-1 and OL-062-2 are cured. The row now calls 18:13 a "regnal-year date formula" and explicitly reserves "accession" for 18:1's synchronism, and it relabels 18:17 a "dispatch-and-arrival formula" rather than a muster, correctly noting no mustering verb occurs in the verse -- confirmed against the Hebrew, which has only send/go-up/come verbs there, and against the book strategy's own campaign-muster list, which does not include 18:17. No new defects found: the silver-and-gold figures and temple-door detail match 18:14-16, and the petuchah at 18:16 checks out against pmarks_2Kgs.json as single-witness corroboration, not a driver.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both terminology objections from OL check out on inspection. 18:13's date, וּבְאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗ה, counts Hezekiah's fourteenth regnal year, not his accession -- the actual accession synchronism sits at 18:1 -- so calling 18:13 an 'accession-year date' collides with the row that already claims that label for 18:1. Separately, 18:17 opens with a dispatch verb (וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֡וּר) and only reaches Jerusalem via a following arrival clause; no mustering verb appears anywhere in the verse, and the mislabel is visible within this same cluster, since row M8-2Kgs-063 correctly calls the identical verse an 'embassy-arrival formula.' Neither fix touches where the tribute notice starts or stops -- the fourteenth-year date and the temple-door-stripping close with its petuchah are unaffected by either correction -- so the frozen boundary stands and only the two labels need replacing.

primary_reviews.rationale: The hinge is verified as printed: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ heads 19:1 with a temporal infinitival clause that binds the scene to the report just delivered at the end of 18:37, and the oracle's final clause at 19:7 matches character for character. I probed the one internal seam candidate the Hebrew offers, וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל יְשַֽׁעַיָֽהוּ at 19:5, an arrival clause of the type the book strategy elsewhere treats as unit-opening; because the delegation's speech is already quoted at 19:3-4, that arrival is resumptive repetition and articulates rather than divides. The forward edge is equally clean, וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה at 19:8 abandoning the temple-and-prophet stage for Libnah, and this row cites no parashah mark at all.

19:1's hearing-hinge (וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ) and 19:7's deliverance-oracle close (וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ) both quote verbatim, and the claimed scene shift from the wall to the temple to Isaiah is accurate. The row correctly identifies 19:8's return to Rabshakeh's itinerary and the Libnah location shift as the true edge, and does not split at 19:5's resumptive 'so the servants ... came to Isaiah,' which is properly read as a Wiederaufnahme after the quoted message rather than a fresh seam.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: No challenge items exist against this row from either primary, and the underlying quotes hold up unassisted. The 19:1 hearing-hinge (וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ) and the 19:7 oracle-closing clause (וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ) both match oshb byte for byte, and the 19:5 arrival of Hezekiah's servants at Isaiah (וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל יְשַֽׁעַיָֽהוּ) is rightly treated as resumptive repetition rather than a hidden seam, since the delegation's message is already quoted at 19:3-4. primary_reviews.rationale: Machine collation places all three quoted strings exactly where the row puts them: וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ heads 19:8 as a wayyiqtol with full re-nomination of רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה at a new front, and אַיּ֤וֹ stands verse-initially in 19:13. The welding of 19:10 to 19:9 that the row asserts is genuine, but it is carried by the terminal לֵאמֹֽר of 19:9, a form the rationale never cites, and 19:10 does begin with a formula, כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן, the same messenger-speech opener (accents apart) as כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן in 19:6. challenges.claim: The only parashah datum in boundary_evidence_refs is the pe keyed to MT 19:14. Marks follow their keyed verse, so that pe divides after 19:14 (between וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ ... וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ and the prayer opening 19:15), not at the 19:13|19:14 seam this row closes on; if it bears at all it groups 19:14 with the preceding embassy material and argues for a 19:8-14 span. Row M8-2Kgs-066 in this same cluster reads the mark exactly that way and discloses the tension, while this row lists it silently, where it reads as corroboration it cannot supply.
challenges.suggested_action: Either drop oshb:2Kgs.19.14 (petuchah, single-witness) from boundary_evidence_refs, or retain it with an explicit sentence stating that the mark stands one verse later, is single-witness and weak, and is read against here on the same ground row 066 gives.

challenges.claim: 'no formula separates the two verses' is inaccurate as written: 19:10 opens with כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן, a messenger-speech formula standing also at 19:6 as כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן and, in the shorter variant, at 22:18 as כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּ. challenges.suggested_action: Cite לֵאמֹֽר at the end of 19:9 as the subordinating form and restate the point as 'no new commission or arrival verb intervenes' (the wording already used correctly in strongest_rejected_alternative) instead of denying that any formula stands at 19:10.

primary_reviews.rationale: The return-formula וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה ... נִלְחָ֖ם עַל לִבְנָ֑ה (19:8) and the renewed dispatch וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ (19:9) both check out against OSHB, and 19:10's כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן content genuinely carries no independent sending verb of its own, so the row's single-scene reading of the embassy holds. The close at 19:13's rhetorical questions and the participant shift making Hezekiah the acting subject at 19:14 are both confirmed, matching the letter-frame device the book strategy assigns to this span.

Both OL items are discharged against the consonantal text. 19:9 really does end in לֵאמֹֽר and 19:10 really does open כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן, so the revised concession that a messenger-speech formula stands at 19:10 while subordination rides on the verse-final infinitive matches the line word for word; the flat denial the digest objected to is gone. The pe is now named as keyed to MT 19:14, one verse beyond the 19:13|19:14 seam, and is read against on the same ground row 066 gives from the far side, which pmarks corroborates (PE at 2Kgs.19.14, nothing at 19:13). New-damage probes found nothing: וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה is genuinely verse-initial, and all six Hebrew runs in the row collate character-for-character with oshb.

Both original items are cured: the rationale now names 19:10's opening koh-tomerun as a genuine recurring messenger-speech formula (matching 19:6) and correctly locates the subordinating device in 19:9's own closing le'mor, and it now discloses the MT 19:14 pe explicitly as sitting one verse past this row's close, single-witness, and read against rather than silently listed as favorable corroboration. Every Hebrew string quoted (19:6, 19:8, 19:9, 19:10, 19:13) collates byte-identical against 2Kgs_oshb.txt, boundary_evidence_refs covers exactly the verses the prose argues, and both edges (the 19:8 return-formula opener, the 19:13 close before Hezekiah's action at 19:14) rest on tier-1 signals with the mark demoted to disclosed non-driving corroboration.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Re-derivation confirms both anchor formulas -- the return-verb chain in 19:8-9 (וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה ... וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ) and the rhetorical-question close in 19:13 (אַיּ֤וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ חֲמָת֙ ...) -- quote OSHB exactly, and the deeper claim that 19:10 carries no independent commission verb is sound, since Hezekiah's messengers were already dispatched in 19:9 and 19:10 is subordinated by that verse's own terminal לֵאמֹֽר. Both OL challenges survive independent testing. Pmarks_2Kgs.json keys the sole PE cited in this row's evidence list to 19:14, which per the mark-follows-verse convention divides after that verse, not at the 19:13|19:14 seam this row actually closes on, and sibling row 066 discloses that exact tension while this row cites the mark silently. The phrase 'no formula separates the two verses' also overclaims: 19:10 opens with כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן, the identical messenger-introduction device found at 19:6 (כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן) and 22:18 (כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּ), confirmed by my own book-wide check, so a formula genuinely stands there even though it opens no new commission. Neither correction moves the span; 19:8-13 remains right, and the fix in both cases is documentation, not boundary.

primary_reviews.rationale: Hezekiah governs every finite verb from 19:14 into the prayer (וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ ... וַיַּ֨עַל֙ ... וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ, then וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל in 19:15), so the syntactic tie the row prefers over the mark is real. challenges.claim: The rationale calls לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה a 'repeated' phrase, yet that pointed string occurs once in the pair: 19:14 ends לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה while 19:15 reads לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮. challenges.suggested_action: Quote both variants ('לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה in 19:14, לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ in 19:15') and say the phrase recurs with the accentuation expected at verse end versus mid-verse, rather than presenting one pointed form as repeated.

primary_reviews.rationale: Hezekiah's act of spreading the letter לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (19:14) and the prayer's own opening לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ (19:15) repeat verbatim in OSHB, giving real textual warrant for binding 19:14 forward to the prayer rather than back to the embassy. The row is transparent that the petuchah at 19:14 (confirmed PE in pmarks_2Kgs.json) points the other way, and treating that single-witness mark as weak corroboration rather than a driver is exactly what the m8-mesh-r2 rule requires.

The pointed-form overstatement is cured: the row now prints לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה and לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ side by side and calls them one consonantal phrase under different cantillation, which the witness bears out — the first is verse-final in 19:14, the second stands third in 19:15. The inclusio also survives collation, אַתָּה ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ mid-19:15 answered by the verse-final כִּ֥י אַתָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ. The repair's added closing sentence is where new damage entered: it seats the prayer's close on the petition וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נוּ נָ֖א מִיָּד֑וֹ, which is the opening clause of 19:19, one sentence after the row has already said the recognition clause closes that same verse.

challenges.claim: The row states twice, incompatibly, what closes 19:19. It first cites כִּ֥י אַתָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ as 'closing 19:19' (correct: that clause is verse-final), then writes 'The prayer closes on its own petition, וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נוּ נָ֖א מִיָּד֑וֹ (19:19), where a setumah ... corroborates'. The petition is the first clause of 19:19, not its last, so the mark keyed to 19:19 does not sit at the petition at all; it sits after the recognition clause the row itself quoted.
challenges.suggested_action: Restate the second sentence as 'the prayer runs from its petition וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נוּ נָ֖א מִיָּד֑וֹ at the head of 19:19 to the recognition clause that closes it, where the setumah (single-witness) corroborates', so both statements about the verse's close agree and the mark is placed where it actually stands.

primary_reviews.rationale: The sole original item -- the overstated 'repeated' claim for the lifnei-YHWH phrase -- is cured exactly as suggested: the rationale now quotes both pointed variants (19:14's end-of-verse form versus 19:15's mid-verse form) and describes them as 'recurring rather than repeating identically.' The inclusio bracketing 19:15/19:19 (the 'you alone are God/YHWH' framing) collates byte-identical to source and remains the genuine tier-1 signal fixing the far edge, with both the 19:14 petuchah and 19:19 setumah correctly disclosed as single-witness corroboration subordinate to that inclusio and to the subject-chain/lifnei-YHWH link at the near edge.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Hezekiah's unbroken subject-chain across 19:14-15 (וַיַּ֨עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה ... וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל) checks out against OSHB and genuinely outweighs the petuchah at 19:14, which this row -- unlike 065 -- discloses and reasons past correctly. OL's single challenge survives verification: the pointed form לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה closing 19:14 and לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ opening the prayer in 19:15 are not byte-identical strings, differing in cantillation, so calling the phrase 'repeated' overstates a link that is real consonantally but not as an exact quoted form; my own targeted search confirms each pointed variant occurs exactly once in the book. Independently I located an inclusio neither primary cites -- 19:15's אַתָּה ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ answered by 19:19's אַתָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ -- which would have strengthened the same argument on firmer ground. The 19:14-19 span and its medium confidence stand; only the word 'repeated' needs qualifying.

primary_reviews.rationale: Verse-initial position holds for both frames the row leans on, וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ heading 19:20 and זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר heading 19:21, and the pair בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ is genuine synonymous parallelism rendered with the correct 3fs subject. Hebrew syntax nevertheless makes בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן the subject of those two qatals, not the party addressed; the addressee is the suffix of לְךָ֜, whom the row itself names as the Assyrian king two clauses later. Sweeping 19:22-28 for a competing addressee turned up none (חֵרַ֨פְתָּ֙ in 19:22, שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ in 19:25, וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ in 19:27 are all 2ms), so the span survives even where its account of the address does not.

challenges.claim: 'the taunt proper addressed to בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן' misassigns the syntax. In 19:21 the sequence runs בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן: the two 3fs qatals take בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן as their SUBJECT and the 2ms לְךָ֜ as the one spoken against, so Zion mocks the Assyrian rather than being addressed. The row contradicts itself three clauses later with 'The taunt's second-person address to the Assyrian king', and the mislabel matters because the adjacent row M8-2Kgs-068 rests its boundary on an addressee change out of this taunt.
challenges.suggested_action: Reword to 'the taunt proper, spoken against the Assyrian king (the 2ms לְךָ֜) with בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן as its grammatical subject', which leaves the elevated-register argument intact.

primary_reviews.rationale: The commission formula at 19:20 and the nested 'this is the word' tag at 19:21 both quote OSHB accurately, and I confirmed the taunt's second-person address (e.g. 19:27-28's 'your sitting down ... your raging against me') never breaks until 19:29's addressee shift. The WEB text runs 19:20 into 19:21 with no paragraph mark between them, so the row's claim that register, not layout, carries the taunt's start is correct on inspection.

The syntactic mislabel is properly repaired: בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן is now read with the two 3fs qatals taking Zion as subject and the 2ms suffix as the party spoken against, and the row no longer contradicts itself three clauses later. The 2ms chain it now traces is real in every verse cited — חֵרַ֨פְתָּ֙ (19:22), שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ (19:25), וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ (19:27) — and 19:20's commission formula is verse-initial while 19:21's tag is not preceded by any second sending verb. What the repair did not reconcile is the closing sentence, which relocates the addressee shift onto 19:29's sign formula; the sibling row 068, revised in the same round, denies exactly that on morphological grounds.

challenges.claim: 'Both addressee and genre shift only at 19:29's distinct sign formula' locates the addressee shift in the wrong clause. The sign formula is וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת, whose לְּךָ֣ is the same 2ms suffix carried through 19:21-28; the shift is visible only in that verse's later 2mp imperatives זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ. Row M8-2Kgs-068 in this same revised cluster states precisely this ('cannot itself carry the addressee shift'), so as written the two rows disagree about the same clause.
challenges.suggested_action: Attribute the shift to 19:29's plural imperatives rather than to the sign formula — e.g. 'the addressee changes only at 19:29's 2mp imperatives, and the genre with it' — which aligns this row with 068's cured reading and leaves the taunt's 2ms chain intact.

primary_reviews.rationale: The medium-severity self-contradiction is cured: the rationale no longer calls Zion the taunt's addressee, instead correctly identifying the 2ms suffix in 19:21's 'she has despised you, she has mocked you' as marking the Assyrian king as the one addressed, with virgin daughter of Zion as its grammatical subject -- and this reading is then carried consistently through the chain of 2ms forms at 19:22, 19:25 and 19:27 rather than reintroducing the earlier confusion anywhere else in the row. All quoted Hebrew collates byte-identical, evidence_refs match every verse the prose leans on, and the row still closes its argument at 19:29's addressee/genre shift, the same edge row 068 opens from the far side.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The commission formula at 19:20 (וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן אָמ֔וֹץ ...) and the nested tag at 19:21 (זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו) both match OSHB, and treating 19:21 rather than any WEB paragraph as the taunt's true opening, on register grounds, holds up. OL's medium-severity challenge is confirmed on inspection: בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן makes בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן the grammatical subject performing the mocking, not its addressee -- the 2ms suffix marks the Assyrian king as the one mocked, so 'the taunt proper addressed to' Zion is a genuine self-contradiction against the row's own later, correct statement that the taunt addresses the Assyrian king throughout. My own sweep of 19:22 (חֵרַ֨פְתָּ֙), 19:25 (שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ), and 19:27-28 (וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ ... וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ) confirms the 2ms addressee never wavers across the span, so the misassignment is isolated to one clause and does not touch the 19:20-28 boundary or its close.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both anchor quotations reproduce consonants and pointing exactly, the samekh keyed to 19:31 does stand at this row's stopping point, and it is labelled weak and non-driving as the addendum requires. The opening, however, is a waw-joined verbless clause, וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת, whose 2ms suffix cannot be distinguished morphologically from the taunt's addressee; the audience first becomes visibly different at the plural imperatives זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ ... וְאִכְל֥וּ later in the same verse. Nothing in the rationale argues for retaining 19:30-31, which leave the imperatives for weqatal וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה with פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית יְהוּדָ֛ה as subject; the fruit catchword (פִרְיָֽם in 19:29, פְרִ֖י in 19:30) is the binder that would have carried them.

challenges.claim: The row calls וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת 'A distinct sign-formula' opening the unit and treats the addressee change as visible there. Morphologically it is not: the clause is joined by waw and its לְּךָ֣ is the same 2ms form used throughout 19:21-28. The shift of audience surfaces only in the plural imperatives of that verse, זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ ... וְאִכְל֥וּ.
challenges.suggested_action: Cite the 2mp imperatives as the locus of the addressee shift and note the connective waw on וְזֶה, so the opening rests on the morphology that actually carries it.

challenges.claim: The rationale describes 19:29 only and then jumps to the close, offering no reason why 19:30-31 belong here. Those verses move to weqatal prediction, וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה ... וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י, under a new grammatical subject, and strongest_rejected_alternative likewise engages only the 19:29 edge.
challenges.suggested_action: Add one clause binding 19:30-31 to the sign, such as the agricultural catchword פִרְיָֽם (19:29) / פְרִ֖י (19:30) together with the shared remnant referent, so the three-verse span is argued end to end.

primary_reviews.rationale: The sign-formula וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת (19:29) and the closing zeal-clause קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה זֹּֽאת (19:31) both quote OSHB exactly. The addressee-shift claim holds up under scrutiny: the taunt's 2ms verbs addressed to the Assyrian king (verified across 19:21-28) give way to v.29's plural imperatives (זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ) that only cohere for a national audience, so the participant change driving this row's opening is real rather than asserted loosely.

Both OL items are cured and neither cure overreaches. The opening is now argued from what the morphology actually shows: וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת is waw-joined and its suffix is the taunt's own 2ms, with the audience change carried by זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ, which are indeed plural imperatives in that verse. The missing end-to-end argument is supplied by a catchword that checks out — פִרְיָֽם is verse-final in 19:29 and פְרִ֖י stands in 19:30 — and the setumah keyed to 19:31 is cited as corroborating 'without driving'. Collation of all nine Hebrew runs against oshb was clean, and 19:32's לָכֵ֗ן is verse-initial as the closing clause asserts.

Both original items are cured: the rationale now explicitly notes that 19:29's opening verbless clause carries the same 2ms suffix running through the taunt and so cannot itself carry the addressee shift, locating that shift instead in the verse's own plural imperatives (sow, reap, plant, eat); and 19:30-31 are now bound to 19:29 by an explicit fruit catchword chain (the noun closing 19:29, echoed in 19:30) running to the closing remnant/escape pairing at 19:31. The one flagged string in my own tokenizer pass, an artifact pairing the particle laken with an attached English suffix, is a script false-positive, not a source mismatch; laken itself collates fine everywhere it stands alone, and the setumah at 19:31 remains correctly disclosed as single-witness corroboration only.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both anchor quotations reproduce OSHB exactly, and the setumah at 19:31 is properly weighted as weak corroboration rather than a driver. Both OL challenges hold up under re-derivation. The opening clause וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת carries the same singular suffix used throughout the taunt, so it cannot itself be the locus of an addressee shift; that shift only becomes visible at the plural imperatives זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים וְאִכְל֥וּ later in the very same verse, exactly where OL locates it. The second challenge also survives: the row argues only the 19:29 opening and the 19:31 close and never explains why 19:30 belongs between them. My own reading supplies what the row omits -- 19:29's closing פִרְיָֽם and 19:30's פְרִ֖י share a fruit catchword, and 19:30's פְּלֵיטַ֧ת anticipates 19:31's וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה -- so the three verses are in fact bound end to end, simply not in the words the row uses. The span requires no change.

primary_reviews.rationale: לָכֵ֗ן does head 19:32 and works inferentially as claimed, and the motive clause closing 19:34 matches the source to the character. The discourse label is wrong twice over: 19:32 is a quotative frame (כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙), 19:33 shuts with the oracle signature נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and 19:34 speaks in the first person, וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י ... לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י, so what stands here is quoted divine speech with a third-person topic, not narration. I probed that signature as a candidate internal break and set it aside, because הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את (19:32), הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את (19:33) and הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את (19:34) recur and hold the three verses together. The length superlative does not survive counting.

challenges.claim: 'third-person narration', stated in the rationale and repeated in strongest_rejected_alternative, mislabels the discourse mode, and that label is the row's operative contrast with its neighbours. 19:32 introduces quoted speech with כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙, 19:33 ends נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and 19:34 is 1cs divine speech, וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י ... לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י. Nothing in 19:32-34 is narrated.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'third-person narration' with 'quoted divine speech whose topic is the Assyrian king in the third person', preserving the contrast with the 2ms taunt and the 2mp sign without misdescribing the clause type.

challenges.claim: 'This is the shortest ... of the three sub-units' fails arithmetic. 19:32-34 is three verses; the sign oracle 19:29-31 (row M8-2Kgs-068) is also three verses; only 19:20-28 is longer. No member is shortest, so the ranking has no referent.
challenges.suggested_action: Delete the superlative or restate it as 'tied with the sign oracle as the shortest of the three', letting the inferential force of לָכֵ֗ן carry the argument by itself.

primary_reviews.rationale: The inferential לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (19:32) and the closing motive clause לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי (19:34) both check out verbatim, and the reversion to third-person narration about the king is real, so the boundary itself stands. But the rationale's claim that this is 'the shortest ... of the three sub-units' does not hold: 068 (19:29-31) and 069 (19:32-34) are both exactly three verses, so 069 is tied for shortest, not uniquely so.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale asserts 19:32-34 is 'the shortest and most tightly argued of the three sub-units,' implying it is uniquely shortest, but 19:29-31 (row 068) is also exactly 3 verses -- the two rows are tied for shortest, not distinct in length.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise to 'one of the two shortest' or drop the length claim; it is not load-bearing for the boundary itself, which rests on the לָכֵן particle and the person-shift, both of which check out.

primary_reviews.rationale: The discourse-mode mislabel is gone and the replacement is well grounded: כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ opens quoted speech, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה is verse-final in 19:33, and 19:34 opens with the 1cs וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י, so nothing in the span is narrator's voice. The arithmetic superlative both reviewers flagged has been deleted outright, and the new 'this city' thread is exact — three different accentuations of one consonantal phrase, one per verse, with 19:35's temporal restart verse-initial after them. The one over-correction is the closing formula 'whose topic, not whose speaker, is referenced in the third person', which the row's own two citations contradict.

challenges.claim: 'Quoted speech whose topic, not whose speaker, is referenced in the third person' is falsified by the two forms the same sentence cites: כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ names the speaker of the oracle in the third person, and the signature נְאֻם יְהוָֽה does so again inside the quotation. Only the addressed-about party, the Assyrian king, is exclusively third person; the speaker is third person in the frame and first person only from 19:34.
challenges.suggested_action: Narrow the formula to what holds, e.g. 'quoted divine speech that refers to the Assyrian king in the third person throughout and turns to 1cs self-reference only at 19:34', dropping the speaker/topic contrast.

primary_reviews.rationale: All three original items are cured together: the 'third-person narration' mislabel is replaced throughout (rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative alike) with 'quoted divine speech whose topic ... is referenced in the third person,' which is what 19:32's messenger formula, 19:33's oracle signature, and 19:34's first-person divine speech actually show; and the false 'shortest of the three' superlative is simply dropped rather than left standing or merely hedged. challenges.claim: The rejected alternative calls the source-citation formula "interchangeable across kings and unrelated to this reign's specific narrative content", yet the material the row's own ellipsis skips inside 2Kgs.20.20 is exactly Hezekiah-specific: וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה אֶת הַבְּרֵכָה֙ וְאֶת הַתְּעָלָ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת הַמַּ֖יִם הָעִ֑ירָה. challenges.claim: "An age-length-mother notice shaped exactly like every other reign-opening in the book" does not survive inspection. Eight reign-openings, all of them northern, are clause-initial synchronisms supplying neither an accession age nor a maternal notice anywhere (13:1, 13:10, 14:23, 15:8, 15:17, 15:23, 15:27, 17:1); see 2Kgs.13.1 בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן אֲחַזְיָ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָחָ֨ז בֶּן יֵה֤וּא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן and 2Kgs.15.27 מָ֠לַךְ פֶּ֣קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֧הוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה. The maternal element occurs in thirteen verses, every one Judahite, and two Judahite openers still lack it, Ahaz at 2Kgs.16.2 בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם running age and length straight into an evaluation, Jehoram likewise at 8:17. Within Judah the clause also varies in shape: 2Kgs.18.2 reads בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ, seating a finite verb where 21:1 seats the king's name.
challenges.suggested_action: Limit the comparison to the Judahite accession notices that genuinely share this shape (21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18), replacing "every other reign-opening in the book" with "the Judahite reign-openings".

challenges.claim: 21:10 is mislabelled and then generalised from an empty set. It is a narrative speech-report, not a messenger formula; the messenger formula of this book appears inside this very oracle at 2Kgs.21.12, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, and again at 2Kgs.22.15, כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל. Meanwhile the rejected alternative's appeal to "every other occurrence of the device" has no referent, because וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר occurs exactly once in 2Kgs. The only other appearances of that prepositional phrase are subordinate clauses opening nothing whatever: 2Kgs.17.23 כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד כָּל עֲבָדָ֣יו הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים and 2Kgs.24.2 כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים.
challenges.suggested_action: Rename the 21:10 device a speech-report or commissioning notice, then either delete the "every other occurrence" appeal or replace it with the accurate statement that the formula is unique here, leaving the seam to rest on the narration-to-quotation transition by itself.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening accession formula בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (21:1) and the messenger formula וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר (21:10) both check out verbatim against oshb, and no parashah mark exists anywhere in 21:1-9 per pmarks_2Kgs.json, matching the row's own claim of an unmarked stretch. However the English gloss given for 21:9, "but they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray," does not match WEB's actual rendering of that verse, "But they didn’t listen, and Manasseh seduced them to do that which is evil more than the nations did whom Yahweh destroyed before the children of Israel.", a divergence worth correcting even though it does not touch the boundary itself.

challenges.claim: The parenthetical English rendering of 2Kgs 21:9, "but they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray," is presented as the verse's content but does not match the WEB witness, which reads "But they didn’t listen, and Manasseh seduced them to do that which is evil more than the nations did whom Yahweh destroyed before the children of Israel." challenges.claim: 'An age-length-mother notice matching the shape used at Judah's other reign-openers' still over-generalises. A consonantal search returns במלכו in 15 verses but ושם אמו in only 13: the two Judahite openers missing the maternal element are בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ (8:17) and בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ (16:2), and 18:2 seats a finite verb הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ where 21:1 seats בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ.

primary_reviews.rationale: Transcription is faithful at 21:10 and at the causal head יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙, the mark keyed to MT 21:11 really is a petuchah, and the observation that 21:16 drops out of quoted speech is right. The Hebrew will not, however, support "one uninterrupted first-person oracle": 21:11 shows no first-person morphology at all, and the earliest such form arrives only at הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה in 21:12, after a clause naming Yahweh in the third person. That clause is the pivot from indictment to sentence, and the break this row sets aside falls at precisely that joint.

challenges.claim: Calling 21:11-15 "one uninterrupted first-person oracle" and dismissing the MT 21:11 petuchah as merely landing "inside the speech" suppresses the same fact twice. 21:11, יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙, is third-person indictment with no first-person form in it; first person starts at הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה in 21:12, and the clause introducing it, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, is a full messenger formula referring to Yahweh in the third person. The indictment therefore ends and the sentence begins exactly between 21:11 and 21:12, which is where the only Masoretic break inside this span sits. 21:12 and its syntax are never cited anywhere in the row, so the one Hebrew-visible internal division goes unaddressed on syntactic grounds.
challenges.suggested_action: Either argue positively why indictment and sentence stay in one row despite a syntactic pivot and a Masoretic break coinciding at 21:11/21:12, or divide the span there; in either case replace "uninterrupted first-person" with an accurate account of where person reference actually shifts.

challenges.claim: "Follows the pattern this book's commission formulas otherwise establish everywhere they occur" is untestable, since 2Kgs supplies no second occurrence: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר stands alone at 21:10, and the two related expressions, 2Kgs.17.23 כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד כָּל עֲבָדָ֣יו הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים and 2Kgs.24.2 כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים, are embedded subordinate clauses rather than unit-openers. Medium confidence resting on a one-member pattern is calibrated against evidence that is not there.
challenges.suggested_action: Strike the book-wide commission-formula appeal and let the leading edge rest on the observable shift from narration into quotation at 21:10, citing that as the reason confidence stays at medium.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both edges hold up: the commission formula וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר opens at 21:10, and 21:16's וְגַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙ returns to third-person narration outside the quoted speech, both confirmed against oshb. The mid-oracle PE at 2Kgs.21.11 (pmarks_2Kgs.json, single-witness) is correctly treated as landing inside the speech rather than at either edge, so it neither drives nor lifts the boundary, exactly as the m8-mesh-r2 rule requires.

The high-severity item is genuinely cured rather than papered over. 21:11 is verified to contain no first-person form anywhere — יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ through וַיַּחֲטִ֥א ... בְּגִלּוּלָֽיו is third-person throughout — and the row now says so, siting the pivot at לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל with הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה as the first 1cs form and tracking it to the motive clause יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶת הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י. The petuchah keyed to MT 21:11 is disclosed as landing exactly at that pivot and explicitly denied any splitting force, which is the correct two-sided handling. The untestable one-member commission appeal is also gone; and the indictment-then-sentence shape the row now invokes does have in-book witnesses I checked independently, יַעַן at 1:16 and יַ֠עַן רַךְ לְבָ֨בְךָ֜ answered by לָכֵן֩ הִנְנִ֨י אֹֽסִפְךָ֜, the latter pair held inside a single row elsewhere in this same cluster. The only residue is cosmetic: evidence_refs still lists 1:3, 1:15, 9:1, 19:20 and 22:15 from the struck appeal.

The revision argues the hardest part of the original high-severity challenge head-on rather than around it: it names 21:11 a third-person indictment with no first-person form, locates the pivot to first person precisely at 21:12's הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה, and states plainly that the MT petuchah at 21:11 lands exactly on that syntactic seam -- then argues why an indictment-then-sentence structure stays inside one commissioned oracle rather than suppressing the tension. strongest_rejected_alternative goes further, calling the split-at-21:11/12 reading 'the genuinely strongest rival,' which is the honest framing a high-severity suppression charge demands. The book-wide 'commission formulas otherwise establish everywhere they occur' overreach is gone; the case now rests on the single 21:10 commission notice and the two-part judgment-oracle shape rather than a fabricated multi-occurrence pattern. All quoted Hebrew (21:10, 21:11, 21:12, 21:16) is byte-identical to 2Kgs_oshb.txt, and boundary_evidence_refs covers every verse the prose argues from.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Priority item. Direct re-derivation from oshb confirms OL's high-severity finding without qualification: 21:11 (opening יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה ... וַיַּחֲטִ֥א) is third-person indictment with zero first-person morphology, and the first first-person form in the unit is הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה in 21:12, introduced by the third-person messenger formula לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙. 'One uninterrupted first-person oracle' beginning at 21:11 is therefore false as written, and the row never engages the coincidence of the span's sole petuchah with this exact indictment-to-sentence pivot. LF's blanket support verdict missed this: LF correctly re-verified the byte-level Hebrew and the 21:16 exit into narration but took the row's 'first-person' characterization on faith instead of checking 21:11's morphology, so OL caught a real defect LF did not. Ruling on the disjunction the task poses: the pivot does not force a subdivision, because accusation-then-sentence is the standard two-part shape of a single prophetic judgment oracle introduced by one commission notice at 21:10, not two independently commissioned speeches, and nothing in this book's own method (e.g. the untroubled internal address-turn at 22:18 inside row 080) treats an internal rhetorical hinge as boundary-forcing by itself; a single weak, single-witness petuchah landing at a plausible internal seam does not overturn that under the m8-mesh-r2 marks-never-drivers rule. Boundary verdict: the frozen span 2Kgs.21.10-2Kgs.21.15 and its two outer edges are NOT harmed, since neither primary disputes them, but the boundary_rationale's internal description is factually wrong and must be corrected, and confidence should not be treated as settled until the rationale explicitly argues why the person-shift at 21:11/12 stays inside one oracle rather than being silently assumed away.
