challenges.claim: "The exact pattern that closes every reign in this book" fails a count. The death notice of the וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו type appears thirteen times as a reign-close in 2Kgs (8:24, 10:35, 13:9, 13:13, 14:16, 14:29, 15:7, 15:22, 15:38, 16:20, 20:21, 21:18, 24:6), whereas the archival opener appears twenty-two times, so the two are not an invariant pair. Amon closes with 2Kgs.21.25 וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָמ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה and then 2Kgs.21.26 וַיִּקְבְֹּ֥ר אֹת֛וֹ בִּקְבֻרָת֖וֹ בְּגַן עֻזָּ֑א, with no death notice; Josiah closes with 2Kgs.23.30 וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בִּקְבֻֽרָת֑וֹ; Amaziah with 2Kgs.14.20 וַיִּקָּבֵ֧ר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם עִם אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֥יר דָּוִֽד; the notice at 2Kgs.15.11 for Zechariah is followed by no death, burial or succession clause at all; and Jehoahaz, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah get no close of this shape.
challenges.suggested_action: Swap "every reign" for the verifiable subset, such as "the thirteen reigns that 2Kgs closes with the sleeping-with-the-fathers notice", or state the count outright so the assertion is falsifiable as written.

primary_reviews.rationale: 21:16's וְגַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙, the source-citation formula at 21:17 (וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י מְנַשֶּׁה֙ ... הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים), and the death-burial-succession formula at 21:18 (וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו ... וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו) all match oshb exactly, and the PE at 2Kgs.21.18 (pmarks_2Kgs.json) is correctly downgraded to a 'weak nod' rather than a driver. Bundling the guilt notice with the closing pair rather than splitting it off matches how this book's other narrator asides attach to their adjacent formula.

The count challenge is answered with a figure that survives independent testing: a consonantal search for וישכב ... עם אבתיו over oshb returns exactly thirteen verses, and they are exactly the thirteen the row lists (8:24, 10:35, 13:9, 13:13, 14:16, 14:29, 15:7, 15:22, 15:38, 16:20, 20:21, 21:18, 24:6), headed here by וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו. The falsifier the row volunteers is also correct — Amon's close at 21:25-26 carries the archival notice and a burial clause but no sleeping-with-fathers formula — and 'every reign' is gone. Leading edge and apparatus both check: the fronted-object bloodshed notice is verse-initial at 21:16, and pmarks keys a petuchah to 21:18, cited as a weak nod only.

The book-wide 'exact pattern that closes every reign' claim is replaced with a specific, grep-verified count: the sleeping-with-fathers formula closes exactly thirteen reigns (8:24, 10:35, 13:9, 13:13, 14:16, 14:29, 15:7, 15:22, 15:38, 16:20, 20:21, 21:18, 24:6 -- all thirteen confirmed against 2Kgs_oshb.txt, no more and no fewer), and Amon's own lack of the device in the very next row is now stated outright instead of left as an unexplained exception. challenges.claim: "A plot-then-verdict shape found wherever an assassinated king's reign closes" is contradicted by every other regicide in 2Kgs; the reprisal clause stands at 21:24 and nowhere else. Joash's servants conspire at MT 12:21 (= web 12:20), וַיָּקֻ֥מוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיִּקְשְׁרֽוּ קָ֑שֶׁר וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת יוֹאָ֔שׁ, yet MT 12:22 (= web 12:21) passes straight to וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו with no reprisal recorded in that pericope. Amaziah's killers at 2Kgs.14.19, וַיִּקְשְׁר֨וּ עָלָ֥יו קֶ֛שֶׁר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם, go unpunished there, the people simply enthroning Azariah in 14:21. In the northern cases the conspirator himself takes the throne, as at 2Kgs.15.30, וַיַּכֵּ֨הוּ֙ וַיְמִיתֵ֔הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּ֑יו, which inverts rather than repeats the verdict motif.

primary_reviews.rationale: The accession formula at 21:19 (בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ), the conspiracy pair וַיִּקְשְׁר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי אָמ֖וֹן עָלָ֑יו וַיָּמִ֥יתוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ (21:23), and וַיַּךְ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַקֹּשְׁרִ֖ים ... וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (21:24) all check out against oshb, and book_strategy_draft.md's own decision matrix independently lists 21:23-24 as one of this book's recurring conspiracy-formula instances, so keeping the plot and counter-execution together is well grounded rather than a straw rejection. One completeness gap: the rationale narrates the source-citation formula as spanning '21:25-26,' and I confirmed 21:25's text (וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָמ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה) independently against oshb, but boundary_evidence_refs cites only 21.26.

primary_reviews.rationale: The 'wherever an assassinated king's reign closes' universal is withdrawn and the rebuilt argument rests on the shared subject chain, which is the right ground; the Joash and Amaziah counter-cases are stated accurately and the MT/WEB offset for 12:21-22 is dual-cited exactly as the crosswalk requires. The LF citation gap is closed too: oshb and web refs for 21:25 are now present alongside 21:26, and every quotation in the row collates cleanly, including וַיַּךְ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַקֹּשְׁרִ֖ים. But the repair introduced a fresh enumeration error in the northern half of the contrast set, and the uniqueness claim still overreaches by one verse elsewhere in the book.

challenges.claim: 'Both northern regicides end with the conspirator himself taking the throne (15:25, 15:30)' undercounts. A consonantal search returns ויקשר at 12:21, 14:19, 15:10, 15:25, 15:30 and 21:23, and the bare וימלך תחתיו at 15:10, 15:14, 15:25 and 15:30. 15:10 is a northern conspiracy with the same outcome, וַיִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ שַׁלֻּ֣ם בֶּן יָבֵ֔שׁ ... וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו, and 15:14 is a further northern regicide, וַיַּ֛ךְ אֶת שַׁלּ֥וּם בֶּן יָבֵ֖ישׁ בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיְמִיתֵ֖הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו. The book has at least four such northern cases, not two.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'both northern regicides' with 'the northern regicides (15:10, 15:14, 15:25, 15:30)', or write 'every northern case ends with the killer on the throne', which is what the four verses actually show and still serves the contrast.

challenges.claim: 'A pairing this book narrates only here' is contestable as stated: 14:5 records וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת עֲבָדָ֔יו הַמַּכִּ֖ים אֶת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָבִֽיו, i.e. retribution on a king's assassins, the same motif as 21:24 though executed by the successor rather than by עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ and placed in the following reign's narrative. The row's narrower statement about MT 12:21-22 is accurate, but the book-level uniqueness claim runs past it.
challenges.suggested_action: Qualify to 'a pairing no other assassination report in this book carries in its own close (compare the displaced reprisal at 14:5)', and add oshb:2Kgs.14.5 to boundary_evidence_refs.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both original defects are resolved without loosening the underlying claim: 21:25 is now quoted in the archival-formula sentence and present in boundary_evidence_refs, and the 'plot-then-verdict shape found wherever an assassinated king's reign closes' universal is replaced by an explicit statement that the reprisal pairing is unique to Amon, backed by the three counter-cases the challenge supplied -- Joash's unpunished conspirators (MT 12:21-22, correctly dual-cited as 'MT; = web:2Kgs.12.20/21' per the crosswalk's offset rule), Amaziah's unpunished killers (14:19-21), and the two northern regicides where the conspirator himself takes the throne (15:25, 15:30). Every Hebrew fragment quoted for 21:19, 21:23, 21:24, 21:25, and 21:26 is byte-identical to the oshb source, the wayyiqtol endings of 15:25/15:30 (וַיְמִיתֵ֖הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו-type clauses) confirm the conspirator-enthronement claim, and the MT 12:21/12:22 dual-citation format matches web_mt_crosswalk.json's stated offset exactly.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The accession formula, the conspiracy-and-reprisal pair at 21:23-24, and the archival-plus-burial close at 21:25-26 all reproduce oshb without deviation. LF's citation-hygiene catch is accurate: 21:25's archival clause is discussed by verse number in the prose ('21:25-26') yet never receives its own entry in boundary_evidence_refs, which lists only 21.26. OL's substantive challenge to a 'plot-then-verdict shape found wherever an assassinated king's reign closes' also survives re-derivation: Joash's conspiracy (MT 12:21, = web 12:20) passes straight to Amaziah's succession with no reprisal clause at all, Amaziah's own killers at 14:19 go unpunished while the people simply enthrone Azariah at 14:21, and both northern regicides (15:25, 15:30) end with the conspirator himself taking the throne, inverting rather than repeating Amon's shape. Both defects sit in the supporting generalization, not the boundary; the accession opening at 21:19 and the archival-and-burial close ahead of Josiah's 22:1 opener remain unchallenged by either primary.

primary_reviews.rationale: Everything operative in this row survives checking. בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ matches its two immediate predecessors element for element, 22:2 does carry the first favourable evaluation since Hezekiah, the petuchah recorded against MT 22:2 exists and follows that verse, and 22:3 opens with the temporal clause וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ. Only the closing phrase of the rejected alternative overstates, extending a separating force to reign-openers that this cluster's own earlier rows decline to separate.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative invokes "the same force separating every reign-opener elsewhere in this book", and no such general force is visible in the Hebrew. Manasseh's opener בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ with its evaluation in 21:2 is followed at once by plain narrative wayyiqtol, וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת הַבָּמ֔וֹת in 21:3, and no Masoretic break intervenes until after MT 21:11; Amon's opener with its evaluation in 21:19-20 is followed by וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּכָל הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר הָלַ֣ךְ אָבִ֑יו in 21:21, with no break until after MT 21:26. Rows M8-2Kgs-074 and M8-2Kgs-077 of this same cluster consequently do not separate either opener, so the universal is contradicted by the drafter's own adjacent decisions.
challenges.suggested_action: Confine the assertion to Josiah, where separation really is attested by the petuchah after MT 22:2 together with the temporal clause opening 22:3, and drop the word "every".

primary_reviews.rationale: The accession formula בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (22:1) and the evaluation pair וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה ... וְלֹא סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול (22:2) match oshb exactly, and the date formula opening 22:3 (וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ) is a genuinely different unit-opening device, so this two-verse row's edges both hold. The PE at 2Kgs.22.2 (pmarks_2Kgs.json) is properly treated as a supporting nod rather than the argument's basis.

The 'every reign-opener' universal is confined to Josiah and the confinement is checkable in the apparatus: pmarks records PE at 22:2 with the next preceding marks at 21:11 and 21:26, so Manasseh's opener really does run unmarked into 21:3's wayyiqtol until after MT 21:11, and Amon's into 21:21 until after MT 21:26. The Josiah-specific convergence holds — וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה is verse-initial in 22:2, וְלֹא סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול verse-final, and וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ opens 22:3 immediately after the mark. The favourable-evaluation claim also survives an independent grep: ויעש ... הישר appears at 12:3, 14:3, 15:3, 15:34, 18:3 and 22:2, so nothing favourable intervenes between Hezekiah and Josiah.

Rather than repeating the discredited 'same force separating every reign-opener' claim, the row names the exact asymmetry: Manasseh's opener runs unmarked from 21:1 to the first petuchah at 21:11, and Amon's runs unmarked from 21:19 to the first petuchah at 21:26 (both confirmed against pmarks_2Kgs.json, which records no intervening keys), so the mark-plus-date-formula convergence at 22:2/22:3 is argued as Josiah-specific rather than a book-wide rule -- and strongest_rejected_alternative says so explicitly, conceding the convergence 'does not recur at the sibling reign-openers earlier in this same cluster.' That is a direct, self-aware answer to the self-contradiction charge rather than a rewording of the same universal. boundary_evidence_refs carries both Manasseh's and Amon's opener verses plus all three relevant marks (21:11, 21:26, 22:2), and every cited Hebrew fragment matches 2Kgs_oshb.txt.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Josiah's accession-and-evaluation pair and the trailing petuchah at 22:2 both match oshb and pmarks_2Kgs.json as both primaries report. OL's challenge to the rejected alternative's claim of 'the same force separating every reign-opener elsewhere in this book' is confirmed directly from this cluster's own adjacent rows: Manasseh's opener runs straight from 21:1-2 into plain wayyiqtol narrative at 21:3 with no mark until MT 21:11, and Amon's opener runs from 21:19-20 into 21:21 with no mark until MT 21:26, so rows 074 and 077 in this very cluster decline to separate at the opener precisely where the rejected alternative claims a universal separating force exists. This corrects an overreaching universal, not the row's own boundary, since the actual seam here -- petuchah after 22:2, date formula opening 22:3 -- is a Josiah-specific convergence neither primary disputes.

challenges.claim: "Parashah marks are absent across this whole stretch, so the seam rests solely on the date-formula-to-departure pairing" understates the apparatus at the leading edge. pmarks_2Kgs.json records a petuchah keyed to 2Kgs.22.2, which under the marks-follow-their-verse convention sits immediately before this row's first verse, and row M8-2Kgs-078 cites that very mark for that very juncture. challenges.suggested_action: Split the sentence so the leading edge cites the adjacent MT 22:2 petuchah as weak single-witness corroboration, and confine the no-marks statement to the trailing edge, where it is exactly true and where syntax must carry all the weight.

primary_reviews.rationale: The date-commission formula opening 22:3 and the departure-formula seam at 22:14 both check out, and the row honestly engages its strongest rival: I confirmed the report-inclusio quotes וַיָּ֥שֶׁב אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָ֑ר (22:9, singular) and וַיָּשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָֽר (22:20, plural) both match oshb exactly, and book_strategy_draft.md's own larger_unit_preservation_check independently flags 22:14 as the only arguable seam in this complex, so the chosen edge is well supported. Leading and trailing forms are where the row says: וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ heads 22:3 and לְכוּ֩ דִרְשׁ֨וּ אֶת יְהוָ֜ה heads 22:13.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every fragment quoted, the circumstantial clause וְהִ֛יא יֹשֶׁ֥בֶת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה included, is byte-faithful to the source, and the pivot at 22:18 is a genuine fronted prepositional phrase that reorients the address without restarting anything. What does not hold is the generalisation offered in support, since this book's closest analogue to the errand keeps the command and the going inside one continuous scene.

challenges.claim: The opening is grounded on an "arrival-and-petition shape that elsewhere opens self-contained audience scenes throughout the book", with the alternative appealing to arrival formulas "opening vignettes throughout the Elisha material". A book-wide search for the clause-initial motion verb returns sixteen verses in 2Kgs, four of which are the regnal-evaluation idiom and no arrival at all (2Kgs.8.18 וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל, likewise 8:27, 16:3 and 21:21), while most of the remainder continue a scene already running. The nearest structural analogue tells against the row: at 2Kgs.8.8 the king commands וְלֵ֕ךְ לִקְרַ֖את אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְדָרַשְׁתָּ֨ אֶת יְהוָ֤ה מֵֽאוֹתוֹ֙, and 2Kgs.8.9 discharges it with וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חֲזָאֵל֮ לִקְרָאתוֹ֒, the same inquiry errand answered by the same verb inside a single scene. At 22:14, וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַ֠כֹּהֵן is likewise a bare wayyiqtol executing the order given in 22:13, carrying no disjunctive syntax, no formula and no mark.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the "throughout the book" generalisation and rest the opening on the change of addressee and location together with the report clause closing 22:20, or else engage the 2Kgs.8.8-9 parallel and explain why the Huldah errand separates where the Hazael errand does not.

primary_reviews.rationale: The arrival formula וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַ֠כֹּהֵן ... אֶל חֻלְדָּ֨ה הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה ... וְהִ֛יא יֹשֶׁ֥בֶת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה (22:14) and the closing report וַיָּשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָֽר (22:20) both match oshb exactly, and 23:1's assembly formula (וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּאַסְפ֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו כָּל זִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם) is a genuine new scene, confirming the closing edge. The internal address-turn at 22:18 (וְאֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֤חַ אֶתְכֶם֙) is correctly kept inside the row as a turn-marker rather than a seam, consistent with how this book treats turn-markers inside a single dialogue elsewhere.

The 'throughout the book' generalisation is dropped and the Hazael parallel is engaged head-on, which is what the challenge demanded; וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חֲזָאֵל֮ לִקְרָאתוֹ֒ is correctly presented as discharging 8:8's command inside one scene, so the bare wayyiqtol וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַ֠כֹּהֵן is no longer asked to carry the separation. The replacement ground is verifiable: חלדה occurs once in 2Kgs (22:14) and משנה as a quarter-name only at 22:14 (with 23:4 and 25:18 in other senses), so אֶל חֻלְדָּ֨ה הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה and בַּמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה really are unstaged before this verse. The second distinguishing feature, however, is scoped so tightly that the analogue it dismisses in fact supplies it.

challenges.claim: 'The scene closes on its own report-back formula ... answering 22:13's imperative in a way nothing inside 8:8-9 parallels' is true only because the comparison is cut at 8:9. The Hazael errand does report back, at 8:14: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָֽה אָמַ֥ר לְךָ֖ אֱלִישָׁ֑ע. Since the row itself treats 8:8-9 as the closest formal analogue for an inquiry errand, the report-back cannot distinguish 22:14-20 from it; only the addressee-novelty ground survives.
challenges.suggested_action: Either extend the comparison to 8:8-15 and rest the separation on addressee-and-location novelty alone, or state explicitly that the report clause is being weighed only against the two verses quoted, noting 8:14 as the Hazael scene's own answering report.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the strongest single cure in the cluster: instead of resting on an unverifiable 'arrival-and-petition shape ... throughout the book,' the row engages the one real rival directly, Hazael's errand at 8:8-9, concedes the going-verb alone cannot carry the seam, and relocates the argument onto two things that do distinguish 22:14 -- a genuinely new, unstaged addressee and location, and a closing report-back formula at 22:20 that 8:8-9 has no counterpart for (confirmed: 8:9 ends on Hazael's question to Ben-hadad, not a return-and-report clause). That argument is sound and grep-checkable against 2Kgs_oshb.txt. What is missing is smaller: the prose leans on 22:13 (the commission 22:14 discharges) and 23:1 (the point after which this row is said to end) as load-bearing reference points for its two edges, but neither verse appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale argues from '22:13's imperative' as the commission this row's opening discharges, and from 23:1 as the point marking where this row's own close falls, but boundary_evidence_refs contains no oshb:2Kgs.22.13 or oshb:2Kgs.23.1 entry.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:2Kgs.22.13 and oshb:2Kgs.23.1 to boundary_evidence_refs, matching the two verses the argument's edges actually depend on.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The arrival clause at 22:14, the address-turn at 22:18, and the closing report at 22:20 all collate exactly, and the 23:1 assembly formula confirms the trailing edge, matching LF's check. OL's challenge to an 'arrival-and-petition shape... throughout the book' holds under independent grep: of the sixteen 2Kgs verses opening with this clause-initial motion verb, four (8:18, 8:27, 16:3, 21:21) are the fixed regnal-evaluation idiom 'walked in the way of,' not arrivals at all, and book_strategy_draft.md's own catalogued 'vignette arrival/petition opener' category is confined to the Elisha material in chapters 2-8 and does not itself list 22:14 as a member, so the row extends a documented pattern by analogy rather than citing a genuine parallel. OL's closest true analogue is the stronger point: at 8:8-9 the king's identical 'go and inquire of Yahweh' command is discharged by the same going-verb within one continuous scene, and the row never explains why the Huldah errand should separate where the Hazael errand does not. None of this reopens the boundary -- the change of addressee and named location, plus the closing report clause answering 22:13's imperative, still ground the scene independent of the flawed generalization -- but the rationale needs the book-wide claim replaced with an argument that engages rather than sidesteps the 8:8-9 parallel.

post_resolution_check.notes: Verified the Hazael-errand comparison (8:8-9, 8:14) against their verses, and confirmed the 'to the king of Judah who sent you' gloss accurately renders the specific Hebrew clause fragment quoted rather than misquoting the WEB translation of the full verse.

primary_reviews.rationale: Machine collation places the opening citation as the whole of 23:1 and וּבְכָל נֶ֔פֶשׁ לְהָקִ֗ים אֶת as the closing clause of 23:3, both byte-identical to the witness. The opener is a verse-initial wayyiqtol whose royal subject governs an unbroken chain through 23:2 (וַיַּ֣עַל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ) and 23:3 (וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ), so no clause inside the span competes for unit-initial status. The headcount holds: 22:12 names exactly five men and 22:14 sends those same five to Huldah, against the far wider cast assembled in 23:1-2. The parashah disclaimer is accurate, since pmarks records nothing between 2Kgs.22.2 and 2Kgs.23.30; and ch 23 lies outside the WEB 11:21-12:21 offset band (WEB ch 23 carries 37 verses, content-aligned with MT), so single-reference citation is right here.

The summons formula וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּאַסְפ֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו כָּל זִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם opens 23:1 with fresh participants (elders of Judah/Jerusalem) against the prior scene's five envoys to Huldah, verified as חִלְקִיָּ֣ה, אֲחִיקָ֣ם, עַכְבּ֨וֹר, שָׁפָ֣ן, עֲשָׂיָ֥ה at 22:12/22:14, and the unit closes on the people's own ratification וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד כָּל הָעָ֖ם בַּבְּרִֽית (23:3) before 23:4's distinct command to Hilkiah alone opens the purge. Both quoted Hebrew strings match the source exactly, and the 'no pe/samekh corroborates either edge' disclosure is accurate since neither verse carries a mark.

Neither primary raised a challenge, and my independent check turned up nothing to add; the boundary and its supporting prose both stand unmodified.

post_resolution_check.notes: Traced the assembly-open/ratification-close Hebrew at 23:1 and 23:3 byte-for-byte against OSHB; both boundary_evidence_refs resolve cleanly. The parenthetical gloss on 23:3 renders the Hebrew more literally than WEB's own "agreed to the covenant" phrasing, a minor paraphrase-as-verbatim gap logged in aggregate defects rather than a boundary problem.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both halves of the elided 23:4 citation and the entirety of 23:14 match the witness character for character, and the opening clause is genuinely verse-initial; my own grep shows וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ occurring only three times in this book (22:12, 23:4, 23:21), which is real opener evidence. The stretch hangs together as one waw-chain of weqatal and wayyiqtol forms down to 23:14, and I found nothing in 23:5-23:11 able to carry a unit break. Two descriptive statements fail on inspection: the movement's own first verse already sends material out of Judah (וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵֽל), and the internal turns dismissed as unmarked include two fronted-object clauses with verb and subject withheld to the end.

challenges.claim: The row says this movement "stays inside Jerusalem and Judah's territory" and that only "the next verse pivots to a named place outside Judah," yet 23:4 itself ends וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵֽל (and he carried their ashes to Bethel). Bethel is therefore already named inside the stretch characterised as exclusively Jerusalem-and-Judah, which blunts the territorial contrast drawn with 23:15.
challenges.suggested_action: Qualify to 'the acting scene stays in Jerusalem and Judah' and record 23:4's ashes-to-Bethel clause as an anticipation of the Bethel movement rather than a counter-example.

challenges.claim: "none of those internal turns carries a location-shift marker comparable to the clauses opening 23:15 and 23:19" misstates the syntax it dismisses. 23:12 and 23:13 are verse-initial waw + fronted-object clauses with locative relatives and the finite verb plus subject held to the very end: וְאֶֽת הַֽמִּזְבְּח֡וֹת ... נָתַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ, and וְֽאֶת הַבָּמ֞וֹת ... טִמֵּ֖א הַמֶּֽלֶךְ. That is the disjunctive frame of 23:15/23:19 minus the additive particle; what actually articulates the register's movements is גַם, not fronting and not a locative relative clause.
challenges.suggested_action: Name גַם as the articulating particle and concede that 23:12 and 23:13 are marked disjunctive clauses which nonetheless stay inside the Jerusalem/Judah domain, which puts the no-split conclusion on accurate grammar.

primary_reviews.rationale: The command formula וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת חִלְקִיָּהוּ֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל opens 23:4 exactly as quoted (continuing לְהוֹצִיא֙ מֵהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה), and the bone-filling summary at 23:14 (וְשִׁבַּר֙ אֶת הַמַּצֵּב֔וֹת וַיִּכְרֹ֖ת אֶת הָאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים וַיְמַלֵּ֥א אֶת מְקוֹמָ֖ם עַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָֽם) closes the movement before 23:15's own וְגַם-led place-name shift to Bethel. No internal verse in 4-13 carries a comparable named-location marker; the Geba-to-Beersheba phrase at v8 still describes Judah's own territory rather than an external place, so the register's tripartite division survives scrutiny.

Both OL items are cured. The Bethel clause is no longer suppressed: וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵֽל is quoted, conceded as verse-final in 23:4, and recast as an anticipation of the second movement, with the territorial claim narrowed to 'the acting scene'. The disjunctive syntax of the two internal turns is likewise conceded rather than denied — וְאֶֽת הַֽמִּזְבְּח֡וֹת ... נָתַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ and the parallel shape closing 23:13 with טִמֵּ֖א הַמֶּֽלֶךְ — and neither carries the additive particle, which a consonantal search confirms: גם is absent from 23:4-14 entirely and present at 23:15, 23:19, 23:24 and 23:27. That same search, though, turns up a counter-example to the new criterion inside the register itself.

challenges.claim: 'What distinguishes a movement-opener from an ordinary internal turn is גַם, not fronting by itself' over-generates. 23:24 has the identical disjunctive shape with the additive particle, וְגַ֣ם אֶת הָאֹב֣וֹת ... בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ, yet its scope is בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם — inside Judah and Jerusalem, opening no new territory — so it cannot be a movement-opener on the row's own territorial test. The particle is therefore necessary for the openers at וְגַ֨ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ and וְגַם֩ אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת but not sufficient.
challenges.suggested_action: State the criterion as a conjunction — a movement-opener carries גַם AND names territory outside Judah/Jerusalem — and note 23:24 as the גַם-clause that stays inside, which preserves the no-split conclusion for 23:12/23:13 on both counts.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both territorial claims are repaired with precision rather than retreat. The 'stays inside Jerusalem and Judah's territory' line now explicitly folds in 23:4's own Bethel-bound ash clause as 'an anticipation of what 23:15 will do at length rather than a counter-example,' and the 'no location-shift marker comparable to 23:15/23:19' line is replaced by a correct concession that 23:12 and 23:13 share the identical disjunctive fronted-object-and-delayed-verb shape, distinguished from 23:15/23:19 only by the absence of the גַם particle. A verse-initial check against 2Kgs_oshb.txt confirms 23:12 (וְאֶֽת הַֽמִּזְבְּח֡וֹת ... נָתַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ) and 23:13 (וְֽאֶת הַבָּמ֞וֹת ... טִמֵּ֖א הַמֶּֽלֶךְ) both open with plain וְאֶת rather than וְגַם, while 23:15 opens וְגַ֨ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ, and 23:4 does end וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵֽל exactly as quoted. Both fixes match their challenges' suggested wording, and boundary_evidence_refs already carried every verse this repaired argument needs.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both OL challenges survive independent testing. Reading 23:4 in full shows it does end with וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵֽל, so Bethel is indeed named inside the very stretch the row calls exclusively Jerusalem-and-Judah; the acting scene stays local even though this one destination clause reaches outside it, exactly the qualification OL proposes. Reading 23:12-13 confirms their construction too: both are verse-initial waw plus fronted object plus locative relative with the finite verb and subject delayed to clause-end (נָתַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ; טִמֵּ֖א הַמֶּֽלֶךְ), a shape genuinely closer to 23:15/23:19 than the row's blanket dismissal implies; what actually distinguishes the register's three movement-openers is the גַם particle, not the fronting itself. Neither correction moves an edge, since the movement still opens at 23:4's command formula and closes at 23:14's bone-filling summary before 23:15's place-shift.

post_resolution_check.notes: Sliced the command formula (23:4), the two internal turns (23:12-13), and the summary close (23:14) against OSHB, and confirmed the bare particle mentions discuss the morpheme abstractly rather than tagging a specific verse quotation. primary_reviews.rationale: All three quotations collate exactly and sit where the row implies: וְגַ֨ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל stands verse-initial in 23:15, the fulfillment notice falls inside 23:16, and the bones clause is verse-final in 23:18. The construction claim survives independent testing, since verse-initial וְגַם occurs in 2Kgs only at 21:16, 23:15, 23:19, 23:24 and 24:4 on my own grep, and only 23:15 and 23:19 pair it with a relative naming fresh territory (וְגַם֩ אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן). Within the span, 23:16-18 forms a single sequence of turning, seeing, sending and speaking with no rival opener, and the 1Kgs 13 chain is correctly flagged as background rather than a consulted source. Neither edge claims a parashah mark, and none is keyed there.

23:15 opens with the named place-shift to Bethel (וְגַ֨ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל) exactly as quoted, the fulfillment notice כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרָא֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים at 23:16 matches the source verbatim, and the close at 23:18 (וַֽיְמַלְּטוּ֙ עַצְמֹתָ֔יו אֵ֚ת עַצְמ֣וֹת הַנָּבִ֔יא אֲשֶׁר בָּ֖א מִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן) precedes 23:19's fresh shift to Samaria. The disclaimer that the 1Kgs 13 cross-reference is 'background observation, not a source consulted' properly respects the cluster's blind-review isolation.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: I collated the Bethel opener, the fulfillment-notice clause, and the bones-preserved close against 2Kgs_oshb.txt and all three match without variance, sitting exactly where the row places them. A book-wide search for verse-initial וְגַם turns up only five hits total (21:16, 23:15, 23:19, 23:24, 24:4), which corroborates the row's implicit treatment of this construction as a rare, meaningful register-movement marker rather than routine phrasing. Neither primary challenged this row, and nothing in my own pass surfaced a defect worth raising.

post_resolution_check.notes: Verified 23:15-18 (location-shift opener, fulfillment notice, undisturbed-bones close) against OSHB word-for-word; the English gloss on 23:15 tracks WEB's own wording almost exactly. Boundary evidence resolves without issue.

primary_reviews.rationale: The two quoted strings are clean and correctly placed: וְגַם֩ אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן opens 23:19, and the travel notice ends 23:20, so the edges themselves rest on real Hebrew. The supporting formula claim does not hold, because 23:4 begins with a command clause rather than the additive construction, leaving the asserted three-way shape match wrong at one of its three members. A second statement misreports content, since the Bethel movement narrates no slaughter of priests for 23:20 to be parallel to. Neither defect shifts an edge, but both undercut a row carrying high confidence.

challenges.claim: "matching the shape of 23:4 and 23:15 exactly" is false of 23:4. 23:19 opens וְגַם֩ אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן and 23:15 opens וְגַ֨ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל, both additive particle + fronted object + locative relative, whereas 23:4 opens וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת חִלְקִיָּהוּ֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל, a wayyiqtol command clause with a list of personal objects. My own book-wide grep for verse-initial וְגַם in 2Kgs returns 21:16, 23:15, 23:19, 23:24 and 24:4 only, so 23:4 cannot belong to the series.
challenges.suggested_action: Remove 23:4 from the shape claim and state instead that the register's first movement is opened by the command formula while only its second and third movements use the additive construction.

challenges.claim: "the narrator treats the Samaria priests' slaughter as parallel to Bethel's rather than describing it afresh" does not match the text. No killing of priests appears anywhere in 23:15-18; the comparison clause stands at the close of 23:19 and concerns the shrine-houses (וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לָהֶ֔ם כְּכָל הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בְּבֵֽית אֵֽל), while 23:20 narrates the slaughter with its own new verbs וַ֠יִּזְבַּח ... וַיִּשְׂרֹ֛ף.
challenges.suggested_action: Ground the brevity in 23:19's own comparison over the high-place houses and say plainly that 23:20's slaughter is fresh material, not a back-reference.

primary_reviews.rationale: The tier-1 edges hold: 23:19's וְגַם֩ אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן opens the Samaria movement as quoted, and וַיָּ֖שָׁב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם at 23:20 closes the whole register before 23:21's addressee-shifted command. But the claim that this opener is 'matching the shape of 23:4 and 23:15 exactly' overstates the parallel: 23:4 opens with a plain command formula (וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ...), not a וְגַם-led place clause, so it does not share 23:15/23:19's grammatical shape at all.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale states the 23:19 opener is 'matching the shape of 23:4 and 23:15 exactly,' but 23:4 (וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת חִלְקִיָּהוּ֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל ...) is a command formula with no וְגַם particle and no location-relative-clause construction, unlike 23:15 and 23:19 which both open וְגַם אֶת [object] אֲשֶׁר בְ/עָרֵי [place]. The claimed three-way grammatical match is only a two-way match (23:15/23:19); 23:4 matches only at the functional level of 'opens a movement,' not in grammatical shape.
challenges.suggested_action: Revise the sentence to claim the functional parallel only (e.g. 'opens a movement, as 23:4 and 23:15 also do') rather than an exact grammatical match, or drop the reference to 23:4's shape.

primary_reviews.rationale: The three-way shape claim is gone and the correction holds on inspection: 23:4 now stands where it belongs, as the wayyiqtol command clause וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ, apart from the additive-particle openers of 23:15 and 23:19, and 23:20's slaughter is credited to its own fresh verb וַ֠יִּזְבַּח rather than to a back-reference the text never makes. The brevity of the movement is now grounded in 23:19's comparison over the shrine-houses, which is what that clause actually compares. One number failed to travel with the repair: my own grep of verse-initial waw-plus-gam returns 21:16, 23:15, 23:19, 23:24 and 24:4, so once 23:4 leaves the series 23:19's וְגַם֩ is its second member, not a third.

challenges.claim: The opening sentence calls 23:19 a third gam-headed clause, but the repair that removed 23:4 from the construction series leaves only two such clauses standing at that point. My grep of verse-initial waw-plus-gam in 2Kgs returns 21:16, 23:15, 23:19, 23:24 and 24:4; inside the register 23:15's וְגַ֨ם is first, 23:19's וְגַם֩ second, and 23:24's וְגַ֣ם third. The ordinal was accurate only under the discarded claim that 23:4 belonged to the same construction.
challenges.suggested_action: Change 'A third' to 'A second', or recast as 'the register's third movement, again headed by the additive particle', so the count matches the corrected series. No span change.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both digest challenges are cured: the row now separates the genuine grammatical match (23:19 shares its gam-plus-fronted-object-plus-locative-relative shape only with 23:15) from the merely functional parallel with 23:4's command formula וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ, and it grounds the movement's brevity in 23:19's own shrine-house comparison clause rather than treating 23:20's priest-slaughter as a back-reference to Bethel. Every quoted Hebrew form collates byte-for-byte against 2Kgs_oshb.txt, and both edges (23:4/23:15 as comparanda, 23:21's command formula as the true close) are covered in boundary_evidence_refs.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: All three challenges check out. A targeted grep for verse-initial וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ confirms it occurs only at 22:12, 23:4, and 23:21, none sharing the גַם-plus-fronted-object-plus-locative-relative shape that only 23:15 and 23:19 exhibit, so the row's claimed three-way match at 23:4/23:15/23:19 is a two-way match dressed as three; LF and OL reached this identically from opposite ends, a genuine convergent finding. Separately, rereading 23:15-20 shows no priest is killed at Bethel; the comparison clause closing 23:19 concerns the shrine-houses' fate, and 23:20's slaughter (וַ֠יִּזְבַּח, וַיִּשְׂרֹ֛ף) introduces new action rather than repeating anything from the Bethel scene, so the row's 'parallel slaughter' explanation for the movement's brevity misidentifies what 23:19 is actually comparing. None of this touches the verified edges at 23:19 and 23:20.

primary_reviews.rationale: Each citation collates and each is verse-initial, as the argument requires. The opening verb phrase is one of just three occurrences book-wide (22:12, 23:4, 23:21 on my grep), so it functions as a genuine opening device rather than an ad hoc label, and the addressee contrast is exact: אֶת כָּל הָעָ֣ם over against the priestly list of 23:4. Nothing within the span can detach, because 23:22 and 23:23 begin with subordinating particles (כִּ֣י לֹ֤א ... כִּ֗י אִם) and cannot stand apart from the command they qualify. The incomparability statement is explicitly limited to what this text asserts rather than advanced as a corpus-wide finding, which is the correct restraint, and 23:24 offers no command verb to rival 23:21.

The command formula at 23:21 (וַיְצַ֤ו הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת כָּל הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר עֲשׂ֣וּ פֶ֔סַח) is verified against the source and rightly distinguished from the register's priest-directed commands by its addressee (all the people) and its subject matter (festival, not idols). The date-anchored close at 23:23 stands before 23:24's plain marker lacking any command verb, and the row properly declines to verify the Passover-uniqueness claim at 23:22 (כִּ֣י לֹ֤א נַֽעֲשָׂה֙ כַּפֶּ֣סַח הַזֶּ֔ה מִימֵי֙ הַשֹּׁ֣פְטִ֔ים...) against the wider corpus, respecting the evidence-only discipline.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The command formula at 23:21 is one of only three verse-initial וַיְצַ֤ו הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ occurrences in the book, and its addressee (כָּל הָעָ֣ם) genuinely contrasts with 23:4's priestly list, so the row's distinguishing claim rests on real, rare evidence rather than an ad hoc label. Both 23:22 and 23:23 open on subordinating particles (כִּ֣י) that keep them syntactically dependent on 23:21's command, confirming they cannot be pried loose as separate openers, and 23:24 supplies no rival command verb. No challenge was raised by either primary, and I found no basis to add one.

primary_reviews.rationale: The particle at 23:24 and the adversative clause at 23:26 both collate and both stand verse-initial, and the statement about the apparatus is factually right: pmarks keys nothing between 2Kgs.22.2 and 2Kgs.23.30. Candour about the softness is welcome, but the rationale reasons from only two of its four verses, never touching 23:25 or 23:27, and that is precisely where the decisive Hebrew sits. As a result the assertion that no tier-1 signal settles the attachment is overstated, since 23:26 answers 23:25 with the same verb negated, and the structural contrast drawn between 23:24 and the register's additive clauses is not observable in the consonantal text.

challenges.claim: "nothing tier-1 and no parashah mark settles which" overlooks a signal inside the row's own span. 23:25 states the king's incomparable turning, וְכָמֹהוּ֩ לֹֽא הָיָ֨ה לְפָנָ֜יו מֶ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֤ב אֶל יְהוָה֙, and 23:26 replies with the adversative and the same root negated, אַ֣ךְ לֹֽא שָׁ֣ב יְהוָ֗ה, an antithesis on one shared verb that binds the wrath notice to the verse directly preceding it. Neither 23:25 nor 23:27 is mentioned anywhere in the rationale, although both lie inside the span.
challenges.suggested_action: Cite the 23:25/23:26 verbal antithesis as the Hebrew warrant for keeping the wrath notice with the reform summary, then revisit whether 'low' remains the right confidence once that evidence is on the record.

challenges.claim: The reason offered for the imperfect echo, that 23:24 "introduces an object list ... rather than a place," is not what the clause shows. 23:24 reproduces the frame of 23:19 completely: fronted objects, then a locative relative אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִרְאוּ֙ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם, then a delayed qatal with explicit subject בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ, answering 23:19's הֵסִ֖יר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ. What differs between them is territorial scope, not construction.
challenges.suggested_action: Rest the distinction on domain, that no new territory is opened, instead of asserting a structural difference the clause does not exhibit.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row's low-confidence flag matches book_strategy_draft.md's pre-registered expected_low_confidence_regions item 7, '23:24-27 residual-reforms + wrath notice (attachment direction arguable),' in substance. The וְגַ֣ם אֶת at 23:24 is verified to introduce an object list rather than a place, correctly distinguished from the register's location-shift use of the same particle, and the adversative אַ֣ךְ לֹֽא שָׁ֣ב יְהוָ֗ה מֵחֲר֤וֹן אַפּוֹ֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל at 23:26 matches the source exactly.

Both ordered repairs are present and verifiable. The verbal antithesis now carries the wrath notice - 23:25's אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֤ב אֶל יְהוָה֙ answered across the seam by 23:26's אַ֣ךְ לֹֽא שָׁ֣ב יְהוָ֗ה - and the 23:24 comparison rests on territorial scope instead of a structural difference the clause does not exhibit. I tested the mark claim rather than taking it: the single-witness apparatus keys no mark anywhere between 23:24 and 23:27, the nearest being 22:2 and 23:30, so 'no parashah mark falls in this stretch' is true and nothing here is mark-driven. The repair did introduce one quote-boundary slip, where the string labelled a locative relative runs two words past the relative into the main clause.

challenges.claim: The string quoted as 'a locative relative', אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִרְאוּ֙ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ, over-runs the relative clause: בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ is the main-clause qatal with its explicit subject, and it is precisely the element the sentence then matches against 23:19's הֵסִ֖יר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ. The relative itself also differs in kind from the two it is said to reuse: 23:24's is a finite niphal clause, whereas 23:15 has אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל and 23:19 has אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן, both verbless prepositional relatives.
challenges.suggested_action: End the quoted relative at the second place-name and cite the delayed qatal separately under its own label; if the full frame-identity claim is kept, disclose that 23:24's relative is verbal where 23:15's and 23:19's are prepositional. No span change.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both OL challenges are cured: the row now cites the 23:25/23:26 shuv/shuv antithesis as the tier-1 tie holding the wrath notice to the reform summary, and it rests the 23:24-vs-23:19 distinction on territorial scope rather than the disproven claim of a structural difference. The 'no parashah mark falls in this stretch' claim and the low confidence both check out against pmarks_2Kgs.json. One residual gap survives the repair: 23:15 is invoked in prose as the shared-construction comparandum for 23:19/23:24 but is never added to boundary_evidence_refs, which lists only 23:19 among the comparanda.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale relies on 23:15 as the comparandum sharing 23:19's gam-plus-fronted-object-plus-locative-relative construction, but boundary_evidence_refs cites only 23:19 and 23:24-28 -- oshb/web:2Kgs.23.15 is never listed.
challenges.suggested_action: Add oshb:2Kgs.23.15 and web:2Kgs.23.15 to boundary_evidence_refs so the citation set matches the comparison the prose actually makes.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both OL points hold once 23:25 and 23:27 are actually read alongside 23:24 and 23:26, which the row's own rationale never does. 23:25's וְכָמֹהוּ֩ לֹֽא הָיָ֨ה לְפָנָ֜יו מֶ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֤ב אֶל יְהוָה֙ and 23:26's אַ֣ךְ לֹֽא שָׁ֣ב יְהוָ֗ה share the same verb, שָׁ֤ב / שָׁ֣ב, in flat antithesis, a real Hebrew tie between the wrath notice and the verse just before it that the disclosed 'nothing tier-1 settles which' statement overlooks. And 23:24 turns out to reuse 23:19's exact shape, fronted objects plus a locative relative (אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִרְאוּ֙ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם) plus a delayed verb-and-subject (בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ answering 23:19's הֵסִ֖יר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ), so what differs from the register's other movements is territorial scope, not construction, as the row's phrasing implies. Neither point relocates an edge; if anything the שָׁ֤ב/שָׁ֣ב antithesis argues for keeping the wrath notice with 23:24-25 rather than detaching it toward 23:28, so I see no matching warrant here to declare a confidence change the way I do for 087, especially since LF's independent pass over this same row raised nothing.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every quoted string checks out, including the elided source-citation formula, whose second half I traced through eleven verses of the book (14:15, 14:18, 14:28, 15:6, 15:36, 16:19, 20:20, 21:17, 21:25, 23:28, 24:5); all three reigns of this part do close with it, though 21:25 lacks the וְכָל element present in the quoted form. The petuchah citation is right in type, verse and disclosure, and is handled as a faint nod rather than a driver. The disclosed tension, however, rests on a template claim I could not confirm and in fact falsified: the enthronement clause at the end of 23:30 patterns with reign closes, not with the accession formula that opens Judahite frames.

challenges.claim: "23:30b's enthronement clause reads exactly like the reign-opening verses that begin every other frame in this part" is contradicted by the book's own templates. My grep for the verse-initial accession pattern returns 8:17, 8:26, 14:2, 15:2, 15:33, 16:2, 18:2, 21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8 and 24:18, i.e. every Judahite frame-opening, and the three in this part all read that way (בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ; בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ). 23:30 instead runs וַיִּמְשְׁח֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו, and a de-pointed grep for that closing collocation returns only 14:21 and 23:30 in the whole book; its closest sibling, וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, stands inside Amon's closing material ahead of the source citation at 21:25, just as 14:21 follows Amaziah's close. The people-of-the-land enthronement clause is therefore a predecessor-close element, so the literary-versus-administrative tension the row discloses does not arise.
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the formula claim, reframe or drop the disclosed seam tension, and reconsider raising the medium confidence now that 23:30b is shown to follow the closing pattern rather than the accession template.

primary_reviews.rationale: The source-citation opener at 23:28 (וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים) and the closing anointing notice at 23:30 (וַיִּקַּ֣ח עַם הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת יְהֽוֹאָחָז֙...וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו) both match the witness exactly, and the row candidly discloses that 23:30b's enthronement clause resembles a regnal opening. challenges.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative asserts that treating 23:30b as the true opening of Jehoahaz's reign is 'arguably the stronger literary reading given this book's own formula pattern,' but this claim was not checked against the book's own pattern before being written. Two other reign transitions (21:23-24 Amon-to-Josiah: וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו; and 14:19-21/15:1-2 Amaziah-to-Azariah: וַיַּמְלִ֣כוּ אֹת֔וֹ תַּ֖חַת אָבִ֥יו) show the 'people of the land ... made X king in his father's place' clause consistently belongs to the OUTGOING king's closing sequence, distinct from and prior to the incoming king's own age+years+mother's-name template. book_strategy_draft.md's own decision matrix also lists 23:28 under 'Regnal closing / source-citation formula,' corroborating that 23:28-30 is one closing unit. The row's downgrade to 'medium' confidence and its framing of an unresolved 'tension' is therefore more hedged than the evidence supports.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This is the priority calibration item, and both challenges survive rigorous independent testing. I built my own consonantal search of the whole book (stripping niqqud/cantillation) for the verse-initial accession template (age-at-accession + royal name + 'when he began to reign') and got exactly fourteen hits: 8:17, 8:26, 14:2, 15:2, 15:33, 16:2, 18:2, 21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18, matching OL's list precisely; 23:30b matches none of that pattern. I then searched for the closing collocation תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו ('in place of his father') and it occurs exactly twice book-wide, 14:21 and 23:30, both embedded in the outgoing king's own death-and-burial sequence rather than the incoming king's template: at 14:18-21 the source citation for Amaziah (14:18) precedes his death (14:19-20) and Azariah's enthronement (14:21), with Azariah's own fresh template only opening at 15:1-2; at 21:23-25 Amon's death (21:23) and Josiah's structurally identical enthronement, וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (21:24), both precede Amon's own source-citation close (21:25), with Josiah's fresh template opening only at 22:1. Both parallels confirm the enthronement clause is consistently predecessor-close material, never a reign-opener, exactly as OL argues and as LF found by checking the same two transitions independently, a genuine convergent finding reached by different methods. book_strategy_draft.md's own decision matrix independently corroborates this, listing 23:28's formula type as one that 'closes (never opens) its unit,' and its expected_low_confidence_regions list flags 23:24-27 (item 7) but not 23:28-30, meaning this span was never pre-registered as a soft spot the way 086 was. On the evidence, the row's disclosed 'tension' between a literary seam and the administrative part-boundary does not arise: the correct literary reading agrees with the fixed part-boundary rather than fighting it, so the strongest_rejected_alternative was never actually the stronger reading. Confidence should rise from medium to high; the boundary itself is not harmed; it is strengthened, since the two edges the row worried might conflict turn out to align.

primary_reviews.rationale: Every one of the nine quotations in this row reproduces the consonants, vowels and accents of the source without deviation, and the accession opener בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ is genuinely verse-initial, as is the installation clause at 24:17 with its disclosed pe. The trouble is the rejected alternative, which turns on the assertion that the counting clauses stay verb-initial and 'never' adopt fronted-object catalogue syntax: 24:16 begins וְאֵת֩ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל שִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֗ים and holds its verb back to וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם, while 24:15 fronts וְאֵת֙ … אֵילֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ before הוֹלִ֛יךְ. Two smaller matters also stand out: the fulfillment tag that ends 24:13 is passed over in silence, and two OSHB ketiv/qere doublets are transcribed as if they were running phrases.

challenges.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative claims the deportation counts 'remain verb-initial continuations of the surrender scene, never shifting into the fronted-object catalogue syntax'. The text refutes this at two points inside the span: 24:16 opens the verse with an accusative-marked object phrase, וְאֵת֩ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל שִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֗ים, and only reaches its verb at וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם; 24:15 likewise fronts וְאֵת֙ … אֵילֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ ahead of הוֹלִ֛יךְ. This is the identical construction that decisions M8-2Kgs-093 and M8-2Kgs-094 treat as the defining mark of a register at 25:13-15, so the criterion used to reject the register reading here does not in fact separate the two.
challenges.suggested_action: Rewrite the rejection so it does not rest on a syntactic contrast the verses contradict: reject the register carve-out on continuity of agent and scene (the king of Babylon as acting subject through 24:13-17) and state plainly that verse-initial accusative fronting occurs inside this narrative too.

challenges.claim: The span swallows a device the campaign's own matrix classifies as unit-closing without discussing it: 24:13 ends כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה, and the matrix row 'Fulfillment notice' lists 24:13 with the effect 'Closes its unit'. The row's confidence is 'high' yet no sentence tests a 24:13/24:14 seam. A book-wide grep also shows the refrain varies rather than recurring in one form: גְּדוּדֵ֣י בְנֵֽי appears at 1:17, 4:44, 7:16, 9:26, 10:17, 14:25, 23:16 and 24:2 (eight verses), whereas כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה occurs at 24:13 alone.
challenges.suggested_action: Add an explicit test and rejection of the 24:13/24:14 seam, and label the 24:13 tag as a form variant of the fulfillment device rather than letting the matrix entry stand unexamined; if the seam cannot be rejected on tier-1 grounds, lower confidence from 'high'.

challenges.claim: Two quotations silently carry OSHB ketiv/qere doublets as though they were continuous text: 'עלה עָל֗וּ' at 24:10 (unpointed ketiv followed by pointed qere) and 'עשרה עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת' at 24:14. Both are byte-faithful to the substrate, but as printed they read as doubled words, and the 24:10 case is embedded in a phrase the row labels a formulaic 'siege pair', which invites exactly that misreading downstream. The same substrate feature sits unremarked at 24:15 (אולי אֵילֵ֣י) and at 24:18.
challenges.suggested_action: Mark ketiv/qere doublets when quoting — e.g. quote the qere and note in brackets that the substrate line carries an unpointed ketiv before it — so a reader does not parse the ketiv as part of the formula.

primary_reviews.rationale: The accession-formula bracketing (24:8 opening this reign, 24:18 opening the next) holds, and the installation-vs-own-accession double frame at 24:17/24:18 correctly parallels the 23:34/23:36 pattern used earlier in the book. But the rejected-alternative’s claim that the deportation-count clauses ‘remain verb-initial continuations’ is only true for 24:14 (וְהִגְלָ֣ה..., genuinely verb-first); 24:16 opens with the fronted object וְאֵת֩ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל..., deferring its verb וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם to the clause’s end -- the same fronting shape later used to typify the register at 25:13.

challenges.claim: 24:16 (וְאֵת֩ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל ... וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם) opens with a fronted direct object, not a verb -- the rejected-alternative’s claim that ‘these counting clauses remain verb-initial continuations ... never shifting into the fronted-object catalogue syntax’ is false for this verse, though it is true of 24:14 (וְהִגְלָ֣ה...).
challenges.suggested_action: Narrow the rejected-alternative’s claim to 24:14 alone, or reframe the actual distinguishing test as single-constituent preposing within an ongoing narrative clause (24:14-16) versus a serial multi-item object-marker (et) chain accumulating before any verb appears (25:13-14), rather than a blanket verb-initial/object-fronted binary.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the most complete repair in the cluster. The 24:13/24:14 seam is met head-on instead of swallowed, confidence has come down to medium accordingly, the word-order claim is narrowed to what 24:14 and 24:16 actually show, and all four ketiv/qere hazards are handled - 24:10 and 24:14 annotated, 24:15's and 24:18's doublets left outside the quotations, which my collation confirms. I probed the narrowing rather than accepting it: 24:15 does front an object in its second clause much as 24:16 does, but the row quotes only its verse-opening וַיֶּ֥גֶל, so the sentence stays true as written. The new agent-continuity criterion is drawn two verses too wide at its left edge.

challenges.claim: The rebuilt rejection rests on 'the king of Babylon acting throughout 24:8-17 in some form', but no Babylonian agent is present in 24:8-9, which are Jehoiachin's accession template and his evaluation formula, וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה; the first Babylonian action is the siege notice at 24:10. The 24:13/24:14 test needs continuity only from 24:10 onward, so the wider span adds exposure without adding force.
challenges.suggested_action: Narrow the continuity claim to 24:10-17, or to 'from the siege notice on', and describe 24:8-9 as the frame's own opening template. No span change.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the deepest repair in the cluster and it holds up: LF-090-1/OL-090-1 are cured by conceding 24:16 genuinely fronts its object (only 24:14 and 24:15 remain verb-initial, confirmed by direct inspection) and rebuilding the register-rejection on continuity of the king-of-Babylon's agency rather than a false uniform word-order claim; OL-090-2 is cured by directly naming and rejecting the 24:13/24:14 seam, with confidence correctly dropped from high to medium; OL-090-3 is cured by annotating both quoted ketiv/qere pairs (24:10 עלה/עָל֗וּ, 24:14 עשרה/עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת). All citations, the pe mark at 24:17, and both edges (24:8 opening, 24:18 closing) check out. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: The accession brackets at 24:8 and 24:18 hold, and the 24:17/24:18 double-frame parallel with 23:34/23:36 is genuine. Checking every clause first-word from 24:14 through 24:16 against oshb confirms both primaries: 24:14 (וְהִגְלָ֣ה אֶת כָּל) and 24:15 (וַיֶּ֥גֶל אֶת יְהוֹיָכִ֖ין) are truly verb-first, but 24:16 (וְאֵת֩ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל ... וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם) defers its verb to the clause's end, falsifying the rejected-alternative's claim that these counts 'never' shift into fronted-object catalogue syntax. OL's further catch -- that the device matrix lists 24:13's כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה as a fulfillment-notice closer, unaddressed at 'high' confidence -- checks out on my own grep: that exact wording is a hapax in the book, against the more common כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה variant found at eight other verses (1:17, 4:44, 7:16, 9:26, 10:17, 14:25, 23:16, 24:2), so 24:13 really is an unexamined formula instance. Testing the 24:13/24:14 seam myself, it fails to justify a split: no date, accession, or newly named agent opens 24:14, and the deportation figures continue under the same king of Babylon, consistent with the strategy's own note that '24:14-16 deportation counts' belong 'inside the Jehoiachin unit.' OL's ketiv/qere point is likewise confirmed directly against the substrate (עלה עָל֗וּ at 24:10, עשרה עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת at 24:14, the same feature unremarked at 24:15's אולי אֵילֵ֣י and 24:18's חמיטל חֲמוּטַ֥ל). Boundary: NOT harmed. Needs prose repair on the syntax claim and an explicit 24:13/24:14 rejection sentence, plus a confidence step-down from high to medium given the gap was asserted rather than tested.

Testing the row's date-formula universal against every date in the fall sequence (25:1, 25:3, 25:8, 25:25, 25:27) turns up a consistent pattern -- full year+month+day (or exile-year+month+day) triads open units, month-only or day-only partials stay internal -- which this row correctly anticipates and which 092 and 096 must apply consistently as well. The samekh keyed to 24:20 matches pmarks_2Kgs.json exactly and is properly logged as non-driving. Neither primary raised a challenge here, and my own re-derivation surfaces none. Boundary: not harmed; confidence (medium) is appropriately hedged as written.

primary_reviews.rationale: The two date expressions behave exactly as this row describes them. 25:1 heads its verse with a complete year-month-day formula, וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮, whereas 25:3 offers only a day count, בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ, which cannot compete as a unit head; the breach clause וַתִּבָּקַ֣ע הָעִ֗יר is verse-initial wayyiqtol as claimed. The contrast drawn against 25:8 holds by content and not merely by assertion: 25:1 counts לְמָלְכ֗וֹ of Zedekiah's reign while 25:8 counts נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל, and the agent changes to רַב. The samekh keyed to 25:7 matches the mark file, sits at the span's outer edge, and is expressly rated weak. Worth recording for adjacent rows: 25:7 itself opens with fronted objects, וְאֶת בְּנֵי֙ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ שָׁחֲט֖וּ, which bears on how much weight object-fronting can carry as a register signal later in this chapter.

The full date formula opening 25:1 and the fresh full date plus new named agent (Nebuzaradan) at 25:8 correctly bracket this span; the internal partial date at 25:3 (day only, no year restated) is rightly treated as sub-articulation of the same siege rather than a competing opener, and the samekh after 25:7 is correctly logged as weak, non-driving corroboration consistent with the m8-mesh-r2 rule.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Confirmed directly: the full triad opening 25:1 (בִשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֒) genuinely outranks the partial day-only date at 25:3 (בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ), which rightly stays internal to the siege narrative rather than opening a rival unit, and the fresh full triad plus the new agent Nebuzaradan at 25:8 is what actually closes this span. The samekh after 25:7 checks against pmarks_2Kgs.json and is correctly treated as weak, non-driving corroboration rather than a boundary driver. No challenges from either primary, and none surface on my own pass through the verses. Boundary: not harmed; the high confidence is earned on tier-1 grounds alone.

sol_resolution.author_instance: book_author_respondents_2kgs (six parts, list schema, normalized by orchestrator; micro-r2 remedies folded in)

boss_ruling.reasoning: No challenges; row accepted as frozen.

post_resolution_check.notes: Sliced the 25:1 and 25:3 date formulas and the samekh at 25:7 against OSHB; confirmed 25:3 carries only a bare day-of-month with no year or reign anchor, supporting this row's claim that it stays internal to the siege narrative rather than opening a rival unit.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation clears every quotation in this row, and the date head at 25:8 is genuine, but the syntactic labelling collapses under inspection. Of the four clauses listed as proceeding 'in verb-initial clauses', only 25:9 is verb-initial (וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף): 25:10 opens וְאֶת חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב and defers נָֽתְצוּ֙; 25:11 opens וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר and defers הֶגְלָ֕ה; 25:12 fronts וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ before הִשְׁאִ֖יר. That matters because the closing edge is set on the premise that fronted-object topicalization is 'absent from the burn-and-wall report just concluded' — a premise the report itself falsifies in three of its four verses, including two the row quotes as specimens of verb-initial narrative.

challenges.claim: The row asserts the unit 'proceeds in verb-initial clauses' and then sets its closing edge on the claim that the object-fronting of 25:13 is 'a topicalized listing pattern absent from the burn-and-wall report just concluded'. Both statements fail against the consonantal text. 25:10 begins וְאֶת חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב with the verb נָֽתְצוּ֙ held back; 25:11 begins וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר with הֶגְלָ֕ה held back; 25:12 begins וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ before הִשְׁאִ֖יר. Verse-initial וְאֶת occurs in 15 verses across 2Kgs on a book-wide grep of the substrate (9:10, 14:6, 14:13, 16:14, 16:18, 17:37, 23:12, 23:13, 24:16, 25:7, 25:10, 25:11, 25:13, 25:14, 25:15), most of them in plain narrative, so it is not a register-diagnostic construction. The WEB obscures this by supplying English subject-first order at 25:10-11.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop the verb-initial characterization and rebuild the 25:12/25:13 edge on something the Hebrew supports — the shift from a named agent performing finite actions (Nebuzaradan burning, demolishing, deporting, leaving) to an inventory of temple objects with an indefinite plural subject (בְּבֵית) and no continuing agent — or, if that will not carry, merge 25:8-17 as the strategy permits and disclose the reduced confidence.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening at 25:8 (full date plus the new agent Nebuzaradan) is sound, but the claim that the intervening verses ‘proceed in verb-initial clauses’ does not hold against the row’s own evidence: 25:10 (וְאֶת חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם ... נָֽתְצוּ֙) and 25:11 (וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם ... הֶגְלָ֕ה) both front a direct object before their verb, and 25:12 (וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ הִשְׁאִ֖יר) fronts a prepositional phrase before its verb -- only 25:9 (וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף) is genuinely verb-initial. The ‘syntactic shift ... absent from the burn-and-wall report’ claim used to justify the 25:12/25:13 edge is therefore inaccurate for three of its four supporting examples.

challenges.claim: The rationale states the unit ‘proceeds in verb-initial clauses’ through 25:9-12 and that the fronted-object pattern is ‘absent from the burn-and-wall report just concluded,’ but 25:10 (וְאֶת חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם...), 25:11 (וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם...), and 25:12 (וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ...) -- three of the four clauses offered as evidence -- all front a non-verb constituent (direct object or prepositional phrase) before their finite verb, the same word-order feature the writer treats as the exclusive, unit-defining hallmark of the register beginning at 25:13. Only 25:9 (וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף) is actually verb-initial.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the verb-initial/object-fronted binary with the feature that actually distinguishes 25:8-12 from 25:13-17: a single fronted constituent inside an ongoing finite-verb narrative clause (25:9-12) versus a serial chain of multiple object-marker-led (et) items accumulating before any verb appears at all (25:13-14). Decision 094’s register-rule argument already supplies an independent, sounder basis for the same boundary and does not depend on this claim.

primary_reviews.rationale: The falsified criterion really is gone: the row states outright that only 25:9 is verb-initial and that the 25:12/25:13 edge cannot rest on a word-order contrast, and it quotes the three fronted clauses accurately. The replacement, though, fails the same class of test on the same verses. 25:10's finite verb takes the Chaldean army as its subject, נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר רַב טַבָּחִֽים, so Nebuzaradan is not the subject of every finite verb in 25:8-12; and 25:13, said to open an inventory with no personal agent at all, names its own agent twice in שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה, with the captain's title resuming as subject two verses later at לָקַ֖ח רַב טַבָּחִֽים. WEB reads both verses the same way, so this is not an artifact of the pointing.

challenges.claim: The agent-continuity criterion that replaced the withdrawn verb-initial test is itself contradicted at both ends of the edge it is asked to carry. '25:8-12 keeps Nebuzaradan, or his title, as the continuing subject of every finite verb' fails at 25:10, whose subject is the Chaldean army: נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר רַב טַבָּחִֽים (WEB 25:10 likewise makes the army of the Chaldeans the one who broke down the walls). '25:13 onward opens an inventory with no continuing personal agent at all' fails at 25:13 itself, שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה, and again at 25:15, לָקַ֖ח רַב טַבָּחִֽים, where the very title this row treats as Nebuzaradan's agency marker at 25:11-12 is the subject inside the register. The Chaldeans-and-captain agent set therefore straddles the 25:12/25:13 edge rather than marking it.
challenges.suggested_action: Rebuild the edge on what actually changes across it - finite actions against the city and its population giving way to an enumerated inventory of temple furnishings - and address 25:10, 25:13 and 25:15 by name. If any agent criterion is retained, restrict it to the role the named human agent plays rather than to 'every finite verb', and disclose the reduced strength; the merged 25:8-17 reading the strategy permits is the alternative if it will not carry.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both LF-093-1 and OL-093-1 are cured: the false claim that the unit 'proceeds in verb-initial clauses' is gone, replaced by an accurate accounting (only 25:9 is verb-initial; 25:10-12 each front an object or prepositional phrase, confirmed by direct inspection against oshb), and the 25:12/25:13 edge is now argued on Nebuzaradan's continuing agency versus the agentless register beginning at 25:13 rather than on the disproven word-order contrast. boundary_evidence_refs and both edges (25:8 date-formula opening, 25:13 register hand-off) are fully covered. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: This is the cluster's cleanest convergent catch. Walking every clause-initial word from 25:9 through 25:12 against oshb: only 25:9 (וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה) is genuinely verb-first; 25:10 (וְאֶת חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙) fronts an object before its verb, 25:11 (וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר ... הֶגְלָ֕ה) does the same, and 25:12 (וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ הִשְׁאִ֖יר) fronts a genitive-headed phrase before its verb. That means the rationale's premise -- that fronted-object topicalization is 'absent from the burn-and-wall report just concluded' -- is false in three of its own four supporting citations, exactly as both LF and OL independently demonstrate from different angles (LF via a chain-versus-single-constituent test, OL via the same clause-by-clause parse). The 25:12/25:13 edge nonetheless survives on the separate, sounder ground both reviewers point to: 25:8-12 keeps a single continuing named agent (Nebuzaradan and his forces performing burn/break/deport/leave in sequence) while 25:13-17 shifts to an inventory register with no continuing personal agent, the content-based distinction decision 094 already supplies. Boundary: NOT harmed, but the syntactic argument must be deleted rather than patched -- the edge should be re-grounded entirely in agent-continuity and register content, not word order.
