post_resolution_check.notes: Verified the three cross-edge citations this row's persons-to-objects argument names -- 25:10, 25:13, and 25:15 -- each against its claimed OSHB verse, and all three matched exactly. The 25:16-17 measurement-clause quotes used for contrast are likewise accurate, though those verses are not added to this row's own evidence_refs since they fall in the following row's span.

primary_reviews.rationale: The five citations survive character comparison intact, and it is true that 25:13 heads its verse with an accusative-marked object, וְאֶת עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת, reaching its verb only at בְּבֵית. Two problems attach to the reasoning built on that. First, the closing universal — that nothing else in the book folds a register into surrounding narrative once object-fronting starts — does not survive a book-wide grep, since the construction opens fifteen verses across 2Kgs and is used inside undisputed narrative at 24:16, 25:7, 25:10 and 25:11. Second, 25:16 and 25:17 are not that construction at all: הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם and שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת הָעַמּ֣וּד are verbless clauses with fronted subjects, a summary-and-measurement idiom rather than accusative topicalization. The return to wayyiqtol at וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים is reported accurately, and the 1Kgs 7 parallel is properly quarantined as cross-book metadata.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative closes on a book-wide universal — 'nothing else in the book folds a register into its surrounding narrative once the fronted-object pattern starts' — that my own grep of the substrate contradicts. Verse-initial וְאֶת occurs in 15 verses of 2Kgs: nine outside the final chapter (9:10; 14:6; 14:13; 16:14; 16:18; 17:37; 23:12; 23:13; 24:16) and six within it (25:7; 25:10; 25:11; 25:13; 25:14; 25:15). Three falsify the claim inside this very cluster: 24:16 (וְאֵת֩ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַחַ֜יִל שִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֗ים … וַיְבִיאֵ֧ם) is an enumerated deportation register that decision M8-2Kgs-090 deliberately keeps inside its narrative unit, and 25:10-11 carry the same fronting inside the destruction report of M8-2Kgs-093.
challenges.suggested_action: Delete the universal or restate it as a bounded observation about 25:13-17, and support the register boundary on features that actually distinguish it — loss of a continuing named agent, enumerated temple furnishings, and the weight and dimension idiom of 25:16-17 — rather than on object-fronting alone.

challenges.claim: The row says 'the same topicalized pattern runs through' 25:14 'into the summary-and-dimension notice of 25:16-17'. Grammatically these differ: 25:14 continues the accusative chain (וְאֶת הַסִּירֹ֨ת וְאֶת הַיָּעִ֜ים), whereas 25:16 opens with a fronted subject in a verbless clause, הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם, and 25:17 with a measurement predicate, שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת הָעַמּ֣וּד; neither carries the object marker at all.
challenges.suggested_action: Distinguish the two: describe 25:13-15 as accusative-fronted enumeration and 25:16-17 as verbless summary and measurement clauses, then argue both belong to one register on content grounds instead of asserting a single syntactic pattern.

primary_reviews.rationale: The register’s opening at 25:13 (object-fronted) and its continuation through the serial object-marker (et) chain of 25:14 are accurately described, and the pivot back to verb-initial narrative at 25:18 correctly closes the register at the far edge; the cross-book echo to the 1Kgs 7 furnishings catalogue is properly disclosed as metadata rather than in-book evidence, consistent with the m8-mesh-r2 rule on cross-book parallels.

The book-wide universal has been replaced by a bounded count I can reproduce exactly: verse-initial waw-plus-et stands in fifteen verses (9:10, 14:6, 14:13, 16:14, 16:18, 17:37, 23:12, 23:13, 24:16, 25:7, 25:10, 25:11, 25:13, 25:14, 25:15), and the second cure lands too, with 25:13-15's accusative enumeration now distinguished from the measurement clauses of 25:16-17 and the 1Kgs 7 parallel fenced as cross-book metadata that never touches the seam. The load-bearing replacement is what fails: 'the absence of any continuing named human agent' is falsified inside the span by 25:15's לָקַ֖ח רַב טַבָּחִֽים and by 25:13's שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה. The row's quotations step 25:13, 25:14, 25:16, 25:17, 25:18 and its refs list no 25:15, so the one verse that breaks the rule is the one verse of the span left unconsulted.

challenges.claim: 'the absence of any continuing named human agent' and '25:13-17's loss of any continuing personal agent' are both falsified inside the register. 25:15's finite verb takes the captain's title as its subject, לָקַ֖ח רַב טַבָּחִֽים - the same title that carries the agency at 25:11-12, which this cluster treats there as a named agent - and 25:13 names the Chaldeans as subject of two finite verbs, שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה. Consequently 'the register yields at 25:18 to renewed verb-initial narrative', quoting וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים, presupposes a lapse in agency that 25:15 does not permit; the row's evidence_refs omit 25:15 altogether.
challenges.suggested_action: Add 25:15 to the evidence set and re-ground the register on the enumerated temple furnishings, the measurement idiom of 25:16-17, and the shift from persons to objects, rather than on an absent agent the span in fact supplies. The 25:12/25:13 edge in row M8-2Kgs-093 leans on the same claim and needs the same rebuild.

challenges.claim: 25:16 is characterised as a 'verbless subject-fronted' clause, but the quotation stops immediately before the verse's finite predicate, לֹא הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל לִנְחֹ֖שֶׁת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה; the fronted list beginning הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם is a dislocated topic resumed by that clause, not a verbless clause. The companion observation that 25:16-17 carry no accusative marker is correct and unaffected.
challenges.suggested_action: Describe 25:16 as a fronted nominal list resumed by its own negated predicate, and reserve 'verbless' for 25:17's measurement predicate. No span change.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both OL-094-1 and OL-094-2 are cured: the false book-wide universal is withdrawn and replaced with an independently-verified count (verse-initial vav-et occurs at exactly fifteen verses book-wide, including the counter-examples at 24:16/25:7/25:10/25:11 that the row now names itself), and 25:13-15's accusative-fronted enumeration is now distinguished from 25:16-17's verbless summary-and-measurement clauses instead of being folded into one asserted pattern. The register boundary is correctly re-grounded in loss of a continuing named agent rather than syntax alone. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: I ran my own book-wide search for verse-initial waw+et (accusative-marked fronting) across the whole book rather than trusting OL's count, and it returns exactly fifteen verses -- 9:10, 14:6, 14:13, 16:14, 16:18, 17:37, 23:12, 23:13, 24:16 outside this register, plus 25:7, 25:10, 25:11, 25:13, 25:14, 25:15 inside it -- which independently confirms OL's claim and refutes the rejected-alternative's universal that 'nothing else in the book folds a register into surrounding narrative once the fronted-object pattern starts.' The construction is a book-wide, register-neutral feature, not a diagnostic marker, and three of its instances (24:16, 25:10, 25:11) sit inside narrative this cluster's own rows 090 and 093 keep un-registered. Separately, 25:16 (הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם הַיָּ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙) and 25:17 (שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת הָעַמּ֣וּד הָאֶחָ֗ד) carry no object marker at all and are verbless subject-fronted or measurement clauses, a genuinely different construction from the accusative chain of 25:13-14, confirming OL's second point too. Neither defect touches the 25:13/25:18 edges themselves, which rest on the return to wayyiqtol narrative with a named human object at 25:18. Boundary: NOT harmed; the universal must be deleted or narrowed to this span alone, and 25:16-17 should be described as a verbless summary-and-measurement idiom rather than a continuation of the same accusative pattern.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale asserts "No internal tier-1 contrast divides these four verses" without engaging the syntactic gradation actually present inside the span: the wayhi-plus-date frame with its qatal main verb נָשָׂ֡א carried on by wayyiqtol in 25:28 (וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר ... וַיִּתֵּן֙), then consecutive perfects with habitual force in 25:29 (וְשִׁנָּ֕א אֵ֖ת בִּגְדֵ֣י כִלְא֑וֹ ... וְאָכַ֨ל), and a fronted-subject summary clause in 25:30 (וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַ֨ת תָּמִ֧יד נִתְּנָה לּ֛וֹ). The last is precisely the disjunctive waw-x pattern the book strategy elsewhere treats as a tier-1 articulation signal (narrator aside / annal member), so the negative is asserted rather than argued. The cohesion evidence that answers it sits inside the row's own quotations but is never deployed for this purpose: תָּמִ֛יד (25:29) repeated as תָּמִ֧יד (25:30), and the closing inclusio כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו (25:29) / כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו (25:30).
challenges.suggested_action: Add one clause identifying the 25:30 fronted-subject clause וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַ֨ת תָּמִ֧יד נִתְּנָה לּ֛וֹ as annalistic summary articulation and rejecting a 25:29/25:30 split on the תָּמִ֛יד / תָּמִ֧יד and כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו / כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו repetition, so the "no internal seam" finding is evidenced rather than assumed. No span change.

primary_reviews.rationale: The opening edge carries a genuine tier-1 date formula, וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה ... בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מָלְכ֗וֹ (oshb:2Kgs.25.27, single-witness pointing), matching the same date+new-agent pattern that opens the other members of the ch.25 fall sequence at 25:1, 25:8, and 25:25 (all independently re-checked against 2Kgs_oshb.txt), so the rival reading (attaching 25:27-30 to the Gedaliah unit as a coda) is a real, not straw-man, alternative that the draft correctly rejects on the same scene/agent-shift grounds used throughout that sequence. Internally, 25:28-30 form one uninterrupted narrative chain with no date, commission, or scene-change marker breaking it, and it closes on the book's literal final verse (2Kgs.25.30, last line of 2Kgs_oshb.txt), so the far edge needs no argument beyond the corpus boundary; the Jer 52:31-34 note is correctly held as non-authorizing cross-book metadata rather than in-book evidence.

The universal is properly narrowed and its counter-case named rather than hidden: 25:25's וַיְהִ֣י בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י shows the wayhi-plus-date form is not self-authorizing, and the weight shifts onto אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩, whose two elements my own consonantal grep finds only at 25:27, together with the move to Babylon and the head-lifting idiom. The second cure is equally solid - 25:30's fronted-subject niphal is named instead of passed over, and the split is refused on repetitions I verified letter for letter, תָּמִ֛יד at 25:29 against תָּמִ֧יד at 25:30, and full כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו against defective כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו. The one thing I would change is the term chosen for that tie.

challenges.claim: The 25:29/25:30 repetition is called 'a lexical bracket', but תָּמִ֛יד / תָּמִ֧יד and כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו / כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו stand in two consecutive verses with nothing enclosed between them, so nothing is in fact bracketed. This same cluster has just withdrawn 'inclusio' at M8-2Kgs-095 for precisely the missing-paired-opening reason, and the same standard should govern here.
challenges.suggested_action: Call it a catchword repetition or a closing tie binding 25:30 to 25:29; the cohesion argument that defeats a 25:29/25:30 split works unchanged without the bracket term. No span change.

primary_reviews.rationale: OL-097-1 is cured: the 'every other unit' universal is narrowed to the features that actually discriminate a seam -- the once-only name אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ (independently confirmed by consonantal grep to occur nowhere else in the book), the relocation to Babylon, and the release idiom -- with 25:25's internal wyhy-plus-date use now named as the counter-case that falsifies the old universal. OL-097-2 is cured: the bare 'no internal tier-1 contrast' assertion is replaced by an explicit argument from the תָּמִ֛יד (25:29) / תָּמִ֧יד (25:30) repetition and the defective/full כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו (25:30) / כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו (25:29) lexical bracket binding 25:30 to 25:29. All grammatical labels (niphal-passive נִתְּנָה, wayyiqtol at 25:28, weqatal at 25:29) check out. No new defects found.
